name: Stuffed grape leaves with lamb and rice
description:
A classic Mediterranean delight, these tender grape leaves are meticulously rolled around a savory filling of seasoned ground lamb and fluffy rice, often simmered in a tangy lemon broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients:
- 50 fresh or jarred grape leaves
- 1 lb ground lamb
- 1 cup short-grain rice, rinsed
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh mint, chopped
- 1/4 cup olive oil, plus more for cooking
- Juice of 2 lemons
- 2 cups water or chicken broth
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. If using fresh grape leaves, blanch them in boiling water for 2-3 minutes until pliable. If using jarred, rinse thoroughly.
2. In a large bowl, combine ground lamb, rinsed rice, chopped onion, parsley, mint, 1/4 cup olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
3. Lay a grape leaf flat, shiny side down. Place a small spoonful of filling near the stem end. Fold the bottom edge over the filling, then fold in the sides, and roll tightly upwards.
4. Arrange the rolled grape leaves snugly in a large pot or Dutch oven. Drizzle with remaining olive oil and lemon juice. Pour in water or broth until the leaves are just covered.
5. Place a heatproof plate on top of the leaves to keep them submerged. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until rice is cooked and lamb is tender. Serve warm.

name: Stew, lamb
description:
A hearty and comforting dish, lamb stew features tender chunks of lamb slow-cooked with an array of vegetables in a rich, savory broth, perfect for a chilly evening.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs lamb stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, peeled and sliced
- 2 celery stalks, sliced
- 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 4 cups beef broth
- 1/2 cup dry red wine (optional)
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Pat lamb dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Brown lamb in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
3. Gradually whisk in beef broth and red wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add bay leaf and thyme.
4. Return lamb to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours.
5. Add potatoes to the stew. Continue to cook, covered, for another 30-45 minutes, or until lamb and potatoes are fork-tender. Remove bay leaf before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed.

name: Stewed rabbit, Puerto Rican style,
description:
A flavorful and rustic Puerto Rican specialty, stewed rabbit (Conejo Guisado) is slow-cooked in a vibrant sofrito-based sauce with potatoes, olives, and aromatic spices, creating a tender and deeply satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2-3 lbs rabbit, cut into serving pieces
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 cup Puerto Rican sofrito
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1/4 cup green olives with pimentos
- 1 can (8 oz) tomato sauce
- 1 cup water or chicken broth
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Season rabbit pieces generously with salt, pepper, and oregano.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown rabbit pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
3. Add sofrito and chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until fragrant and onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Stir in tomato sauce, water or broth, bay leaf, and green olives. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
5. Return the browned rabbit pieces to the pot. Cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 45 minutes.
6. Add the cubed potatoes to the stew. Continue to cook, covered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until rabbit is tender and potatoes are cooked through. Remove bay leaf before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed.

name: Venison or deer, potatoes, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; gravy

name: Chicken or turkey, potatoes, corn, and cheese, with gravy
description:
A comforting and hearty casserole-style dish featuring tender chicken or turkey, fluffy potatoes, sweet corn, and melted cheese, all bound together with a rich, savory gravy.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups cooked chicken or turkey, shredded or cubed
- 3 medium potatoes, cooked and cubed
- 1.5 cups corn (fresh, frozen, or canned, drained)
- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup milk
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens. Season with salt, pepper, and thyme.
3. In a large bowl, gently combine cooked chicken/turkey, cubed potatoes, and corn. Pour about half of the gravy over the mixture and stir to coat.

5. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and the dish is heated through. Serve with remaining gravy on the side.

name: Chicken or turkey, potatoes, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no sauce

Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:

- 2 carrots, sliced

2. In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens. Season with salt, pepper, and sage.
3. In a large bowl, gently combine cooked chicken/turkey, cooked rice, and corn. Pour about half of the gravy over the mixture and stir to coat.
4. Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish. Sprinkle evenly with shredded cheddar cheese.
5. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and the dish is heated through. Serve with remaining gravy on the side.

name: Chicken or turkey, rice, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; soy-based sauce
description:
A savory and aromatic dish featuring tender chicken or turkey, fluffy rice, and a vibrant mix of vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all stir-fried in a rich, umami-packed soy-based sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken or turkey breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 carrots, julienned
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped bok choy or spinach
- 3 cups cooked white or brown rice
- For the Sauce:
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients (soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, cornstarch slurry). Set aside.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken/turkey and stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
3. Add garlic and ginger to the wok, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add julienned carrots and broccoli florets, stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
4. Return chicken/turkey to the wok. Add chopped bok choy/spinach and cooked rice. Pour the sauce over everything.
5. Toss constantly for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients. Serve immediately.

name: Chicken or turkey, rice, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; tomato-based sauce
description:
A vibrant and flavorful dish featuring tender chicken or turkey, fluffy rice, and a medley of nutrient-rich vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all simmered in a tangy, robust tomato-based sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken or turkey breast, cut into chunks
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp dried basil
- 3 cups cooked white or brown rice
- 2 carrots, sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Season chicken/turkey chunks with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken/turkey in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, oregano, and basil, cook for 1 minute more.
3. Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken/turkey to the pot.
4. Add sliced carrots. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 15 minutes.
5. Stir in broccoli florets and kale/spinach. Continue to cook, covered, for another 10-15 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender and chicken/turkey is cooked through. Adjust seasoning as needed.
6. Serve the chicken and vegetable mixture over cooked rice.

name: Pot pie, chicken
description:
A classic comfort food, chicken pot pie features tender chicken and mixed vegetables in a creamy, savory sauce, all baked under a flaky, golden pastry crust.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
- 1 cup chopped carrots
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1 cup chopped celery
- 1/2 cup chopped onion
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1 cup milk
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 2 sheets refrigerated pie crust

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook until browned and cooked through. Remove chicken and set aside.
3. Add carrots, peas, celery, and onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Stir in thyme, salt, and pepper.
5. Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Pour the mixture into a 9-inch pie dish.
6. Place one pie crust over the filling, trim edges, and crimp. Cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbly. Let stand 5-10 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken or turkey, stuffing, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no sauce
description:
A wholesome and satisfying meal featuring tender chicken or turkey, savory stuffing, and a vibrant mix of vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, prepared simply without any added sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken or turkey breast, cooked and sliced/cubed
- 4 cups prepared stuffing (from mix or homemade)
- 2 carrots, steamed and sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets, steamed
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach, lightly sautéed
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp dried sage

Instructions:
1. Prepare stuffing according to package directions or your favorite recipe. Keep warm.
2. Steam carrots and broccoli until tender-crisp. Lightly sauté kale or spinach until wilted.
3. In a large pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the cooked chicken/turkey and warm through. Season with salt, pepper, and sage.
4. Serve portions of warm stuffing, chicken/turkey, and the steamed/sautéed vegetables on plates. No additional sauce is needed, allowing the natural flavors to shine.

- 4 cups prepared stuffing (from mix or homemade)
- 2 carrots, steamed and sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets, steamed
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach, steamed
- For the Gravy:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup milk or cream
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp dried sage (optional)

Instructions:
1. Prepare chicken/turkey, stuffing, and vegetables as instructed (cook/steam).
2. To make the gravy: In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk/cream until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens. Season with salt, pepper, and sage.

name: Chicken or turkey, dumplings, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark green leafy; gravy
description:
A hearty and comforting classic, this dish features tender chicken or turkey, fluffy dumplings, and a vibrant mix of vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all simmered in a rich, savory gravy.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken or turkey thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach
- 4 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour (for gravy)
- 1/2 cup cold water (for gravy)
- For the Dumplings:
- 1.5 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 3/4 cup milk
- 1/4 cup melted butter
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 tsp dried thyme

Instructions:
1. Season chicken/turkey with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken/turkey in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion and carrots to the pot, sauté until softened. Stir in thyme. Return chicken/turkey to the pot. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes.
3. While simmering, prepare dumplings: In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt. Add milk and melted butter, stir until just combined.
4. Drop spoonfuls of dumpling dough onto the simmering stew. Cover tightly and cook for 15-20 minutes without lifting the lid, until dumplings are fluffy and cooked through.
5. Remove dumplings and chicken/turkey to a plate. In a small bowl, whisk 1/2 cup flour with 1/2 cup cold water until smooth. Slowly whisk into the simmering broth to thicken into gravy. Add broccoli and kale/spinach, cook until tender-crisp.
6. Return chicken/turkey to the gravy. Serve hot with dumplings and vegetables.

name: Chicken fricassee, Puerto Rican style
description:
A vibrant and flavorful Puerto Rican classic, Pollo en Fricasé features tender chicken pieces simmered in a rich, aromatic tomato-based sauce with olives, potatoes, and a medley of traditional spices.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2.5 lbs chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks), skin on or off
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 cup Puerto Rican sofrito
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (8 oz) tomato sauce
- 1/4 cup alcaparrado (capers and olives mix)
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Season chicken pieces generously with salt, pepper, oregano, and cumin.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
3. Add sofrito, chopped onion, and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until fragrant and onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Stir in tomato sauce, alcaparrado, chicken broth, and bay leaf. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
5. Return the browned chicken pieces to the pot. Cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 30 minutes.
6. Add the cubed potatoes to the stew. Continue to cook, covered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and potatoes are cooked through. Remove bay leaf before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed and garnish with fresh cilantro.

name: Paella with seafood
description:
A magnificent Spanish classic, seafood paella is a vibrant and aromatic rice dish, richly flavored with saffron and brimming with a delicious assortment of fresh seafood, cooked to perfection in a wide, shallow pan.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 red bell pepper, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Pinch of saffron threads, steeped in 1/4 cup warm water
- 2 cups bomba or arborio rice
- 4 cups seafood broth
- 1 lb mixed seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari, scallops)
- 1/2 cup frozen peas
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Lemon wedges (for serving)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow skillet over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper, sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
2. Add minced garlic, diced tomatoes, and smoked paprika. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
3. Stir in rice, coating it evenly. Pour in seafood broth and saffron water. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover (if possible, or just let simmer uncovered), and cook for 15 minutes without stirring.
4. Arrange the mixed seafood and peas on top of the rice. Continue to cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until rice is tender, liquid is absorbed, and seafood is cooked through. Avoid stirring to allow a 'socarrat' (crispy rice bottom) to form.
5. Remove from heat, cover with foil or a clean kitchen towel, and let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Shrimp chow mein or chop suey with noodles
description:
A delightful Asian-inspired dish, shrimp chow mein/chop suey features succulent shrimp and crisp-tender vegetables, stir-fried in a savory sauce and served over or with noodles.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 8 oz chow mein noodles (crispy or soft, as preferred)
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups shredded cabbage
- 1 cup sliced celery
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- 1/2 cup chicken or vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- Salt and white pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss shrimp with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch. Set aside.
2. If using soft noodles, cook according to package directions. If using crispy, prepare as desired.
3. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add shrimp and stir-fry until pink and cooked through (about 2-3 minutes). Remove and set aside.
4. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add onion, cabbage, celery, and carrots. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
5. Return shrimp to the wok. Add bean sprouts, chicken/vegetable broth, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using). Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until heated through and sauce slightly thickens.
6. Stir in sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Serve immediately over or mixed with chow mein noodles.

name: Shrimp creole, with rice
description:
A vibrant and spicy Louisiana classic, Shrimp Creole features succulent shrimp simmered in a rich, flavorful tomato-based sauce with the 'holy trinity' of celery, bell peppers, and onions, traditionally served over fluffy white rice.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 cup chicken or seafood broth
- 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (or to taste)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 3 cups cooked white rice (for serving)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion, green bell pepper, and celery. Sauté until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
2. Add minced garlic, oregano, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken/seafood broth, and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
4. Season shrimp with salt and pepper. Add shrimp to the simmering sauce and cook for 3-5 minutes, or until shrimp are pink and cooked through. Do not overcook.
5. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve hot over fluffy white rice, garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Tuna noodle casserole with vegetables, cream or white sauce
description:
A beloved American comfort food, this classic tuna noodle casserole features tender egg noodles, flaky tuna, and mixed vegetables, all baked in a creamy, savory sauce until bubbly and golden.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 8 oz egg noodles, cooked and drained
- 2 cans (5 oz each) tuna, drained and flaked
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1/2 cup chopped celery
- 1/4 cup chopped onion
- For the Cream Sauce:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups milk
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (optional, for topping)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. To make the cream sauce: In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
3. In a large bowl, combine cooked egg noodles, drained tuna, frozen peas, chopped celery, and chopped onion. Pour the cream sauce over the mixture and stir gently to combine.
4. Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. If desired, sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
5. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the topping is golden brown. Let stand for a few minutes before serving.

name: Fish, noodles, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark green leafy; cheese sauce
description:
A comforting and cheesy dish featuring flaky fish, tender noodles, and a vibrant mix of vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all smothered in a rich, creamy cheese sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb white fish fillets (cod, haddock, or tilapia), cooked and flaked
- 8 oz egg noodles, cooked according to package directions
- 2 carrots, steamed and sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets, steamed
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach, steamed
- For the Cheese Sauce:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups milk
- 1.5 cups shredded cheddar cheese (or your favorite melting cheese)
- 1/2 tsp mustard powder (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Prepare fish, noodles, and vegetables as instructed (cook/steam).
2. To make the cheese sauce: In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened.
3. Remove from heat and stir in shredded cheese until melted and smooth. Add mustard powder, salt, and pepper. Adjust seasoning.
4. Gently combine the cooked fish, noodles, carrots, broccoli, and kale/spinach in a large serving bowl or casserole dish.
5. Pour the hot cheese sauce over the mixture and gently toss to coat. Serve warm.

name: Fish, noodles, and vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark-green leafy; cheese sauce
description:
A comforting and cheesy dish featuring flaky fish, tender noodles, and a selection of non-cruciferous, non-dark leafy vegetables, all smothered in a rich, creamy cheese sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb white fish fillets (cod, haddock, or tilapia), cooked and flaked
- 8 oz egg noodles, cooked according to package directions
- 1 cup green beans, steamed
- 1 cup peas (fresh or frozen), steamed
- For the Cheese Sauce:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups milk
- 1.5 cups shredded cheddar cheese (or your favorite melting cheese)
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Prepare fish, noodles, green beans, and peas as instructed (cook/steam).
2. To make the cheese sauce: In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened.
3. Remove from heat and stir in shredded cheese until melted and smooth. Add garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Adjust seasoning.
4. Gently combine the cooked fish, noodles, green beans, and peas in a large serving bowl or casserole dish.
5. Pour the hot cheese sauce over the mixture and gently toss to coat. Serve warm.

name: Soup, bouillabaisse
description:
A classic Provençal fish stew, bouillabaisse is a rich and complex seafood soup, traditionally made with various Mediterranean fish and shellfish, simmered in a flavorful broth with tomatoes, saffron, and herbs.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 leeks, white and light green parts, sliced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 fennel bulb, thinly sliced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 6 cups fish stock
- 1 cup dry white wine
- Pinch of saffron threads
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 lb firm white fish (cod, snapper), cut into chunks
- 1/2 lb mussels, scrubbed and debearded
- 1/2 lb shrimp, peeled and deveined
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)
- Crusty bread (for serving)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium heat. Add onion, leeks, garlic, and fennel. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
2. Stir in crushed tomatoes, fish stock, white wine, saffron, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
3. Season the fish chunks, mussels, and shrimp with salt and pepper.
4. Add the firm white fish to the simmering broth. Cook for 5 minutes. Then add the mussels and shrimp. Cover and cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until mussels have opened and shrimp are pink and cooked through. Discard any unopened mussels.
5. Remove bay leaf. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve hot in bowls, garnished with fresh parsley, and with crusty bread for dipping.

name: Tuna noodle casserole with vegetables and mushroom sauce
description:
A comforting and savory American classic, this tuna noodle casserole features tender egg noodles, flaky tuna, and mixed vegetables, all baked in a rich, earthy mushroom sauce until bubbly and golden.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 8 oz egg noodles, cooked and drained
- 2 cans (5 oz each) tuna, drained and flaked
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1/2 cup chopped celery
- 1/4 cup chopped onion
- For the Mushroom Sauce:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 8 oz fresh mushrooms, sliced
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups milk
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (optional, for topping)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. To make the mushroom sauce: In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
3. In a large bowl, combine cooked egg noodles, drained tuna, frozen peas, chopped celery, and chopped onion. Pour the mushroom sauce over the mixture and stir gently to combine.
4. Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. If desired, sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
5. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the topping is golden brown. Let stand for a few minutes before serving.

name: Codfish with starchy vegetables, Puerto Rican style
description:
A rustic and flavorful Puerto Rican dish, Bacalao con Viandas features salted codfish rehydrated and cooked with an assortment of starchy root vegetables like yuca, yautía, and potatoes, often dressed with olive oil and onions.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 30 minutes (plus 24 hr soaking)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb salted codfish (bacalao)
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and quartered
- 1 lb yuca (cassava), peeled and cut into large chunks
- 1 lb yautía (taro root), peeled and cut into large chunks
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Rinse codfish thoroughly. Soak in cold water for at least 24 hours, changing water several times, to remove excess salt. Drain and flake the codfish, removing any bones or skin.
2. In a large pot, boil potatoes, yuca, and yautía in lightly salted water until tender, about 20-30 minutes. Drain and set aside.
3. In a separate saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add sliced onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
4. Add the flaked codfish to the saucepan with the onions and garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes, gently stirring, until heated through and flavors meld.
5. Arrange the boiled starchy vegetables on a serving platter. Top with the cooked codfish and onion mixture. Drizzle with any remaining olive oil from the pan. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve warm.

name: Biscayne codfish, Puerto Rican style
description:
A vibrant and savory Puerto Rican dish, Bacalao a la Vizcaína (Biscayne Codfish) features salted codfish simmered in a rich tomato-based sauce with bell peppers, olives, chickpeas, and potatoes, offering a delightful blend of textures and flavors.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 30 minutes (plus 24 hr soaking)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb salted codfish (bacalao)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 1 red bell pepper, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
- 1/2 cup green olives with pimentos
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1/2 cup dry white wine (optional)
- 1/2 cup water or fish broth
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Rinse codfish thoroughly. Soak in cold water for at least 24 hours, changing water several times, to remove excess salt. Drain, flake, and remove any bones or skin.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and bell peppers, sauté until softened, about 7-10 minutes. Add minced garlic and oregano, cook for 1 minute more.
3. Stir in tomato sauce, chickpeas, green olives, white wine (if using), water/broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
4. Add the cubed potatoes and flaked codfish to the pot. Gently stir to combine. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and flavors have melded.
5. Remove bay leaf. Adjust seasoning as needed (codfish can still be salty). Garnish with fresh parsley and serve warm.

name: Stew, NFS
description:
A generic term for a hearty and comforting dish, stew typically features chunks of meat and/or vegetables simmered slowly in a flavorful liquid until tender, offering a deeply satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs stew meat (beef, lamb, or chicken), cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, peeled and sliced
- 2 celery stalks, sliced
- 3 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 4 cups beef or chicken broth
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Pat meat dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Brown meat in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
3. Gradually whisk in broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add bay leaf and thyme.
4. Return meat to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours (for beef/lamb) or 20 minutes (for chicken).
5. Add potatoes to the stew. Continue to cook, covered, for another 30-45 minutes (for beef/lamb) or 20-30 minutes (for chicken), or until meat and potatoes are fork-tender. Remove bay leaf before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed and garnish with fresh parsley.

name: Chow mein or chop suey, NS as to type of meat, with noodles
description:
A versatile Asian-inspired dish, chow mein or chop suey features tender meat (type unspecified) and crisp-tender vegetables, stir-fried in a savory sauce and served over or with noodles.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb protein (chicken, pork, beef, or tofu), thinly sliced
- 8 oz chow mein noodles (crispy or soft, as preferred)
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups shredded cabbage
- 1 cup sliced celery
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- 1/2 cup chicken or vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- Salt and white pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss protein with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch. Set aside.
2. If using soft noodles, cook according to package directions. If using crispy, prepare as desired.
3. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add protein and stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
4. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add onion, cabbage, celery, and carrots. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
5. Return protein to the wok. Add bean sprouts, chicken/vegetable broth, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using). Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until heated through and sauce slightly thickens.
6. Stir in sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Serve immediately over or mixed with chow mein noodles.

name: Paella, NFS
description:
A magnificent Spanish classic, paella is a vibrant and aromatic rice dish, richly flavored with saffron and often brimming with a delicious assortment of meats, seafood, and vegetables, cooked to perfection in a wide, shallow pan.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into chunks
- 1/2 lb chorizo sausage, sliced
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 red bell pepper, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, drained
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- Pinch of saffron threads, steeped in 1/4 cup warm water
- 2 cups bomba or arborio rice
- 4 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup frozen peas
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Lemon wedges (for serving)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and chorizo, cook until browned. Remove and set aside.
2. Add onion and bell pepper to the pan, sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic, diced tomatoes, and smoked paprika. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
3. Stir in rice, coating it evenly. Pour in chicken broth and saffron water. Season with salt and pepper. Return chicken and chorizo to the pan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover (if possible, or just let simmer uncovered), and cook for 15 minutes without stirring.
4. Add peas on top of the rice. Continue to cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Avoid stirring to allow a 'socarrat' (crispy rice bottom) to form.
5. Remove from heat, cover with foil or a clean kitchen towel, and let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Chow mein or chop suey, various types of meat, with noodles
description:
A delightful and versatile Asian-inspired dish, this chow mein or chop suey features a medley of different meats and crisp-tender vegetables, stir-fried in a savory sauce and served over or with noodles.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 lb chicken breast, thinly sliced
- 1/2 lb pork loin, thinly sliced
- 8 oz chow mein noodles (crispy or soft, as preferred)
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups shredded cabbage
- 1 cup sliced celery
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- Salt and white pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss chicken and pork with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch. Set aside.
2. If using soft noodles, cook according to package directions. If using crispy, prepare as desired.
3. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add chicken and pork and stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
4. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add onion, cabbage, celery, and carrots. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
5. Return cooked meats to the wok. Add bean sprouts, chicken broth, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using). Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until heated through and sauce slightly thickens.
6. Stir in sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Serve immediately over or mixed with chow mein noodles.

name: Stewed tripe, with potatoes, Puerto Rican style
description:
A hearty and flavorful Puerto Rican delicacy, Mondongo (Stewed Tripe) features tender tripe slow-cooked in a rich, aromatic tomato-based sauce with potatoes, chickpeas, and a medley of traditional spices, creating a deeply satisfying and comforting meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 30 minutes (plus tripe cooking time)

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs beef tripe, cleaned and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 cup Puerto Rican sofrito
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (8 oz) tomato sauce
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 4 cups beef broth or water
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Boil tripe in water for 1-2 hours, or until tender. Drain and set aside.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sofrito, chopped onion, and minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant and onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
3. Stir in tomato sauce, chickpeas, beef broth/water, bay leaf, oregano, and cumin. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
4. Add the cooked tripe and cubed potatoes to the pot. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 30-45 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and flavors have melded.
5. Remove bay leaf before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

name: Gumbo with rice
description:
A quintessential Louisiana comfort food, gumbo is a rich and savory stew, typically made with a dark roux, the 'holy trinity' of vegetables, and various meats or seafood, served generously over fluffy white rice.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup vegetable oil
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour (for roux)
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 6 cups chicken or seafood broth
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes (optional)
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
- 1/2 lb andouille sausage, sliced
- 1/2 lb shrimp, peeled and deveined (optional)
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (or to taste)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 3 cups cooked white rice (for serving)
- Fresh parsley or green onions, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Make the roux: In a large Dutch oven, heat oil over medium heat. Gradually whisk in flour. Cook, stirring constantly, for 20-30 minutes until the roux is a rich, dark brown color (like chocolate). Be patient and don't burn it!
2. Add onion, bell pepper, and celery to the roux. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, oregano, thyme, and cayenne pepper, cook for 1 minute more.
3. Gradually whisk in chicken/seafood broth until smooth. Add diced tomatoes (if using), chicken, and sausage. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 30-45 minutes, or until chicken is tender.
4. If using shrimp, add them during the last 5 minutes of cooking, until pink and cooked through.
5. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve hot over cooked white rice, garnished with fresh parsley or green onions.

name: Jambalaya with meat and rice
description:
A flavorful and hearty Louisiana one-pot dish, jambalaya features rice cooked with a medley of meats (often sausage, chicken, and/or pork), vegetables, and a rich, spicy broth, creating a robust and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 lb smoked sausage (andouille or kielbasa), sliced
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, undrained
- 2 cups long-grain white rice, uncooked
- 4 cups chicken broth
- 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning
- 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (or to taste)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley or green onions, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Add chicken and sausage, cook until browned. Remove and set aside.
2. Add onion, bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 7-10 minutes. Add minced garlic, Cajun seasoning, and cayenne pepper, cook for 1 minute more.
3. Stir in diced tomatoes (with liquid) and uncooked rice. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
4. Pour in chicken broth. Return chicken and sausage to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed.
5. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5-10 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Adjust seasoning as needed. Garnish with fresh parsley or green onions and serve hot.

name: Beef and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no potatoes, no sauce
description:
A lean and flavorful meal featuring tender beef and a vibrant mix of nutrient-rich vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, prepared simply without potatoes or any added sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 carrots, julienned or thinly sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano

Instructions:
1. Season beef slices with salt, pepper, and oregano.
2. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add beef in batches and stir-fry quickly until browned and cooked to desired doneness. Remove and set aside.
3. Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Add julienned carrots, broccoli florets, and sliced onion. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Add minced garlic and chopped kale/spinach. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until greens are wilted. Return beef to the skillet and toss everything together to heat through.
5. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve immediately.

name: Beef and vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark-green leafy; no potatoes, no sauce
description:
A lean and straightforward meal featuring tender beef and a selection of non-cruciferous, non-dark leafy vegetables, prepared simply without potatoes or any added sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup green beans, trimmed
- 1 cup sliced mushrooms
- 1 cup peas (fresh or frozen)
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme

Instructions:
1. Season beef slices with salt, pepper, and thyme.
2. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add beef in batches and stir-fry quickly until browned and cooked to desired doneness. Remove and set aside.
3. Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Add green beans, sliced mushrooms, and sliced onion. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Add minced garlic and peas. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until heated through. Return beef to the skillet and toss everything together to heat through.
5. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve immediately.

name: Beef shish kabob with vegetables, excluding potatoes
description:
A classic grilled delight, beef shish kabobs feature tender cubes of marinated beef skewered with a colorful assortment of fresh vegetables, grilled to perfection for a smoky, flavorful meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus marinating time)

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs beef sirloin or tenderloin, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 red bell pepper, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
- 1 green bell pepper, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
- 1 large onion, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes
- Wooden or metal skewers

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk together olive oil, soy sauce, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, oregano, and black pepper. Add beef cubes and toss to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
2. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes to prevent burning.
3. Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
4. Thread beef cubes alternately with red bell pepper, green bell pepper, onion, and cherry tomatoes onto the skewers.
5. Grill kabobs for 8-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until beef is cooked to desired doneness and vegetables are tender-crisp and slightly charred. Serve immediately.

name: Beef with vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no potatoes, tomato-based sauce
description:
A hearty and flavorful dish featuring tender beef and a vibrant mix of nutrient-rich vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all simmered in a tangy, robust tomato-based sauce without potatoes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp dried basil
- 2 carrots, sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, oregano, and basil, cook for 1 minute more.
3. Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Return beef to the pot.
4. Add sliced carrots. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is nearly tender.
5. Stir in broccoli florets and kale/spinach. Continue to cook, covered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender and beef is cooked through. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve warm.

name: Swiss steak
description:
A classic comfort food, Swiss steak features tenderized beef steaks braised slowly in a rich, savory tomato-based gravy with vegetables, resulting in incredibly tender meat and a deeply flavorful sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs beef round steak, cut into 4-6 serving pieces
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 large onion, sliced
- 1 green bell pepper, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tsp dried oregano

Instructions:
1. Combine flour, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish. Dredge beef steaks in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Brown steaks on both sides. Remove and set aside.
3. Add sliced onion and bell pepper to the pot, sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and oregano, cook for 1 minute more.
4. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer.
5. Return browned steaks to the pot. Ensure they are mostly submerged in the sauce. Cover tightly and reduce heat to low. Simmer on the stovetop for 2-2.5 hours, or bake in a preheated 325°F (160°C) oven for 2-2.5 hours, until beef is fork-tender. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve hot.

name: Beef rolls, stuffed with vegetables or meat mixture, tomato-based sauce
description:
A savory and comforting dish, beef rolls feature thin slices of beef wrapped around a flavorful stuffing of vegetables or a meat mixture, then slowly braised in a rich, tangy tomato-based sauce until tender.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs beef round steak or flank steak, thinly sliced (about 6-8 slices)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 tsp dried Italian seasoning
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- For the Stuffing (Vegetable):
- 1 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1/2 cup finely chopped bell pepper
- 1/4 cup finely chopped parsley
- 1 egg, beaten
- 2 tbsp milk

Instructions:
1. Prepare stuffing: In a bowl, combine breadcrumbs, Parmesan, bell pepper, parsley, beaten egg, milk, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
2. Lay beef slices flat. Place a spoonful of stuffing on one end of each slice. Roll up tightly and secure with toothpicks or kitchen twine.
3. Season beef rolls with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Brown beef rolls on all sides. Remove and set aside.
4. Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot, sauté until softened. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and Italian seasoning. Bring to a simmer.
5. Return beef rolls to the pot. Ensure they are mostly submerged in the sauce. Cover tightly and reduce heat to low. Simmer on the stovetop for 1.5-2 hours, or bake in a preheated 325°F (160°C) oven for 1.5-2 hours, until beef is fork-tender. Remove toothpicks/twine before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed.

name: Beef with vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark-green leafy; no potatoes, tomato-based sauce
description:
A comforting and savory dish featuring tender beef and a selection of non-cruciferous, non-dark leafy vegetables, all simmered in a robust, tangy tomato-based sauce without potatoes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 tsp dried Italian seasoning
- 1 cup green beans, trimmed
- 1 cup peas (fresh or frozen)
- 1 cup sliced mushrooms
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and Italian seasoning, cook for 1 minute more.
3. Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Return beef to the pot.
4. Add sliced mushrooms and green beans. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is nearly tender.
5. Stir in peas. Continue to cook, covered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender and beef is cooked through. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve warm.

name: Beef with vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no potatoes, mushroom sauce
description:
A rich and earthy dish featuring tender beef and a vibrant mix of nutrient-rich vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all enveloped in a savory, creamy mushroom sauce without potatoes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs beef sirloin or tenderloin, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 8 oz fresh mushrooms, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 carrots, sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach
- For the Mushroom Sauce:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups beef broth
- 1/2 cup heavy cream (optional)
- 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches, then remove and set aside.
2. Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pot. Add onion and sliced mushrooms, sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 7-10 minutes. Add minced garlic, cook for 1 minute more.
3. To make the sauce: Melt butter in the same pot. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in beef broth and heavy cream (if using) until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Stir in Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
4. Return beef to the sauce. Add sliced carrots. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is nearly tender.
5. Stir in broccoli florets and kale/spinach. Continue to cook, covered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender and beef is cooked through. Adjust seasoning as needed. Serve warm.

name: Beef and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no potatoes, soy-based sauce
description:
A savory and aromatic stir-fry featuring tender beef and a vibrant mix of nutrient-rich vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all tossed in a rich, umami-packed soy-based sauce without potatoes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 carrots, julienned
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup chopped bok choy or spinach
- For the Sauce:
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients (soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, cornstarch slurry). Set aside.
2. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add beef and stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
3. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add julienned carrots and broccoli florets, stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
4. Return beef to the wok. Add chopped bok choy/spinach. Pour the sauce over everything.
5. Toss constantly for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients. Serve immediately.

name: Beef and broccoli
description:
A classic Chinese-American stir-fry, Beef and Broccoli features tender slices of beef and crisp-tender broccoli florets, all coated in a savory, slightly sweet ginger-garlic soy sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 4 cups broccoli florets
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- For the Sauce:
- 1/2 cup beef broth
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss beef slices with 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Set aside for 15 minutes.
2. In a separate bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients (beef broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, cornstarch slurry). Set aside.
3. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add beef in batches and stir-fry quickly until browned. Remove and set aside.
4. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add broccoli florets and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
5. Return beef to the wok. Pour the sauce over everything. Toss constantly for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients. Serve immediately, often with rice.

name: Beef, tofu, and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no potatoes, soy-based sauce
description:
A wholesome and flavorful stir-fry featuring tender beef, soft tofu, and a vibrant mix of nutrient-rich vegetables like carrots, broccoli, or dark-green leafy greens, all tossed in a rich, umami-packed soy-based sauce without potatoes.

3. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add tofu cubes and pan-fry until golden brown on all sides. Remove and set aside.
4. Add garlic and ginger to the wok, stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add julienned carrots and broccoli florets, stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp.

name: Szechuan beef
description:
A fiery and flavorful Chinese-American dish, Szechuan Beef features crispy strips of beef stir-fried with vibrant vegetables in a spicy, sweet, and savory Szechuan sauce, known for its distinctive numbing heat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil (divided)
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 green bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1/2 onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 1-2 tbsp dried red chilies (optional, to taste)
- For the Sauce:
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tsp Szechuan peppercorns, crushed (optional)
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss beef slices with 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Set aside for 15 minutes.
2. In a separate bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients (broth, soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, Szechuan peppercorns, cornstarch slurry). Set aside.
3. Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add beef in batches and stir-fry quickly until browned and slightly crispy. Remove and set aside.

5. Return beef to the wok. Pour the sauce over everything. Toss constantly for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients. Serve immediately, often with rice.

name: Hunan beef
description:
A bold and spicy Chinese-American stir-fry, Hunan Beef features tender slices of beef and crisp vegetables in a rich, fiery sauce, known for its robust flavors and a kick of heat.

name: Beef chow mein or chop suey, no noodles
description:
A savory and satisfying Chinese-American dish, beef chow mein or chop suey features tender strips of beef and crisp-tender vegetables, stir-fried in a rich sauce, served without noodles for a lighter option.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 2 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 large onion, thinly sliced
- 2 cups shredded cabbage
- 1 cup sliced celery
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- 1/2 cup beef broth
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- Salt and white pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, toss beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch. Set aside.
2. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add beef and stir-fry until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
3. Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add onion, cabbage, celery, and carrots. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Return beef to the wok. Add bean sprouts, beef broth, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, and oyster sauce (if using). Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until heated through and sauce slightly thickens.
5. Stir in sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Serve immediately, often with rice.

name: Kung Pao beef
description:
A popular and spicy Chinese-American stir-fry, Kung Pao Beef features tender beef, crunchy peanuts, and vibrant vegetables, all tossed in a bold, sweet, sour, and spicy sauce with a hint of Szechuan peppercorns.

- 1 green bell pepper, diced

- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 6-8 dried red chilies (optional, to taste)

- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp brown sugar

name: Beef, ground, with egg and onion
description:
A simple yet satisfying dish, ground beef with egg and onion is a versatile combination, often forming the base for patties, meatloaf, or a flavorful scramble, offering a comforting and protein-rich meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground beef
- 1 large onion, finely chopped
- 1-2 eggs, beaten
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
2. Add ground beef to the skillet. Break it up with a spoon and cook until browned and no longer pink. Drain any excess fat.
3. Season the beef and onion mixture with salt, pepper, and garlic powder (if using).
4. Pour the beaten egg(s) over the beef mixture. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until the egg is cooked and scrambled throughout the beef. Serve immediately.

name: Beef salad
description:

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef sirloin or flank steak
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 head romaine lettuce, chopped
- 1 cucumber, sliced
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped
- For the Dressing:
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Season beef steak with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef for 3-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Let rest for 5 minutes, then thinly slice against the grain.
2. Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tbsp olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
3. In a large bowl, combine chopped romaine lettuce, sliced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and chopped cilantro/parsley.
4. Add the sliced beef to the salad. Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.

name: Beef taco filling: beef, cheese, tomato, taco sauce
description:

Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground beef
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 1 packet (1 oz) taco seasoning mix
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 cup shredded cheddar or Mexican blend cheese
- 1 large tomato, diced

3. Stir in taco seasoning mix and water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid has mostly evaporated and beef is well seasoned.
4. To serve as filling: Keep the seasoned beef warm. Offer shredded cheese, diced tomato, and taco sauce on the side for assembly into taco shells or tortillas.
