name: Soup, meatball
description:
A hearty and comforting soup, brimming with tender meatballs, often simmered in a rich broth with vegetables and pasta, offering a satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground beef (or mixed meat)
- 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 6 cups beef broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes
- 1/2 cup small pasta (e.g., ditalini)

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, oregano, salt, and pepper. Form into small meatballs.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown meatballs on all sides; remove and set aside.
3. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Pour in beef broth and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
5. Add the meatballs back to the pot. Stir in pasta. Cook until pasta is al dente and meatballs are cooked through, about 10-15 minutes.
6. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.

name: Soup, pho, with meat
description:
A fragrant and deeply flavorful Vietnamese noodle soup, featuring tender slices of meat (typically beef or chicken), delicate rice noodles, and fresh herbs in a rich, aromatic broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 30 minutes (active) + 4-8 hours (simmering)

Ingredients:
- 4 lbs beef bones (knuckles, marrow, oxtail)
- 1 large onion, halved
- 4-inch ginger, sliced
- 3 star anise
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 5 cloves
- 1 black cardamom pod
- 1 tbsp coriander seeds
- 1 tbsp fennel seeds
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 2 tbsp fish sauce
- 1 lb flat rice noodles
- 1 lb thinly sliced beef (sirloin, brisket, or flank)
- Fresh herbs (cilantro, basil, mint), bean sprouts, lime wedges, sliced jalapeños for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse beef bones thoroughly. Blanch bones in boiling water for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse again.
2. Roast onion and ginger until fragrant and slightly charred. Toast star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, coriander, and fennel seeds in a dry pan until aromatic.
3. Combine blanched bones, roasted onion and ginger, toasted spices, salt, and sugar in a large stockpot. Add 6-8 quarts of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for at least 3-4 hours (or up to 8 hours), skimming any foam.
4. Strain the broth, discarding solids. Return broth to a clean pot, add fish sauce, and adjust seasoning.
5. Cook rice noodles according to package directions.
6. To serve, place cooked noodles in a bowl, top with thinly sliced raw beef. Ladle hot broth over the beef (it will cook in the hot broth). Garnish with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime, and jalapeños.

name: Soup, pho, no meat
description:
A vegetarian rendition of the classic Vietnamese pho, featuring delicate rice noodles and fresh herbs in a rich, aromatic vegetable broth, offering a flavorful and light experience.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes (active) + 30-60 minutes (simmering)

Ingredients:
- 8 cups vegetable broth
- 1 large onion, halved
- 4-inch ginger, sliced
- 3 star anise
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 5 cloves
- 1 black cardamom pod
- 1 tbsp coriander seeds
- 1 tbsp fennel seeds
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 lb flat rice noodles
- Assorted vegetables (e.g., sliced mushrooms, bok choy, carrots)
- Fresh herbs (cilantro, basil, mint), bean sprouts, lime wedges, sliced jalapeños for garnish

Instructions:
1. Roast onion and ginger until fragrant and slightly charred. Toast star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, coriander, and fennel seeds in a dry pan until aromatic.
2. Combine vegetable broth, roasted onion and ginger, toasted spices, salt, and sugar in a large stockpot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for at least 30 minutes to an hour.
3. Strain the broth, discarding solids. Return broth to a clean pot, add soy sauce, and adjust seasoning.
4. Cook rice noodles according to package directions. Lightly steam or sauté desired vegetables.
5. To serve, place cooked noodles in a bowl, top with cooked vegetables. Ladle hot broth over. Garnish with fresh herbs, bean sprouts, lime, and jalapeños.

name: Soup, pepperpot
description:
A rich and spicy stew-like soup, traditionally from Philadelphia, featuring tripe, other meats, and vegetables, seasoned with a generous amount of black pepper for a distinctive kick.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef tripe, cleaned and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 lb stewing beef, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 1 green bell pepper, diced
- 4 cups beef broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes
- 1/2 cup diced potatoes
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp black pepper (or more to taste)
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- Salt to taste
- Optional: dumplings or pasta

Instructions:
1. Boil tripe in water for 30 minutes, drain, and rinse. Repeat this process once more to tenderize and clean. Pat dry.
2. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Brown stewing beef on all sides; remove and set aside.
3. Add onion, carrots, celery, and bell pepper to the pot and cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
4. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in beef broth and diced tomatoes, bringing to a simmer.
5. Add the browned beef, tripe, potatoes, black pepper, and thyme. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until meats are tender.
6. Season with salt to taste. If desired, add dumplings or pasta during the last 15-20 minutes of cooking.

name: Soup, beef, canned
description: A convenient, ready-to-heat soup featuring beef and often vegetables in a savory broth, offering a quick and easy meal solution from a can.

name: Soup, sopa or caldo de res
description:
A traditional and comforting Mexican beef soup, rich with tender chunks of beef, a medley of fresh vegetables, and often corn on the cob, simmered in a flavorful broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs beef short ribs or beef shank, bone-in
- 1 large onion, quartered
- 4 cloves garlic, smashed
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 8 cups water
- 3 carrots, cut into large chunks
- 3 celery stalks, cut into large chunks
- 2 zucchini, cut into large chunks
- 2 ears of corn, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 1/2 head of cabbage, cut into wedges
- Optional: 2 potatoes, peeled and quartered

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, combine beef, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, skim any foam, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is tender.
2. Remove beef from the pot and set aside to cool slightly. Strain the broth, discarding onion and garlic. Return broth to the pot.
3. Add carrots, celery, and potatoes (if using) to the broth. Simmer for 15 minutes.
4. Shred or cut the beef into smaller pieces. Add zucchini, corn, and cabbage to the pot. Return beef to the pot. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender.
5. Adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot, often with lime wedges and warm tortillas.

name: Soup, pozole
description:
A hearty and celebratory Mexican stew, featuring tender hominy and succulent pork (or chicken), simmered in a rich, often chili-infused broth, and traditionally garnished with fresh toppings.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs pork shoulder or pork butt, cut into large chunks
- 1 large onion, halved
- 4 cloves garlic, smashed
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 (25 oz) can hominy, drained and rinsed
- 8 cups water or chicken broth
- For the red chili sauce (Pozole Rojo): 8-10 dried guajillo chilies, 2-3 dried ancho chilies, 2 cloves garlic, 1/4 onion, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp oregano
- Garnishes: shredded cabbage or lettuce, sliced radishes, diced onion, lime wedges, dried oregano, tostadas

Instructions:
1. Place pork, halved onion, smashed garlic, salt, pepper, and water/broth in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender.
2. Remove pork, shred it, and set aside. Strain the broth, discarding solids.
3. For the chili sauce: Remove stems and seeds from dried chilies. Boil chilies in water for 10-15 minutes until softened. Blend softened chilies with 1 cup of their cooking liquid, 2 cloves garlic, 1/4 onion, cumin, and oregano until smooth. Strain the chili sauce into the broth.
4. Add shredded pork and drained hominy to the broth. Simmer for 20-30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
5. Serve hot with desired garnishes.

name: Soup, Italian wedding
description:
A beloved Italian-American soup, featuring tiny meatballs, tender pasta, and fresh greens (like escarole or spinach) in a savory chicken broth, symbolizing the 'marriage' of flavors.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- For meatballs: 1/2 lb ground beef, 1/4 lb ground pork, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, salt and pepper
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 carrots, finely diced
- 2 celery stalks, finely diced
- 8 cups chicken broth
- 1/2 cup small pasta (e.g., acini di pepe, orzo)
- 4 cups fresh spinach or escarole, chopped
- Optional: extra grated Parmesan for serving

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine ground beef, pork, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, parsley, salt, and pepper. Form into tiny meatballs (about 1/2 inch).
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
3. Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer. Carefully drop the meatballs into the simmering broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until meatballs are cooked through.
4. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Stir in spinach or escarole and cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
5. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with extra Parmesan if desired.

name: Soup, pork or ham
description:
A comforting and savory soup, often featuring tender pieces of pork or ham, simmered with vegetables and sometimes beans or potatoes in a rich, flavorful broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes (if using diced ham) / 2 hours (if using ham hock)

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb smoked ham hock or leftover cooked ham, diced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth
- 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 cup diced potatoes
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. If using ham hock, simmer it in 6 cups of water for 1.5-2 hours until meat falls off the bone. Remove hock, shred meat, discard bone, and use the cooking liquid as broth. If using diced ham, heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 7 minutes.
2. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Pour in broth (or ham hock liquid). Add diced ham (if not using hock), cannellini beans, potatoes, and thyme. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
3. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in fresh parsley before serving.

name: Soup, broth
description:
A light and clear liquid, typically made by simmering meat, bones, or vegetables in water with herbs and spices, forming the flavorful base for many soups and dishes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 cups
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 8 cups water
- 1 lb chicken bones (or beef bones, or vegetable scraps like onion peels, carrot ends, celery leaves)
- 1 large onion, quartered
- 2 carrots, roughly chopped
- 2 celery stalks, roughly chopped
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 tsp whole black peppercorns
- Optional: fresh parsley stems, thyme sprigs

Instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a large stockpot. Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce heat to low. Skim any foam that rises to the surface.
2. Cover partially and simmer gently for at least 1-2 hours for vegetable broth, or 3-4 hours for chicken/beef broth. The longer it simmers, the more flavor it will develop.
3. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding all solids. Let cool completely before storing in an airtight container in the refrigerator or freezer.

name: Soup, chicken, canned
description: A convenient, ready-to-heat soup featuring chicken pieces and often noodles or rice in a savory broth, offering a quick and easy meal solution from a can.

name: Soup, chicken
description:
A universally comforting and nourishing soup, featuring tender chicken, a medley of vegetables, and often noodles or rice, all simmered in a rich, savory broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 cups chicken broth
- 1 cup egg noodles or rice
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot; cook until softened, about 7 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer. Return chicken to the pot. Add egg noodles or rice and cook according to package directions until tender.
4. Stir in fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Soup, sopa or caldo de pollo
description:
A traditional and restorative Mexican chicken soup, brimming with tender chicken pieces, a colorful array of vegetables, and often rice or pasta, all in a flavorful, aromatic broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 whole chicken (about 3-4 lbs), cut into pieces, or 2 lbs chicken thighs/drumsticks
- 1 large onion, quartered
- 4 cloves garlic, smashed
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 8-10 cups water
- 3 carrots, cut into large chunks
- 3 celery stalks, cut into large chunks
- 2 zucchini, cut into large chunks
- 1/2 cup rice or small pasta
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- Lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, combine chicken, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, skim any foam, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
2. Remove chicken from the pot and set aside to cool slightly. Strain the broth, discarding onion and garlic. Return broth to the pot.
3. Shred the chicken meat from the bones and discard bones. Add carrots, celery, and rice/pasta to the broth. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice/pasta and vegetables are tender.
4. Add zucchini and shredded chicken back to the pot. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes. Stir in fresh cilantro. Adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot with lime wedges.

name: Soup, hot and sour
description:
A classic Chinese soup known for its tantalizing balance of spicy and tangy flavors, typically featuring shredded pork, tofu, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots in a thickened broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth
- 4 oz pork loin or chicken breast, thinly sliced or shredded
- 4 oz firm tofu, diced
- 1/2 cup dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
- 1/4 cup bamboo shoots, shredded
- 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp chili garlic sauce (or more to taste)
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1/2 tsp white pepper
- 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water (slurry)
- 1 egg, beaten
- 2 green onions, sliced for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, bring broth to a simmer. Add pork/chicken, tofu, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots. Cook for 5 minutes.
2. Stir in rice vinegar, soy sauce, chili garlic sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper. Bring back to a simmer.
3. Slowly whisk in the cornstarch slurry, stirring constantly until the soup thickens.
4. Slowly pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring gently to create egg ribbons. Cook for 1 minute.
5. Remove from heat. Taste and adjust seasoning (more vinegar for sour, more chili for hot). Serve hot, garnished with sliced green onions.

name: Soup, cream of chicken
description:
A rich and creamy soup, often used as a base for casseroles, featuring tender chicken pieces in a thick, savory cream-based broth, offering comforting flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 4 cups chicken broth
- 1 cup milk or half-and-half
- 1 cup cooked chicken, shredded or diced
- 1/2 tsp onion powder
- 1/4 tsp garlic powder
- Salt and white pepper to taste
- Optional: 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
2. Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until thickened.
3. Slowly whisk in milk or half-and-half. Add cooked chicken, onion powder, and garlic powder.
4. Continue to simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and flavors meld.
5. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Stir in parsley if desired. Serve hot.

name: Soup, Manhattan clam chowder
description:
A vibrant, tomato-based clam chowder, distinct from its creamy New England counterpart, featuring tender clams, diced vegetables, and herbs in a savory, clear broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 4 cups clam juice or vegetable broth
- 2 (6.5 oz) cans chopped clams, drained (reserve liquid)
- 1 cup diced potatoes
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, celery, and carrots; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
2. Stir in crushed tomatoes, clam juice/broth, reserved clam liquid, diced potatoes, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
3. Stir in drained chopped clams and cook for another 2-3 minutes to heat through. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in fresh parsley before serving.

name: Soup, New England clam chowder
description:
A rich and creamy American classic, featuring tender clams, diced potatoes, and often salt pork or bacon, all simmered in a thick, milk or cream-based broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 slices bacon or 2 oz salt pork, diced
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 4 cups clam juice or fish stock
- 2 cups diced potatoes
- 2 (6.5 oz) cans chopped clams, drained (reserve liquid)
- 2 cups half-and-half or whole milk
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and white pepper to taste
- Optional: fresh parsley for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a large pot or Dutch oven, cook bacon or salt pork over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon/pork with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
2. Add onion and celery to the pot; cook until softened, about 7 minutes. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
3. Gradually whisk in clam juice/fish stock until smooth. Add diced potatoes and thyme. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
4. Stir in half-and-half/milk and drained chopped clams (and reserved liquid if desired). Heat gently, but do not boil. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with crispy bacon/pork and fresh parsley.

name: Soup, bisque
description:
A rich and creamy French-style soup, traditionally made from puréed shellfish (like lobster or crab), but also prepared with vegetables, characterized by its smooth texture and intense flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp butter
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 1 carrot, finely diced
- 1 celery stalk, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 4 cups seafood stock (or vegetable broth)
- 1 cup heavy cream
- 1/2 cup dry white wine (optional)
- 1/2 lb cooked shrimp or crab meat, roughly chopped
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and white pepper to taste
- Fresh chives or parsley for garnish

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add onion, carrot, and celery; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
2. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Gradually whisk in seafood stock (and white wine if using) until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until slightly thickened.
3. Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream, cooked shrimp/crab, and cayenne pepper (if using). Heat gently, but do not boil.
4. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. For an extra smooth bisque, you can carefully purée a portion of the soup with an immersion blender or in batches in a regular blender, then return to the pot. Serve hot, garnished with fresh chives or parsley.

name: Lobster gumbo
description:
A luxurious take on the classic Louisiana stew, featuring succulent lobster meat, often with other seafood, simmered in a rich, dark roux-based broth with the 'holy trinity' of vegetables.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup vegetable oil
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 cups seafood stock
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes (optional)
- 1 lb cooked lobster meat, cut into chunks
- 1/2 lb cooked shrimp (optional)
- 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Cooked white rice for serving
- Fresh parsley or green onions for garnish

Instructions:
1. To make the roux: In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, heat oil over medium heat. Gradually whisk in flour. Cook, stirring constantly, for 20-30 minutes until the roux reaches a dark chocolate color (be careful not to burn).
2. Add onion, celery, and bell pepper to the roux; cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Slowly whisk in seafood stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Add diced tomatoes (if using), cayenne pepper, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. Stir in cooked lobster meat and shrimp (if using). Cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until seafood is heated through. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot over cooked white rice, garnished with fresh parsley or green onions.

name: Shrimp gumbo
description:
A quintessential Louisiana comfort food, featuring plump shrimp, often with sausage, simmered in a rich, dark roux-based broth with the 'holy trinity' of vegetables and served over rice.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup vegetable oil
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 8 cups seafood stock
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes (optional)
- 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/2 lb andouille sausage, sliced (optional)
- 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Cooked white rice for serving
- Fresh parsley or green onions for garnish

Instructions:
1. To make the roux: In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, heat oil over medium heat. Gradually whisk in flour. Cook, stirring constantly, for 20-30 minutes until the roux reaches a dark chocolate color (be careful not to burn). If using sausage, add it to the roux and cook until browned, then remove and set aside.
2. Add onion, celery, and bell pepper to the roux; cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Slowly whisk in seafood stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Add diced tomatoes (if using), cayenne pepper, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. Add raw shrimp (and cooked sausage if using). Cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until shrimp are pink and cooked through. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot over cooked white rice, garnished with fresh parsley or green onions.

name: Soup, fish or shrimp
description:
A light and flavorful seafood soup, featuring tender pieces of fish or succulent shrimp, often with vegetables, simmered in a delicate, aromatic broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 6 cups fish stock or vegetable broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes (optional)
- 1/2 lb firm white fish (e.g., cod, snapper), cut into 1-inch pieces, or 1/2 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Lemon wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 7 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
2. Pour in fish stock/broth and diced tomatoes (if using). Add oregano. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
3. Add fish or shrimp to the simmering soup. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until fish is opaque and flaky, or shrimp are pink and cooked through.
4. Stir in fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot with lemon wedges.

name: Gravy, poultry
description:
A rich and savory sauce, typically made from the drippings of roasted poultry, thickened with flour or cornstarch, and seasoned to complement chicken or turkey dishes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp poultry drippings (from roasted chicken/turkey) or butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups chicken broth
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Optional: 1/4 tsp poultry seasoning

Instructions:
1. If using drippings, skim excess fat, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the roasting pan or a saucepan. If using butter, melt it in a saucepan over medium heat.
2. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
3. Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency.
4. Season with salt, pepper, and poultry seasoning (if using) to taste. Serve hot.

name: Gravy, beef
description:
A classic, rich, and savory sauce, typically made from the drippings of roasted beef, thickened and seasoned to perfectly accompany roasts, mashed potatoes, or Yorkshire pudding.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp beef drippings (from roasted beef) or butter
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups beef broth
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Optional: 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce

Instructions:
1. If using drippings, skim excess fat, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the roasting pan or a saucepan. If using butter, melt it in a saucepan over medium heat.
2. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
3. Gradually whisk in beef broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency.
4. Stir in Worcestershire sauce if using. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Gravy, beef, fat free
description:
A lighter version of classic beef gravy, made without added fat, offering a savory and flavorful accompaniment to meals while being mindful of dietary needs.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 8 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups fat-free beef broth
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp cold water
- 1/2 tsp onion powder
- 1/4 tsp garlic powder
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Optional: 1/2 tsp browning sauce for color

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together cornstarch and cold water to create a slurry.
2. In a saucepan, bring fat-free beef broth to a simmer over medium heat. Stir in onion powder and garlic powder.
3. Gradually whisk the cornstarch slurry into the simmering broth. Continue to whisk until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency.
4. Stir in browning sauce if desired for a richer color. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Gravy, poultry, fat free
description:
A lighter, fat-free version of poultry gravy, offering a savory and flavorful accompaniment to chicken or turkey dishes without the added richness of fat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 8 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups fat-free chicken broth
- 2 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp cold water
- 1/2 tsp poultry seasoning
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together cornstarch and cold water to create a slurry.
2. In a saucepan, bring fat-free chicken broth to a simmer over medium heat. Stir in poultry seasoning.
3. Gradually whisk the cornstarch slurry into the simmering broth. Continue to whisk until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency.
4. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Gravy, made with soy sauce
description:
A savory and umami-rich gravy, incorporating soy sauce for a distinct Asian-inspired flavor profile, perfect for complementing various meat or vegetable dishes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp butter or oil
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups vegetable or chicken broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger (optional)
- 1/2 tsp sesame oil (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, melt butter or heat oil over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
2. Gradually whisk in broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens.
3. Stir in soy sauce, grated ginger (if using), and sesame oil (if using). Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Gravy, NFS
description:
A versatile, savory sauce, typically thickened and seasoned, used to enhance the flavor and moisture of various dishes, from roasted meats to mashed potatoes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp butter or oil
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 2 cups broth (chicken, beef, or vegetable)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a saucepan, melt butter or heat oil over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
2. Gradually whisk in broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency.
3. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Oyster sauce
description: A rich, savory, and slightly sweet condiment widely used in Asian cuisine, made from oyster extracts, soy sauce, and often thickened, adding a distinct umami depth to dishes.

name: Mole sauce
description: A complex and iconic Mexican sauce, known for its deep, rich flavor profile derived from a blend of chilies, spices, nuts, seeds, and often a hint of chocolate, typically served over poultry or enchiladas.

name: Egg, whole, raw
description: A fresh, uncooked whole egg, consisting of a yolk and albumen (egg white) encased in a shell, a fundamental ingredient in countless culinary applications.

name: Egg, whole, cooked, NS as to cooking method
description: A whole egg that has been prepared through heat, transforming its liquid contents into a solid form, ready for consumption in various dishes.

name: Egg, whole, boiled or poached
description: A whole egg gently cooked in hot water, resulting in a firm white and a yolk that can range from runny to fully set, depending on cooking time.

name: Egg, whole, fried, NS as to fat
description: A whole egg cooked in a pan with heat, resulting in a crispy edge and a set white, with the yolk remaining soft or firm, depending on preference.

name: Egg, whole, fried no added fat
description: A whole egg cooked in a non-stick pan without any added oil or butter, resulting in a lighter, less crispy fried egg.

name: Egg, whole, fried with margarine
description: A whole egg cooked in a pan with margarine, yielding a fried egg with a slightly different flavor and texture compared to butter or oil.

name: Egg, whole, fried with oil
description: A whole egg cooked in a pan with cooking oil, resulting in a classic fried egg with a crisp edge and a tender interior.

name: Egg, whole, fried with butter
description: A whole egg cooked in a pan with butter, imparting a rich, golden flavor and a delicate crispness to the edges of the fried egg.

name: Egg, whole, fried with animal fat or meat drippings
description: A whole egg fried in rendered animal fat or savory meat drippings, infusing it with a deep, robust flavor and a wonderfully crispy texture.

name: Egg, whole, pickled
description:
Hard-boiled eggs preserved in a vinegar-based brine, often with spices, resulting in a tangy and firm snack or condiment.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 eggs
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus 3-5 days chilling)

Ingredients:
- 12 hard-boiled eggs, peeled
- 2 cups white vinegar
- 1 cup water
- 1 tbsp pickling spice
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tsp sugar
- Optional: 1/2 onion, sliced, 1 clove garlic, smashed

Instructions:
1. Place peeled hard-boiled eggs into a clean, heat-proof jar.
2. In a saucepan, combine vinegar, water, pickling spice, salt, sugar, onion (if using), and garlic (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
3. Carefully pour the hot brine over the eggs in the jar, ensuring they are fully submerged.
4. Seal the jar and let it cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 3-5 days before eating to allow flavors to develop. Pickled eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for several weeks.

name: Egg, creamed
description:
A comforting classic, creamed eggs feature chopped hard-boiled eggs gently folded into a rich, savory cream sauce, often served over toast.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 hard-boiled eggs, chopped
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 1.5 cups milk
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Pinch of nutmeg (optional)

Instructions:
1. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
2. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, creating a roux.
3. Gradually whisk in milk, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens and is smooth.
4. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg if desired.
5. Gently fold in the chopped hard-boiled eggs.
6. Serve warm over toast or biscuits.

name: Egg, Benedict
description:
An iconic brunch dish, Eggs Benedict features perfectly poached eggs, Canadian bacon, and a luscious hollandaise sauce, all atop a toasted English muffin.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 English muffins, split and toasted
- 4 slices Canadian bacon, lightly fried
- 4 large eggs
- For Hollandaise Sauce:
- 3 egg yolks
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- Pinch of salt
- Pinch of cayenne pepper

Instructions:
1. Prepare Hollandaise: Whisk egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie) until light and frothy. Slowly drizzle in melted butter while continuously whisking until the sauce thickens. Season with salt and cayenne. Keep warm.
2. Poach Eggs: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Carefully crack each egg into a small bowl, then gently slide into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still runny. Remove with a slotted spoon.
3. Assemble: Place toasted English muffin halves on plates. Top each half with a slice of Canadian bacon, then a poached egg. Spoon generous amounts of hollandaise sauce over each egg. Serve immediately.

name: Egg, deviled
description:
A beloved party appetizer, deviled eggs are hard-boiled eggs halved and filled with a creamy, tangy mixture of mashed yolks, mayonnaise, mustard, and seasonings.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 halves
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 6 hard-boiled eggs, peeled
- 1/4 cup mayonnaise
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- 1 teaspoon white vinegar (or pickle juice)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Paprika for garnish

Instructions:
1. Halve the hard-boiled eggs lengthwise and carefully scoop out the yolks into a small bowl.
2. Mash the yolks with a fork until smooth.
3. Add mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, vinegar, salt, and pepper to the mashed yolks. Mix well until creamy and thoroughly combined.
4. Spoon or pipe the yolk mixture back into the egg white halves.
5. Garnish with a sprinkle of paprika before serving. Chill until ready to serve.

name: Huevos rancheros
description:
A vibrant Mexican breakfast, Huevos Rancheros features fried eggs served on warm tortillas, smothered in a zesty salsa, often with beans and avocado.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 corn tortillas
- 4 large eggs
- 1 cup salsa ranchera (store-bought or homemade)
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
- 1/4 cup crumbled cotija cheese or shredded cheddar (optional)
- Chopped cilantro for garnish (optional)
- Sliced avocado for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Lightly fry each tortilla for about 30 seconds per side until warmed and slightly pliable. Set aside.
2. In the same skillet, fry the eggs to your desired doneness (sunny-side up is traditional).
3. Warm the salsa in a small saucepan.
4. Assemble: Place two tortillas on each plate. Top each tortilla with a fried egg. Spoon warm salsa generously over the eggs.
5. Garnish with crumbled cheese, cilantro, and avocado if desired. Serve immediately.

name: Egg casserole with bread, cheese, milk and meat
description:
A hearty and comforting breakfast casserole, layering bread, savory meat, rich cheese, and a custardy egg-milk mixture, baked until golden and bubbly.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus chilling time)

Ingredients:
- 6 slices bread, cubed
- 1 cup cooked breakfast sausage or ham, crumbled/diced
- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 6 large eggs
- 2 cups milk
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- Pinch of dry mustard (optional)

Instructions:
1. Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. Spread the cubed bread evenly in the bottom of the dish. Sprinkle the cooked meat and shredded cheese over the bread.
3. In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and dry mustard (if using). Pour this mixture evenly over the bread, meat, and cheese.
4. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight for best results.
5. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
6. Bake uncovered for 45-55 minutes, or until the casserole is set and golden brown on top. Let stand for a few minutes before serving.

name: Egg foo yung, NFS
description:
A classic Chinese-American dish, Egg Foo Yung features fluffy egg omelets packed with various ingredients, pan-fried until golden, and served with a savory gravy.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 large eggs, beaten
- 1/2 cup chopped cooked protein (e.g., chicken, pork, shrimp)
- 1/4 cup chopped bean sprouts
- 1/4 cup chopped green onions
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch
- Vegetable oil for frying
- For Gravy:
- 1 cup chicken broth
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine beaten eggs, cooked protein, bean sprouts, green onions, and 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Mix well.
2. Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
3. Pour about 1/4 cup of the egg mixture per patty into the hot oil, flattening slightly. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove and drain on paper towels. Keep warm.
4. Prepare Gravy: In a small saucepan, combine chicken broth, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Whisk in the cornstarch slurry and cook, stirring, until thickened.
5. Serve egg foo yung patties hot, topped with gravy.

name: Egg omelet or scrambled egg, NS as to fat
description:
A versatile breakfast staple, whether a fluffy omelet or creamy scrambled eggs, prepared simply and ready to be customized with your favorite additions.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 large eggs
- 1 tablespoon milk or water (optional)
- 1 teaspoon cooking fat (butter, oil, or margarine)
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Crack eggs into a bowl. Add milk or water (if using), salt, and pepper. Whisk until yolks and whites are fully combined and slightly frothy.
2. Heat cooking fat in a non-stick skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
3. For scrambled eggs: Pour egg mixture into the skillet. Let sit for 30 seconds, then gently push cooked egg from the edges to the center, allowing uncooked egg to flow underneath. Continue stirring and folding until eggs are cooked to your desired consistency.
4. For an omelet: Pour egg mixture into the skillet. Let sit undisturbed for 1-2 minutes until edges are set but the top is still slightly wet. Gently fold one side over the other. Cook for another minute, then slide onto a plate.

name: Soup, egg drop
description:
A delicate and comforting Chinese soup, featuring wispy ribbons of cooked egg swirling in a clear, savory broth, often enhanced with subtle seasonings and green onions.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 cups chicken broth
- 2 large eggs
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp water
- 1 tsp soy sauce
- 1/2 tsp sesame oil
- 2 green onions, sliced (for garnish)
- Salt and white pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk eggs lightly. In another small bowl, dissolve cornstarch in water to create a slurry.

3. Slowly pour the cornstarch slurry into the simmering broth, stirring constantly, until the soup slightly thickens.
4. While stirring the soup in a circular motion, slowly drizzle the whisked eggs into the broth. The eggs will cook into delicate ribbons.
5. Remove from heat immediately. Ladle into bowls and garnish with sliced green onions.
6. Serve hot.

A complete and wholesome egg white dish, packed with protein from meat, flavor from cheese, and nutrients from vegetables, prepared as an omelet, scrambled, or fried.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 10-15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 large egg whites
- 1 tbsp milk or water (optional)
- 1/4 cup shredded cheese
- 1/4 cup cooked, diced lean meat
- 1/4 cup diced vegetables (e.g., bell peppers, spinach, mushrooms, onions)
- 1 tsp cooking oil or cooking spray
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk egg whites with milk or water, salt, and pepper until slightly frothy.
2. Heat cooking oil or spray a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add diced vegetables and cook until tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes. Add cooked meat and heat through.
3. Pour egg white mixture into the skillet. If making an omelet, let it set for 1-2 minutes, then sprinkle cheese, meat, and vegetables over one half, fold the other half over, and cook until cheese is melted and eggs are set. If making scrambled egg whites, stir gently with a spatula until cooked to desired consistency, then mix in cheese, meat, and vegetables.
4. Serve immediately.

name: Meringues
description:
Delicate and airy confections, meringues are made from whipped egg whites and sugar, baked until crisp and light, offering a sweet, melt-in-your-mouth experience.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12-18 small meringues
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 3 large egg whites, at room temperature
- 1/4 tsp cream of tartar (optional, helps stabilize)
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 225°F (107°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a clean, dry bowl, beat egg whites with an electric mixer on medium speed until foamy. Add cream of tartar (if using) and continue beating.
3. Gradually add granulated sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, while continuing to beat on high speed. Beat until stiff, glossy peaks form and the sugar is fully dissolved (rub a small amount between your fingers; it should feel smooth). Beat in vanilla extract (if using).
4. Spoon or pipe meringue onto the prepared baking sheet.
5. Bake for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until meringues are firm and dry. Turn off the oven and let them cool completely inside the oven with the door ajar for at least 30 minutes, or until completely cool and crisp.
6. Store in an airtight container.

- 4-6 cups water or broth
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil or bacon fat
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: bay leaf, herbs

Instructions:
1. Soak dried beans overnight in plenty of water, or quick soak by boiling for 10 minutes, then letting sit for 1 hour.
2. Drain and rinse the soaked beans. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or bacon fat over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Add the drained beans, water or broth, and bay leaf (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beans are tender. Add more liquid if needed.
4. Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper. Mash a small portion of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the liquid if desired.
5. Serve hot.
