4. Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve hot, garnished with cilantro if desired.

name: Black beans, from canned, fat added
description:
A quick and flavorful dish made from canned black beans, enhanced with added fat and aromatics for a rich and satisfying side or base for a meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10-15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 tbsp olive oil or bacon fat
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil or bacon fat in a skillet or saucepan over medium heat.
2. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in the rinsed and drained canned black beans. Add a splash of water or broth if needed to prevent sticking.
4. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are heated through. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Serve hot, garnished with cilantro if desired.

name: Black beans, from canned, no added fat
description:
A quick and healthy dish made from canned black beans, prepared without any added fat, offering a simple and nutritious side or base for a meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10-15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Cooking spray or a splash of vegetable broth
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: fresh cilantro

Instructions:
1. Spray a non-stick skillet or saucepan with cooking spray (or use a splash of broth) and heat over medium heat.
2. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in the rinsed and drained canned black beans. Add a small amount of water or broth if needed to prevent sticking.
4. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are heated through. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Serve hot, garnished with cilantro if desired.

name: Black beans, from canned, reduced sodium
description:
A healthier option for a quick meal, these canned black beans are prepared with reduced sodium, offering a mild and earthy base for various dishes while managing salt intake.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10-15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15-ounce) can reduced-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1 tsp olive oil or cooking spray
- Pepper to taste
- Optional: fresh cilantro, a pinch of salt if desired

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil or spray a non-stick skillet or saucepan with cooking spray over medium heat.
2. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in the rinsed and drained reduced-sodium black beans. Add a splash of water or broth if needed to prevent sticking.
4. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are heated through. Season with pepper and optional cilantro. Taste and add a pinch of salt only if necessary.
5. Serve hot.

name: Black beans, from fast food / restaurant
description: A popular side dish or ingredient in various fast food or restaurant meals, featuring black beans prepared for quick service, often seasoned with a distinct flavor profile.

name: Black beans with meat
description:
A hearty and flavorful dish, combining tender black beans with savory meat, creating a robust and satisfying meal, often a staple in Latin American cuisine.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 20-25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained (or 1.5 cups cooked dried black beans)
- 1/2 lb cooked meat (e.g., ground beef, shredded pork, diced chicken)
- 1/2 cup diced onion
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup diced bell pepper
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp cumin
- 1/2 tsp oregano
- 1/2 cup chicken or vegetable broth
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: fresh cilantro, lime wedges for serving

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
2. Add the cooked meat and stir to combine, heating through if necessary.
3. Stir in the black beans and broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and liquid to reduce slightly.
4. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve hot, garnished with cilantro and lime wedges if desired.

name: Fava beans, cooked
description:
Tender and earthy, cooked fava beans offer a distinct, slightly nutty flavor and creamy texture, often enjoyed as a side dish, in salads, or as part of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15-20 minutes (for fresh, plus shelling)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb fresh fava beans in pods (yields about 1 cup shelled beans)
- Water for boiling
- Salt to taste
- Optional: 1 tbsp olive oil, a squeeze of lemon juice

Instructions:
1. Shell the fava beans from their pods. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
2. Add the shelled fava beans to the boiling water and cook for 2-5 minutes, depending on size, until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking and preserve color.
3. Once cooled, peel the outer membrane from each fava bean (this step is optional but recommended for a more tender texture, especially for larger beans).
4. Season with salt, a drizzle of olive oil, and a squeeze of lemon juice if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.
5. Alternatively, if using dried fava beans, soak overnight, then boil for 45-60 minutes until tender, then peel.

name: Lima beans, NFS
description: A distinctive legume known for its flat, kidney-shaped appearance and buttery, slightly starchy texture, often used in succotash, stews, or as a simple side dish.

name: Lima beans, from dried
description:
A comforting and creamy dish made from dried lima beans, slow-cooked until tender and buttery, offering a wholesome and satisfying side or base for a meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried lima beans, rinsed and sorted
- 4-6 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil or butter (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: bay leaf, fresh thyme

Instructions:
1. Soak dried lima beans overnight in plenty of water, or quick soak by boiling for 10 minutes, then letting sit for 1 hour.
2. Drain and rinse the soaked beans. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or butter (if using) over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Add the drained beans, water or broth, and bay leaf/thyme (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1-1.5 hours, or until beans are tender. Add more liquid if needed.
4. Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

name: Pink beans, cooked
description:
Tender and subtly sweet, cooked pink beans offer a delicate flavor and creamy texture, making them a versatile addition to soups, stews, and rice dishes, particularly in Caribbean and Latin American cuisines.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried pink beans, rinsed and sorted
- 4-6 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: bay leaf, 1/2 tsp cumin

Instructions:
1. Soak dried pink beans overnight in plenty of water, or quick soak by boiling for 10 minutes, then letting sit for 1 hour.
2. Drain and rinse the soaked beans. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil (if using) over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cumin (if using) and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Add the drained beans, water or broth, and bay leaf (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beans are tender. Add more liquid if needed.
4. Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

name: Pinto beans, NFS
description: A popular and versatile legume, pinto beans are known for their mottled pink and brown appearance, creamy texture, and earthy flavor, a staple in Mexican and Southwestern American cuisine.

name: Pinto beans, from dried, fat added
description:
A rich and comforting dish made from dried pinto beans, slow-cooked until tender and infused with savory flavors from added fat, perfect for refried beans, burritos, or as a hearty side.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried pinto beans, rinsed and sorted
- 4-6 cups water or chicken broth
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp olive oil or bacon fat
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: bay leaf, chili powder

Instructions:
1. Soak dried pinto beans overnight in plenty of water, or quick soak by boiling for 10 minutes, then letting sit for 1 hour.
2. Drain and rinse the soaked beans. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or bacon fat over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cumin/chili powder (if using) and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Add the drained beans, water or broth, and bay leaf (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beans are tender. Add more liquid if needed.
4. Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

name: Pinto beans, from dried, no added fat
description:
A wholesome and flavorful dish made from dried pinto beans, slow-cooked until tender and creamy without any added fat, perfect for a healthy and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried pinto beans, rinsed and sorted
- 4-6 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1/4 cup diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional: bay leaf, chili powder

Instructions:
1. Soak dried pinto beans overnight in plenty of water, or quick soak by boiling for 10 minutes, then letting sit for 1 hour.
2. Drain and rinse the soaked beans. In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine the drained beans, water or vegetable broth, diced onion, minced garlic, cumin/chili powder (if using), and bay leaf (if using).
3. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beans are tender. Add more liquid if needed.
4. Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

name: Pinto beans, from canned, fat added
description: Convenient and hearty, these canned pinto beans are a staple, often seasoned with a touch of added fat for extra richness and flavor, perfect for quick meals or as a side.

name: Pinto beans, from canned, no added fat
description: A wholesome and convenient pantry essential, these canned pinto beans offer a neutral base for countless dishes, free from added fats for a lighter touch.

name: Pinto beans, from canned, reduced sodium
description: Health-conscious and versatile, these canned pinto beans provide the same creamy texture and earthy flavor with less sodium, making them ideal for a balanced diet.

name: Pinto beans, from fast food / restaurant
description: Often a savory side dish at your favorite eatery, these pinto beans are typically slow-cooked and seasoned, offering a comforting and flavorful accompaniment to various meals.

name: Pinto beans with meat
description:
A robust and satisfying dish, pinto beans simmered with savory meat, often pork or bacon, create a hearty and flavorful meal, perfect for a comforting dinner.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb dried pinto beans, rinsed
- 6 cups water or chicken broth
- 1/2 lb smoked ham hock or bacon, diced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp cumin
- 1/2 tsp chili powder
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Soak pinto beans overnight or quick soak (boil for 1 minute, let stand 1 hour). Drain.
2. In a large pot, combine beans, water/broth, ham hock/bacon, onion, garlic, cumin, and chili powder.
3. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until beans are tender.
4. Remove ham hock/bacon if desired, shred meat and return to pot. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Kidney beans, NFS
description: These large, kidney-shaped beans boast a firm texture and mild flavor, making them a versatile ingredient in chilis, salads, and stews, absorbing flavors beautifully.

name: Kidney beans, from dried, fat added
description: Dried kidney beans, prepared with added fat, offer a rich and satisfying texture, perfect for hearty dishes where their robust flavor can truly shine.

name: Kidney beans, from dried, no added fat
description: A foundational ingredient for many cuisines, these dried kidney beans, cooked without added fat, provide a wholesome and versatile base for chilis, salads, and vegetarian meals.

name: Kidney beans, from canned, fat added
description: Convenient and ready-to-use, these canned kidney beans with added fat offer a richer flavor and smoother texture, ideal for quick additions to soups, stews, and casseroles.

name: Kidney beans, from canned, no added fat
description: A pantry staple for quick and healthy meals, these canned kidney beans are ready to use, offering a firm texture and mild flavor without any added fat.

name: Kidney beans, from canned, reduced sodium
description: For health-conscious cooks, these canned kidney beans offer the same great taste and texture with less sodium, making them a smart choice for a balanced diet.

name: Kidney beans, from fast food / restaurant
description: Often found in chilis or as a side dish, these restaurant-prepared kidney beans are typically seasoned and cooked to a tender perfection, offering a comforting and familiar taste.

name: Kidney beans with meat
description:
A hearty and flavorful combination, kidney beans simmered with savory meat, often beef or pork, create a satisfying and protein-rich meal, perfect for a chilly evening.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground beef or pork
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 (15 oz) cans kidney beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a large pot or Dutch oven, brown ground meat over medium heat. Drain excess fat.
2. Add onion and garlic; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
3. Stir in kidney beans, diced tomatoes, beef broth, chili powder, and cumin.
4. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 20-30 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
5. Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Peruvian beans, from dried
description: Also known as Mayocoba or Canary beans, these dried Peruvian beans cook up creamy and tender with a mild, buttery flavor, making them excellent for refried beans or simple side dishes.

name: Soybeans, cooked
description: Nutrient-dense and versatile, cooked soybeans offer a firm texture and mild, nutty flavor, perfect for adding protein to salads, stir-fries, or enjoying as a simple snack.

name: Mung beans, cooked
description: Small, green, and incredibly versatile, cooked mung beans have a soft texture and slightly sweet, nutty flavor, often used in Asian cuisine for soups, curries, and sprouted salads.

name: Baked beans
description:
A classic comfort food, baked beans are slow-cooked to perfection in a rich, savory-sweet sauce, often featuring molasses, brown sugar, and sometimes pork, creating a deeply satisfying side dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb dried navy beans, rinsed
- 6 cups water
- 1/2 cup molasses
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1/4 cup ketchup
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 4 oz salt pork or bacon, diced
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Soak navy beans overnight. Drain and rinse.
2. Place beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 30-45 minutes until slightly tender but not mushy. Drain, reserving 1 cup of cooking liquid.
3. Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
4. In an oven-safe pot or Dutch oven, combine beans, molasses, brown sugar, ketchup, mustard, and onion. Stir in reserved cooking liquid.
5. Bury the diced salt pork or bacon into the beans.
6. Cover and bake for 4-6 hours, stirring occasionally, until beans are very tender and sauce has thickened. Add more water if needed. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Baked beans, vegetarian
description:
A wholesome twist on a classic, vegetarian baked beans offer the same sweet and savory depth without meat, relying on a rich sauce of molasses, brown sugar, and spices for their comforting flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb dried navy beans, rinsed
- 6 cups water
- 1/2 cup molasses
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1/4 cup ketchup
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 1 tsp smoked paprika (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Soak navy beans overnight. Drain and rinse.
2. Place beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 30-45 minutes until slightly tender but not mushy. Drain, reserving 1 cup of cooking liquid.
3. Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
4. In an oven-safe pot or Dutch oven, combine beans, molasses, brown sugar, ketchup, mustard, onion, and smoked paprika. Stir in reserved cooking liquid.
5. Cover and bake for 4-6 hours, stirring occasionally, until beans are very tender and sauce has thickened. Add more water if needed. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Baked beans from fast food / restaurant
description: A popular side dish at many eateries, these baked beans are typically slow-cooked in a sweet and tangy sauce, offering a convenient and satisfying accompaniment to your meal.

name: Beans and tomatoes, no added fat
description:
A simple and healthy combination, tender beans simmered with ripe tomatoes create a light yet flavorful dish, perfect as a side or a base for a quick meal, without any added fat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15 oz) can cannellini or great northern beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine chopped onion and a splash of water or vegetable broth. Cook over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
2. Add minced garlic and oregano; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Stir in rinsed beans and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
4. Reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Beans and tomatoes, fat added
description:
A comforting and flavorful dish, tender beans simmered with ripe tomatoes and a touch of added fat (like olive oil or bacon drippings) create a richer, more satisfying side or light meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil or bacon fat
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 (15 oz) can cannellini or great northern beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil or bacon fat in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
2. Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
3. Add minced garlic and oregano; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in rinsed beans and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
5. Reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
6. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Black bean salad
description:
A vibrant and refreshing dish, black bean salad combines tender black beans with colorful vegetables, often corn, bell peppers, and cilantro, all tossed in a zesty lime vinaigrette for a burst of fresh flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 (15 oz) cans black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 cup corn (fresh, frozen, or canned)
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 red onion, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp lime juice
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine black beans, corn, red bell pepper, red onion, and cilantro.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, cumin, salt, and pepper.
3. Pour the dressing over the bean mixture and toss gently to combine.
4. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.

name: Refried beans
description:
A beloved Mexican staple, refried beans are creamy, savory, and rich, made by mashing cooked beans (often pinto or black) with seasonings and fat, perfect as a side or filling.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp lard or vegetable oil
- 1/2 onion, finely chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 (15 oz) cans pinto beans, drained (reserve liquid)
- 1/2 cup reserved bean liquid or chicken broth
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
2. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
3. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add drained pinto beans and cumin. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring.
5. Add reserved bean liquid or broth. Bring to a simmer.
6. Using a potato masher or fork, mash the beans to your desired consistency. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until heated through and thickened.
7. Season with salt to taste.

name: Refried beans, from fast food / restaurant
description: A popular side dish at Mexican restaurants, these creamy and savory refried beans are typically made from pinto beans, seasoned and mashed to perfection, offering a comforting accompaniment.

name: Refried beans with meat
description:
Elevating the classic, refried beans with meat incorporate savory ground beef, chorizo, or bacon, adding a rich, hearty dimension to this creamy Mexican staple.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp lard or vegetable oil
- 1/2 lb ground beef or chorizo
- 1/2 onion, finely chopped
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 (15 oz) cans pinto beans, drained (reserve liquid)
- 1/2 cup reserved bean liquid or chicken broth
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add ground beef or chorizo and cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
2. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
3. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in drained pinto beans and cumin. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
5. Add reserved bean liquid or broth. Bring to a simmer.
6. Using a potato masher or fork, mash the beans to your desired consistency, incorporating the meat. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until heated through and thickened.
7. Season with salt to taste.

name: Refried beans, from canned, reduced sodium
description: A convenient and health-conscious option, these canned refried beans offer the same creamy texture and savory flavor with less sodium, perfect for quick meals or dips.

name: Bean dip, made with refried beans
description:
A creamy and flavorful appetizer, bean dip made with refried beans is a crowd-pleaser, often seasoned with spices and cheese, perfect for scooping with tortilla chips.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (16 oz) can refried beans
- 1/2 cup sour cream or Greek yogurt
- 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 1/4 cup salsa
- 1/4 tsp cumin
- Pinch of chili powder (optional)
- Tortilla chips, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, combine refried beans, sour cream, shredded cheddar cheese, salsa, cumin, and chili powder (if using).
2. Stir until well combined.
3. Transfer to a serving dish. Serve immediately with tortilla chips, or cover and refrigerate for later. Can be warmed gently if desired.

name: Layer dip
description:
A festive and flavorful appetizer, layer dip is a vibrant stack of creamy, savory, and fresh ingredients like refried beans, guacamole, sour cream, salsa, cheese, and fresh veggies, perfect for sharing.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (16 oz) can refried beans
- 1 cup guacamole
- 1 cup sour cream, mixed with 1 packet taco seasoning
- 1 cup salsa
- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 1/2 cup chopped tomatoes
- 1/4 cup sliced black olives
- 2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
- Tortilla chips, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a large, clear serving dish (9x13 inch pan works well), spread the refried beans evenly as the first layer.
2. Carefully spread the guacamole over the beans.
3. Next, spread the seasoned sour cream over the guacamole.
4. Spoon the salsa evenly over the sour cream.
5. Sprinkle with shredded cheddar cheese, then chopped tomatoes, black olives, and cilantro.
6. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving with tortilla chips.

name: Hummus, plain
description:
A creamy and nutritious Middle Eastern dip, plain hummus is made from mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, and garlic, offering a smooth, earthy flavor perfect for dipping or spreading.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
- 1/4 cup tahini
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil (plus more for drizzling)
- 2-4 tbsp cold water
- Salt to taste
- Pinch of paprika (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a food processor, combine chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and salt.
2. Process until smooth, gradually adding cold water 1 tablespoon at a time until desired creamy consistency is reached.
3. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
4. Transfer to a serving bowl, drizzle with a little extra olive oil, and sprinkle with paprika before serving.

name: Hummus, flavored
description:
Taking the classic dip to new heights, flavored hummus infuses the creamy chickpea base with exciting additions like roasted red peppers, sun-dried tomatoes, or spicy jalapeños for a vibrant taste experience.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
- 1/4 cup tahini
- 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 2 tbsp olive oil (plus more for drizzling)
- 2-4 tbsp cold water
- Salt to taste
- 1/2 cup roasted red peppers (drained) OR 2 tbsp sun-dried tomatoes OR 1 jalapeño (seeded)
- Pinch of paprika (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a food processor, combine chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt, and your chosen flavoring ingredient (roasted red peppers, sun-dried tomatoes, or jalapeño).
2. Process until smooth, gradually adding cold water 1 tablespoon at a time until desired creamy consistency is reached.
3. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
4. Transfer to a serving bowl, drizzle with a little extra olive oil, and sprinkle with paprika before serving.

name: Black bean sauce
description:
A pungent and savory Chinese condiment, black bean sauce is made from fermented black soybeans, garlic, and sometimes ginger, offering a deep umami flavor perfect for stir-fries and marinades.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: Yields about 1 cup
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup fermented black beans, rinsed and roughly chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 2 tbsp water or chicken broth
- 1 tsp cornstarch (mixed with 1 tbsp water)

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, combine rinsed black beans, minced garlic, grated ginger, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and water/broth.
2. Heat a small saucepan or wok over medium heat. Add the black bean mixture and bring to a simmer.
3. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld.
4. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens to your desired consistency.
5. Remove from heat and use immediately in stir-fries or as a marinade.

name: Beans and franks
description:
A nostalgic and comforting American classic, beans and franks combines tender baked beans with sliced hot dogs or frankfurters, simmered in a savory-sweet sauce for a quick and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (28 oz) can baked beans (or homemade)
- 4-6 hot dogs, sliced into rounds
- 1/4 cup ketchup
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 1 tbsp yellow mustard
- 1/2 onion, chopped (optional)

Instructions:
1. If using onion, sauté it in a pot over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
2. Add sliced hot dogs and cook for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned.
3. Stir in baked beans, ketchup, brown sugar, and mustard.
4. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and flavors have melded.
5. Serve hot.

name: Pork and beans
description:
A classic American comfort food, pork and beans features tender navy beans simmered in a savory tomato-based sauce, often with small pieces of salt pork or bacon for a rich, smoky flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb dried navy beans, rinsed
- 6 cups water
- 4 oz salt pork or bacon, diced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 1 (15 oz) can tomato sauce
- 1/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tsp dry mustard
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Soak navy beans overnight. Drain and rinse.
2. Place beans in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 30-45 minutes until slightly tender but not mushy. Drain, reserving 1 cup of cooking liquid.
3. In a large pot or Dutch oven, cook diced salt pork or bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove pork/bacon and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
4. Add onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
5. Stir in beans, tomato sauce, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, dry mustard, and reserved bean liquid. Bring to a simmer.
6. Return cooked pork/bacon to the pot. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1-2 hours, or until beans are very tender and sauce has thickened. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Beans with meat, NS as to type
description:
A hearty and versatile dish, beans simmered with meat (type unspecified) offer a comforting and protein-rich meal, with flavors varying based on the specific beans and meat used.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 lb ground beef or turkey
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 (15 oz) cans mixed beans (e.g., kidney, pinto, black), rinsed and drained
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 cup beef or vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
3. Add onion and garlic; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
4. Stir in rinsed beans, diced tomatoes, broth, chili powder, and cumin.
5. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 20-30 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Falafel
description:
A popular Middle Eastern street food, falafel are crispy, deep-fried patties or balls made from ground chickpeas or fava beans, seasoned with herbs and spices, typically served in pita bread.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried chickpeas, soaked overnight
- 1/2 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Vegetable oil, for frying

Instructions:
1. Drain soaked chickpeas thoroughly. Do NOT cook them.
2. In a food processor, combine soaked chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander, baking soda, salt, and pepper.
3. Process until the mixture is finely ground but not a paste. It should hold together when pressed.
4. Form the mixture into small patties or balls (about 1.5 inches).
5. Heat about 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C).
6. Carefully fry falafel in batches for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through.
7. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve hot.

name: Bean cake
description:
A versatile dish found in various cuisines, bean cakes can range from savory patties made with mashed beans and spices to sweet desserts, offering a unique texture and flavor profile.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup chopped red onion
- 1/4 cup chopped bell pepper
- 1 egg
- 1 tbsp chili powder
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp olive oil, for frying

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, mash the black beans with a fork or potato masher until mostly smooth but still with some texture.
2. Stir in breadcrumbs, red onion, bell pepper, egg, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper until well combined.
3. Form the mixture into 4-6 patties.
4. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
5. Cook the bean cakes for 4-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and heated through.
6. Serve hot, perhaps with salsa or avocado.

name: Baked beans, reduced sodium
description: Enjoy the comforting taste of classic baked beans with a health-conscious twist; these reduced-sodium versions offer the same sweet and savory sauce with less salt, perfect for a balanced diet.

name: Chili, vegetarian
description:
A hearty and flavorful meatless stew, vegetarian chili is packed with beans, tomatoes, corn, and a medley of vegetables, seasoned with robust chili powder and spices for a comforting and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 1 (15 oz) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 cup corn (fresh or frozen)
- 2 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tbsp cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add onion and bell pepper; cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
3. Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans, corn, and vegetable broth.
5. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 30 minutes (longer for more flavor).
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Blackeyed peas, NFS
description: These distinctive cream-colored beans with a black 'eye' are a Southern culinary staple, known for their earthy flavor and creamy texture, often symbolizing good luck.

name: Blackeyed peas, from dried
description: Dried blackeyed peas, when cooked, yield a tender, earthy bean with a creamy texture, perfect for traditional Southern dishes or as a nutritious addition to salads and stews.

name: Chickpeas, NFS
description: Also known as garbanzo beans, chickpeas are versatile legumes with a nutty flavor and firm texture, a staple in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Indian cuisines.

name: Chickpeas, from dried, fat added
description: Dried chickpeas, cooked with added fat, offer a richer, more satisfying texture and flavor, ideal for hearty stews, curries, or as a base for flavorful dips.

name: Chickpeas, from dried, no added fat
description: A wholesome and versatile legume, dried chickpeas, cooked without added fat, provide a firm texture and nutty flavor, perfect for salads, stews, or homemade hummus.

name: Chickpeas, from canned, fat added
description: Convenient and ready-to-use, these canned chickpeas with added fat offer a slightly richer taste and smoother texture, perfect for quick additions to dishes or blending into dips.

name: Chickpeas, from canned, no added fat
description: A pantry essential, these canned chickpeas are ready to use, offering a firm texture and nutty flavor without any added fat, making them perfect for quick salads, curries, or hummus.

name: Chickpeas, from canned, reduced sodium
description: For health-conscious cooks, these canned chickpeas offer the same great taste and texture with less sodium, making them a smart choice for a balanced diet.

name: Split peas, from dried, no added fat
description: Dried split peas, cooked without added fat, break down beautifully into a creamy, comforting texture, forming the base for wholesome soups and stews with a mild, earthy flavor.

name: Split peas, from dried, fat added
description: Dried split peas, cooked with added fat, yield a richer, more satisfying texture and flavor, perfect for hearty, comforting soups and stews.

name: Wasabi peas
description: A spicy and crunchy snack, wasabi peas are dried green peas coated in a fiery wasabi seasoning, offering an intense kick and satisfying crispness.

name: Lentils, NFS
description: These small, lens-shaped legumes are celebrated for their earthy flavor, quick cooking time, and versatility, forming the backbone of countless soups, stews, and salads worldwide.

name: Lentils, from dried, fat added
description: Dried lentils, cooked with added fat, absorb flavors beautifully, resulting in a richer, more satisfying texture and taste, perfect for hearty stews or side dishes.

name: Lentils, from dried, no added fat
description: A nutritious and versatile legume, dried lentils, cooked without added fat, offer an earthy flavor and tender texture, ideal for wholesome soups, salads, and vegetarian dishes.

name: Lentils, from canned
description: Convenient and ready-to-use, canned lentils offer a quick solution for adding protein and fiber to meals, with a tender texture and mild, earthy flavor.

name: Dal
description:
A staple of Indian cuisine, Dal refers to a variety of dried, split pulses (like lentils, peas, or beans) cooked into a thick, flavorful stew or soup, often seasoned with aromatic spices.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup red lentils (masoor dal), rinsed
- 3 cups water or vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp ghee or oil
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- 1 tsp cumin seeds
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- 1/2 tsp garam masala
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1 tomato, diced
- Salt to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a medium pot, combine rinsed lentils and water/broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until lentils are tender and mushy.
2. While lentils cook, heat ghee or oil in a separate small pan over medium heat.
3. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter (about 30 seconds).
4. Add chopped onion and cook until softened and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes.
5. Add minced garlic and grated ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
6. Stir in turmeric powder, garam masala, and cayenne pepper (if using); cook for 30 seconds.
7. Add diced tomato and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
8. Pour the spice mixture (tarka) into the cooked lentils. Stir well.
9. Season with salt to taste. Simmer for another 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
10. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Bean chips
description: A crunchy and savory snack, bean chips are made from various beans, offering a unique texture and often a healthier alternative to traditional potato chips, perfect for dipping.

name: Papad, grilled or broiled
description: A thin, crispy Indian cracker made from lentil, chickpea, or rice flour, papad is often seasoned with spices and becomes delightfully crunchy when grilled or broiled, perfect as an appetizer or accompaniment.

name: Sambar, vegetable stew
description:
A flavorful and aromatic South Indian lentil and vegetable stew, Sambar is simmered with tamarind, a blend of unique spices, and often drumsticks or eggplant, creating a tangy and comforting dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup toor dal (split pigeon peas), rinsed
- 3 cups water
- 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (e.g., chopped carrots, green beans, eggplant)
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 tomato, chopped
- 1 tbsp tamarind paste, dissolved in 1/4 cup warm water
- 1 tbsp Sambar powder
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- Salt to taste
- For tempering: 1 tbsp oil, 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, pinch of asafoetida, few curry leaves, 1-2 dried red chilies

Instructions:
1. Pressure cook or boil toor dal with 2 cups water and turmeric powder until soft and mushy (about 3-4 whistles in a pressure cooker or 20-25 mins boiling). Mash lightly.
2. In a separate pot, add chopped vegetables, onion, tomato, and 1 cup water. Cook until vegetables are tender.
3. Add the mashed dal to the vegetables. Stir in tamarind water, Sambar powder, and salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
4. For tempering: Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds; once they splutter, add cumin seeds, asafoetida, curry leaves, and dried red chilies. Sauté for 30 seconds.
5. Pour the tempering over the simmering Sambar. Stir gently and serve hot.

name: Lentil curry
description:
A comforting and aromatic dish, lentil curry features tender lentils simmered in a rich, spiced sauce, often with tomatoes, onions, and ginger, creating a deeply flavorful and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 tbsp olive oil or ghee
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, combine rinsed lentils and broth/water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
2. While lentils cook, heat oil/ghee in a separate large skillet over medium heat.
3. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
5. Stir in diced tomatoes, curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
6. Add the cooked lentils (with their liquid) to the skillet with the spice mixture. Stir well.
7. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
8. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Lentil curry with rice
description:
A complete and satisfying meal, lentil curry with rice combines aromatic, spiced lentil stew with fluffy rice, offering a harmonious blend of flavors and textures in every comforting bite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 tbsp olive oil or ghee
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 cup basmati or jasmine rice
- 2 cups water (for rice)
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Cook rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. In a separate pot, combine rice and 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
2. Prepare lentil curry: In a large pot, combine rinsed lentils and broth/water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
3. While lentils cook, heat oil/ghee in a separate large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in diced tomatoes, curry powder, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Add the cooked lentils (with their liquid) to the skillet with the spice mixture. Stir well.
6. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
7. Serve lentil curry over the cooked rice, garnished with fresh cilantro.

name: Soy nuts
description: A crunchy and protein-rich snack, soy nuts are roasted soybeans, offering a satisfying bite and a mild, nutty flavor, perfect for on-the-go energy or as a salad topping.

name: Soy chips
description: Crispy and savory, soy chips are a wholesome snack made from soybeans, providing a satisfying crunch and a good source of protein, often seasoned for extra flavor.

name: Soybean curd
description: Also known as tofu, soybean curd is a versatile plant-based protein made from coagulated soy milk, offering a neutral flavor that readily absorbs marinades and seasonings.

name: Edamame, cooked
description: Vibrant green and subtly sweet, cooked edamame are young soybeans, often served in their pods, offering a delightful snack or appetizer rich in protein and fiber.

name: Soybean curd cheese
description: A unique dairy-free alternative, soybean curd cheese (often a firm, aged tofu product) offers a savory, sometimes tangy flavor and a firm texture, suitable for slicing or crumbling.

name: Miso sauce
description: A savory and umami-rich Japanese condiment, miso sauce is typically made from fermented soybean paste, often blended with mirin, sake, and sugar, perfect for marinades, glazes, and dressings.

name: Hoisin sauce
description: A thick, fragrant, and sweet-savory Chinese condiment, hoisin sauce is made from fermented soybeans, garlic, vinegar, and spices, widely used as a glaze, dipping sauce, or stir-fry ingredient.

name: Soy sauce
description: A fundamental condiment in Asian cuisine, soy sauce is a salty, umami-rich liquid made from fermented soybeans, wheat, salt, and water, used to enhance flavor in countless dishes.

name: Soy sauce, reduced sodium
description: Offering the same distinctive umami flavor with less salt, reduced sodium soy sauce is a health-conscious alternative for seasoning dishes without compromising taste.

name: Yogurt, soy
description: A dairy-free alternative to traditional yogurt, soy yogurt is made from fermented soy milk, offering a creamy texture and tangy flavor, perfect for breakfast or smoothies.

name: Teriyaki sauce
description: A popular Japanese-inspired marinade and glaze, teriyaki sauce is a sweet and savory blend of soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar, imparting a glossy finish and rich flavor to meats and vegetables.

name: Teriyaki sauce, reduced sodium
description: Enjoy the classic sweet and savory notes of teriyaki sauce with a healthier twist; this reduced-sodium version offers great flavor for marinades and glazes with less salt.

name: Worcestershire sauce
description: A complex and savory fermented condiment, Worcestershire sauce boasts a unique blend of vinegar, anchovies, tamarind, molasses, and spices, adding a deep umami kick to savory dishes.

name: Soybean curd, deep fried
description: Crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, deep-fried soybean curd (tofu) offers a delightful texture and readily absorbs flavors, making it a versatile addition to many dishes.

name: Soybean curd, breaded, fried
description: Featuring a satisfying crunch, breaded and fried soybean curd (tofu) is coated in a seasoned crust and cooked until golden, creating a delicious and versatile plant-based protein.

name: Vermicelli, made from soybeans
description: These delicate, translucent noodles, made from soybeans, offer a light texture and readily absorb the flavors of broths and sauces, perfect for stir-fries, soups, and salads.

name: Textured vegetable protein, dry
description: A versatile and shelf-stable plant-based protein, dry textured vegetable protein (TVP) is made from defatted soy flour, rehydrating to a meat-like texture, ideal for vegetarian cooking.

name: Frozen dessert, non-dairy
description: A delightful treat for those avoiding dairy, non-dairy frozen desserts offer a creamy and sweet indulgence, made from bases like soy milk, almond milk, or coconut milk.

name: Soup, bean
description:
A comforting and hearty classic, bean soup features tender beans simmered in a flavorful broth, often with vegetables and spices, creating a warm and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
- 1 (15 oz) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
3. Add garlic and oregano; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in rinsed cannellini beans, kidney beans, vegetable broth, and diced tomatoes.
5. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 20-30 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Soup, bean, canned
description: A convenient and quick meal solution, canned bean soup offers a ready-to-heat, comforting blend of beans and broth, perfect for a simple lunch or light dinner.

name: Soup, miso or tofu
description:
A light and savory Japanese soup, miso or tofu soup features a delicate broth (often dashi) infused with miso paste, typically containing cubes of silken tofu and sometimes seaweed or scallions.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 cups dashi broth (or vegetable broth)
- 1/4 cup miso paste (white or red)
- 4 oz silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
- 2 tbsp chopped scallions
- 1/4 cup dried wakame seaweed (optional, rehydrated)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, bring dashi broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Do not boil.
2. Remove a small amount of hot broth and whisk it with the miso paste in a separate bowl until smooth. This prevents the miso from clumping.
3. Reduce heat to low. Stir the dissolved miso paste back into the saucepan. Do not boil after adding miso, as it can diminish its flavor and beneficial properties.
4. Gently add the tofu cubes and rehydrated wakame (if using). Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
5. Serve immediately, garnished with chopped scallions.

name: Soup, bean, canned, reduced sodium
description: A health-conscious choice for a quick meal, this canned bean soup offers the same comforting flavors with less sodium, making it a smart option for a balanced diet.

name: Soup, bean, with meat
description:
A hearty and satisfying meal, bean soup with meat combines tender beans and savory meat (like ham, sausage, or beef) in a rich, flavorful broth, perfect for a comforting dinner.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 lb smoked sausage or ham, diced
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 (15 oz) cans mixed beans (e.g., cannellini, kidney), rinsed and drained
- 6 cups chicken or beef broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add diced sausage or ham and cook until lightly browned. Remove meat and set aside, leaving drippings in the pot.
3. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
4. Add garlic and thyme; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
5. Stir in rinsed beans, broth, and diced tomatoes. Return cooked meat to the pot.
6. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for at least 30-40 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Soup, split pea, with meat
description:
A classic comfort food, split pea soup with meat (often ham or bacon) is a thick, creamy, and savory soup, slow-simmered to perfection, offering a deeply satisfying and hearty meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup dried green split peas, rinsed
- 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth
- 1 cup diced ham or 4 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. If using bacon, cook it in a large pot until crispy. Remove bacon, crumble, and set aside. Leave 1 tbsp drippings in the pot. If using ham, heat olive oil in the pot.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
3. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in rinsed split peas, broth, bay leaf, and diced ham (if using).
5. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until peas are very tender and have broken down, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
6. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with crumbled bacon (if used) or fresh parsley.

name: Soup, split pea
description:
A comforting and wholesome classic, split pea soup is a thick, creamy, and earthy soup made from dried green split peas, often seasoned with vegetables and herbs for a deeply satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup dried green split peas, rinsed
- 6 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bay leaf
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
3. Add garlic and thyme; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in rinsed split peas, vegetable broth/water, and bay leaf.
5. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until peas are very tender and have broken down, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
6. Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Soup, lentil, canned
description: A convenient and quick meal, canned lentil soup offers a ready-to-heat, hearty blend of tender lentils and savory broth, perfect for a simple lunch or light dinner.

name: Soup, lentil, canned, reduced sodium
description: A health-conscious choice for a quick meal, this canned lentil soup offers the same comforting flavors with less sodium, making it a smart option for a balanced diet.

name: Soup, lentil
description:
A wholesome and comforting classic, lentil soup is a hearty and flavorful dish made from tender lentils, vegetables, and aromatic spices, perfect for a nourishing meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
- 6 cups vegetable broth or water
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
3. Add garlic, cumin, and thyme; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in rinsed lentils, vegetable broth/water, and diced tomatoes.
5. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Soup, lentil, with meat
description:
A robust and satisfying meal, lentil soup with meat (often sausage, ham, or ground beef) combines tender lentils and savory meat in a rich, flavorful broth, perfect for a comforting dinner.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 lb ground beef or sausage, or diced ham
- 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
- 6 cups beef or chicken broth
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. If using ground meat, add and cook until browned, breaking it up. Drain excess fat. If using ham, add and cook until lightly browned.
3. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
4. Add garlic, cumin, and thyme; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
5. Stir in rinsed lentils, broth, and diced tomatoes.
6. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until lentils are tender and flavors have melded.
7. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Soup, mulligatawany
description:
A rich and flavorful Anglo-Indian soup, Mulligatawany is a curry-spiced broth often made with lentils, chicken or vegetables, apples, and coconut milk, offering a complex and aromatic taste.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil or ghee
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 apple, peeled, cored, and diced
- 1/2 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 4 cups chicken or vegetable broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 cup full-fat coconut milk
- 2 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat oil/ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
2. Add onion, carrot, and apple; cook until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
3. Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin, and turmeric; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Stir in rinsed lentils, broth, and diced tomatoes. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
5. Stir in coconut milk and heat through for 5 minutes (do not boil).
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Bacon strip, meatless
description: A plant-based alternative to traditional bacon, meatless bacon strips offer a savory, smoky flavor and crispy texture, perfect for breakfast or as a topping.

name: Bacon bits
description: Small, crunchy pieces of imitation bacon, these bits add a smoky, savory flavor and texture to salads, baked potatoes, and other dishes, often made from soy protein.

name: Breakfast link, pattie, or slice, meatless
description: A convenient plant-based option for breakfast, these meatless links, patties, or slices offer a savory, seasoned flavor and satisfying texture, perfect alongside eggs or pancakes.

name: Chicken, meatless, NFS
description: A versatile plant-based protein, meatless chicken (not further specified) offers a similar texture and neutral flavor to chicken, making it a great substitute in various recipes.

name: Hot dog, vegetarian
description: A plant-based alternative to traditional hot dogs, vegetarian hot dogs offer a savory flavor and familiar texture, perfect for grilling or simmering, and serving in a bun.

name: Luncheon slice, meatless-beef, chicken, salami or turkey
description: Convenient and versatile, these meatless luncheon slices offer a plant-based alternative to traditional deli meats, available in varieties like beef, chicken, salami, or turkey for sandwiches and snacks.

name: Meatball, meatless
description: A delicious plant-based alternative, meatless meatballs offer a savory, seasoned flavor and tender texture, perfect for pasta dishes, subs, or appetizers.

name: Veggie burger patty, no bun
description: A wholesome and flavorful plant-based option, a veggie burger patty (without the bun) is made from a blend of vegetables, grains, and legumes, offering a satisfying and nutritious meal.

name: Swiss steak, with gravy, meatless
description:
A comforting and hearty plant-based meal, meatless Swiss steak features tender, braised meat substitute smothered in a rich, savory gravy, perfect for a satisfying dinner.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb meatless steak (e.g., seitan or large portobello mushrooms)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, sliced
- 1 green bell pepper, sliced
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1 cup vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce (vegan if preferred)
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (for dredging)

Instructions:
1. If using seitan, slice into 1/2-inch thick pieces. If using portobello, remove stems. Dredge meatless steak in flour, seasoning with salt and pepper.
2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the meatless steak on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
3. Add sliced onion and bell pepper to the skillet; cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Stir in diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, Worcestershire sauce, and oregano. Bring to a simmer.
5. Return the browned meatless steak to the skillet, nestling it into the sauce. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-30 minutes, or until the steak is tender and the gravy has thickened.
6. Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Pot pie, no meat
description:
A comforting vegetarian classic, meatless pot pie features a rich, creamy filling of mixed vegetables (like peas, carrots, potatoes) in a savory gravy, all topped with a flaky, golden crust.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, diced
- 2 celery stalks, diced
- 1 cup diced potatoes
- 1 cup frozen peas
- 1/2 cup frozen corn
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1/2 cup milk (dairy or non-dairy)
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 sheet puff pastry or pie crust, thawed

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
3. Add onion, carrots, celery, and potatoes; cook until vegetables begin to soften, about 8-10 minutes.
4. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
5. Gradually whisk in vegetable broth and milk, stirring until the sauce thickens. Add thyme, salt, and pepper.
6. Stir in frozen peas and corn. Remove from heat.
7. Place the thawed puff pastry or pie crust over the vegetable mixture, crimping the edges to seal. Cut a few slits in the top for steam to escape.
8. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly.

name: Tofu and vegetables including carrots, broccoli, and/or dark-green leafy; no potatoes, with soy-based sauce
description:
A vibrant and healthy stir-fry, this dish combines firm tofu with a colorful medley of carrots, broccoli, and dark leafy greens, all tossed in a savory soy-based sauce for a quick and nutritious meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 cup chopped carrots
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 2 cups chopped dark leafy greens (e.g., spinach, kale)
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- Cooked rice or noodles, for serving

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and cornstarch to create the sauce. Set aside.
2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
3. Add pressed and cubed tofu and cook until golden brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove tofu and set aside.
4. Add carrots and broccoli to the skillet; stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
5. Add garlic and ginger; stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
6. Add dark leafy greens and stir-fry until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
7. Return tofu to the skillet. Give the sauce a quick whisk and pour it over the tofu and vegetables. Stir constantly until the sauce thickens and coats everything.
8. Serve immediately over cooked rice or noodles.

name: Tofu and vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark-green leafy; no potatoes, with soy-based sauce
description:
A vibrant and healthy stir-fry featuring tender tofu and a colorful medley of vegetables (excluding specific ones) all coated in a savory soy-based sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 30 min tofu pressing)

Ingredients:
- 1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed and cubed
- 1 tbsp cornstarch
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 cup sliced bell peppers (any color)
- 1 cup sliced zucchini
- 1 cup sliced mushrooms
- 1/2 cup snap peas
- Cooked rice, for serving

Instructions:
1. 1. Press tofu for 30 minutes, then cut into cubes. Toss with cornstarch.
2. 2. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic for the sauce.
3. 3. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add tofu and cook until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove tofu and set aside.
4. 4. Add bell peppers, zucchini, mushrooms, and snap peas to the same skillet. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
5. 5. Return tofu to the skillet. Pour the sauce over the tofu and vegetables, tossing to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
6. 6. Serve immediately over cooked rice.

name: Vegetarian, fillet
description: A plant-based fillet, often made from soy, wheat, or pea protein, designed to mimic the texture and savory taste of a traditional meat fillet, perfect for a hearty vegetarian meal.

name: Vegetarian stew
description:
A comforting and hearty stew brimming with a variety of vegetables, legumes, and often grains, simmered in a rich, flavorful broth, perfect for a wholesome meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup diced celery
- 1 cup diced parsnips
- 1 (28 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 cup green lentils, rinsed
- 1 tsp dried thyme
- 1/2 tsp dried rosemary
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 cup chopped kale or spinach (optional)

Instructions:
1. 1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic, celery, and parsnips, cook for another 5 minutes.
2. 2. Stir in diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, rinsed lentils, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until lentils and vegetables are tender.
3. 3. Season with salt and pepper. If using, stir in kale or spinach and cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
4. 4. Serve hot.

name: Vegetarian stroganoff
description:
A creamy and savory vegetarian take on the classic stroganoff, featuring mushrooms or plant-based protein in a rich, tangy sauce, often served over noodles.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, sliced
- 8 oz cremini mushrooms, sliced
- 1 block (8 oz) firm tofu or 1 cup plant-based beef strips, cubed
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1 cup plant-based sour cream or cashew cream
- 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
- Cooked egg noodles or pasta, for serving
- Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions:
1. 1. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and tofu/plant-based strips, cook until browned, about 7-10 minutes. Season with thyme, salt, and pepper.
2. 2. In a small bowl, whisk together vegetable broth and flour until smooth. Pour into the skillet, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens, about 1-2 minutes.
3. 3. Reduce heat to low. Stir in plant-based sour cream and Dijon mustard. Heat through gently, do not boil.
4. 4. Serve immediately over cooked egg noodles or pasta, garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Veggie burger, on bun
description:
A delicious plant-based patty, often made from beans, grains, or vegetables, served on a soft bun with your favorite toppings.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 veggie burger patty (store-bought or homemade)
- 1 burger bun
- Lettuce leaf
- Tomato slice
- Onion slice
- Pickles
- Ketchup and mustard, to taste

Instructions:
1. 1. Cook the veggie burger patty according to package directions (grill, pan-fry, or bake).
2. 2. Lightly toast the burger bun if desired.
3. 3. Assemble the burger: Place the cooked patty on the bottom half of the bun. Top with lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles. Add ketchup and mustard as desired.
4. 4. Place the top half of the bun on top and serve.

name: Veggie burger, on bun, with cheese
description:
A savory plant-based patty, topped with melted cheese and served on a soft bun, offering a satisfying and flavorful vegetarian meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 veggie burger patty
- 1 slice of plant-based cheese
- 1 burger bun
- Lettuce leaf
- Tomato slice
- Onion slice
- Pickles
- Ketchup and mustard, to taste

Instructions:
1. 1. Cook the veggie burger patty according to package directions. During the last minute of cooking, place the cheese slice on top of the patty to melt.
2. 2. Lightly toast the burger bun if desired.
3. 3. Assemble the burger: Place the cooked patty with melted cheese on the bottom half of the bun. Top with lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles. Add ketchup and mustard as desired.
4. 4. Place the top half of the bun on top and serve.

name: Falafel sandwich
description:
A popular Middle Eastern street food featuring crispy, spiced chickpea fritters (falafel) tucked into warm pita bread with fresh vegetables and a creamy tahini sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4-5 falafel patties (store-bought or homemade)
- 1 pita bread
- 1/4 cup shredded lettuce
- 2 slices tomato
- 2 slices cucumber
- 1 tbsp tahini sauce
- Optional: pickled turnips, hot sauce

Instructions:
1. 1. Heat falafel patties according to package instructions (fry, bake, or air fry) until crispy and hot.
2. 2. Warm the pita bread slightly (microwave for 10-15 seconds or toast lightly).
3. 3. Carefully open the pita bread to form a pocket.
4. 4. Fill the pita pocket with shredded lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and the hot falafel patties.
5. 5. Drizzle with tahini sauce and add any optional toppings like pickled turnips or hot sauce.
6. 6. Serve immediately.

name: Peanut butter and jelly
description:
A timeless American classic, combining creamy or crunchy peanut butter with sweet fruit jelly, often spread between two slices of bread.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 2 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 slices of bread (white or wheat)
- 2 tbsp peanut butter
- 1-2 tbsp jelly or jam

Instructions:
1. 1. Lay out two slices of bread.
2. 2. Spread peanut butter evenly on one slice of bread.
3. 3. Spread jelly or jam evenly on the other slice of bread.
4. 4. Place the two slices of bread together, peanut butter side facing jelly side.
5. 5. Cut in half diagonally or straight across, if desired, and serve.

name: Peanut butter and chocolate spread
description: A decadent combination of rich peanut butter and sweet chocolate, creating a delightful spread perfect for toast, desserts, or a spoonful straight from the jar.

name: Peanut sauce

name: Soup, peanut
description:
A hearty and flavorful soup with a creamy peanut base, often incorporating vegetables, spices, and sometimes meat or plant-based protein, popular in West African cuisine.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bell pepper (any color), chopped
- 1 sweet potato, peeled and diced
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, undrained
- 1/2 cup creamy peanut butter
- 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Cooked rice or chopped cilantro for garnish

Instructions:
1. 1. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and bell pepper, cook for another 3 minutes.
2. 2. Stir in diced sweet potato, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and red pepper flakes (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until sweet potato is tender.
3. 3. Stir in peanut butter until fully dissolved and the soup is creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
4. 4. Serve hot, garnished with cooked rice or fresh cilantro if desired.

name: Gravy, vegetarian
description:
A rich and savory plant-based sauce, typically made from vegetable broth, herbs, and thickeners, perfect for drizzling over vegetarian roasts, mashed potatoes, or vegetables.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil or vegan butter
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tbsp soy sauce or tamari
- 1/2 tsp onion powder
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. 1. In a medium saucepan, melt olive oil or vegan butter over medium heat.
2. 2. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until a light roux forms.
3. 3. Gradually whisk in the vegetable broth, ensuring no lumps. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency.
4. 4. Stir in soy sauce, onion powder, and garlic powder. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
5. 5. Serve hot.

name: Peanut butter sandwich, NFS

A simple and satisfying sandwich featuring a generous spread of peanut butter between two slices of bread, a classic comfort food.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 1 minute

Ingredients:

Instructions:
1. 1. Lay out two slices of bread.
2. 2. Spread peanut butter evenly on one slice of bread.
3. 3. Place the two slices of bread together.
4. 4. Cut in half diagonally or straight across, if desired, and serve.

name: Peanut butter sandwich, with regular peanut butter, on white bread

A classic and comforting sandwich featuring creamy or crunchy regular peanut butter spread generously on soft white bread.

name: Peanut butter sandwich, with reduced fat peanut butter, on white bread
description:
A lighter version of the classic, featuring reduced-fat peanut butter spread on soft white bread for a satisfying snack.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 1 minute

Ingredients:
- 2 slices white bread
- 2 tbsp reduced fat peanut butter

name: Garlic bread, NFS
description:
A beloved side dish, garlic bread features slices of bread generously slathered with a savory garlic-butter mixture and baked until golden and fragrant.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 loaf French bread or baguette
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened
- 3-4 cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped (optional)
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- Pinch of black pepper

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. Slice the bread lengthwise or into 1-inch thick slices, but not all the way through if keeping it as a loaf.
3. In a small bowl, combine softened butter, minced garlic, chopped parsley (if using), salt, and pepper.
4. Spread the garlic butter mixture evenly over the cut sides of the bread.
5. Wrap the loaf loosely in aluminum foil or place slices on a baking sheet.
6. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until heated through and fragrant. For a crispier top, unwrap and bake for an additional 2-3 minutes.
7. Serve warm.

name: Bruschetta
description:
A classic Italian appetizer, bruschetta features grilled bread rubbed with garlic, drizzled with olive oil, and typically topped with fresh diced tomatoes and basil.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 baguette or rustic bread, sliced 1/2 inch thick
- 2 ripe Roma tomatoes, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, 1 minced, 1 whole for rubbing
- 1/4 cup fresh basil, chopped
- 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
- 1 tablespoon balsamic glaze (optional)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat grill or broiler to medium-high.
2. Brush both sides of the bread slices lightly with olive oil.
3. Grill or broil bread for 1-2 minutes per side, until lightly golden and crisp. Remove from heat.
4. While bread is still warm, rub one side of each slice with the whole garlic clove.
5. In a medium bowl, combine diced tomatoes, minced garlic, chopped basil, 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix gently.
6. Spoon the tomato mixture generously over each toasted bread slice.
7. Drizzle with balsamic glaze if desired.
8. Serve immediately.

name: Biscuit, NFS
description:
A classic, flaky, and tender baked good, typically made with flour, fat, and a leavening agent, perfect for breakfast or alongside savory meals.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 biscuits
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
- 3/4 cup cold milk

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
2. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
3. Cut in the cold butter using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
4. Gradually add cold milk, mixing until just combined and a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.
5. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently knead 3-4 times. Pat or roll to about 1/2 to 3/4 inch thickness.
6. Cut out biscuits using a round cutter. Place on an ungreased baking sheet, about 1 inch apart.
7. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown on top.
8. Serve warm.
