name: Cornbread stuffing
description:
A savory and aromatic side dish, cornbread stuffing combines crumbled cornbread with herbs, vegetables, and broth, often baked until golden and moist.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 servings
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 6 cups crumbled cornbread (day-old is best)
- 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley
- 1 tsp dried sage
- 1/2 tsp dried thyme
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
- 2 cups chicken or vegetable broth

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and celery; cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
3. Remove from heat and stir in parsley, sage, thyme, salt, and pepper.
4. In a large bowl, combine crumbled cornbread with the cooked vegetable mixture.
5. In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs and broth. Pour over the cornbread mixture and mix gently until well combined.
6. Transfer the stuffing to the prepared baking dish.
7. Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until golden brown and heated through. If desired, cover with foil for the first 20 minutes to prevent drying, then uncover to brown.
8. Serve hot.

name: Cornbread muffin, stick, round
description:
Individual portions of classic cornbread, baked in muffin tins or special molds, offering a convenient and perfectly sized serving with a golden crust and tender interior.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 muffins/sticks
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup yellow cornmeal
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar (optional)
- 1 tbsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 large egg
- 1 cup milk
- 1/4 cup melted unsalted butter or vegetable oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or cornbread stick/round molds.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, sugar (if using), baking powder, and salt.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, milk, and melted butter/oil.
4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix; a few lumps are fine.
5. Fill the prepared muffin cups or molds about 2/3 full.
6. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean and the tops are golden brown.
7. Serve warm.

name: Cornbread muffin, stick, round, made from home recipe
description:
Homemade cornbread muffins, sticks, or rounds offer a delightful individual portion of the classic, with a golden crust and a tender, crumbly texture, perfect for any meal.

name: Corn flour patty or tart, fried
description:
Crispy on the outside and tender within, these fried patties or tarts made from corn flour offer a delightful savory or slightly sweet bite, often enjoyed as a snack or side.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 patties
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup corn flour (masa harina)
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 cup warm water
- Vegetable oil for frying

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, combine corn flour and salt.
2. Gradually add warm water, mixing with your hands until a soft, pliable dough forms. If too dry, add a little more water; if too sticky, add a little more corn flour.
3. Divide the dough into 8-10 equal balls.
4. Flatten each ball into a patty or tart shape, about 1/4 inch thick.
5. Heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
6. Carefully place patties into the hot oil (do not overcrowd the pan). Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
7. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
8. Serve warm, plain or with desired toppings.

name: Corn pone, baked
description:
A traditional Southern dish, baked corn pone is a simple, rustic cornmeal bread, often oval-shaped, with a firm crust and a dense, savory interior.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 pones
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups yellow cornmeal
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 1/2 cups boiling water
- 2 tbsp melted butter or bacon grease (plus more for greasing)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a baking sheet or cast iron skillet.
2. In a large bowl, combine cornmeal and salt.
3. Carefully pour in the boiling water and stir until a thick batter forms. Let stand for 5 minutes.
4. Stir in the melted butter or bacon grease.
5. Using wet hands, shape the mixture into oval-shaped patties, about 3-4 inches long and 1 inch thick.
6. Place the pones on the prepared baking sheet or skillet.
7. Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp on the outside.
8. Serve warm.

name: Corn pone, fried
description:
Crispy on the outside and tender within, fried corn pone is a savory cornmeal patty, a Southern classic, often enjoyed with hearty meals.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 pones
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups yellow cornmeal
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 1/2 cups boiling water
- Vegetable oil or bacon grease for frying

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine cornmeal and salt.
2. Carefully pour in the boiling water and stir until a thick batter forms. Let stand for 5 minutes.
3. Using wet hands, shape the mixture into oval-shaped patties, about 3-4 inches long and 1 inch thick.
4. Heat about 1/2 inch of vegetable oil or bacon grease in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
5. Carefully place pones into the hot oil (do not overcrowd the pan). Fry for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crisp.
6. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
7. Serve warm.

name: Gordita/sope shell, plain, no filling
description:
Thick, savory corn masa shells, perfect for filling with a variety of ingredients, offering a hearty and authentic base for Mexican dishes like gorditas or sopes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 shells
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups masa harina
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 1/2 cups warm water
- Vegetable oil for frying (optional, for sopes)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine masa harina and salt.
2. Gradually add warm water, mixing with your hands until a soft, pliable dough forms. Knead for 2-3 minutes until smooth. If too dry, add a little more water; if too sticky, add a little more masa harina.
3. Divide the dough into 10-12 equal balls.
4. Using a tortilla press or rolling pin, flatten each ball into a thick disc, about 1/4 to 1/3 inch thick and 3-4 inches in diameter.
5. Heat a comal or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Cook each shell for 1-2 minutes per side, until lightly browned and cooked through.
6. For sopes: While still warm, pinch up the edges of the cooked disc to form a rim. Lightly fry in a little oil until crisp, if desired.
7. Serve warm, ready for filling.

name: Hush puppy
description:
Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, hush puppies are savory, deep-fried cornmeal fritters, a beloved Southern side dish often served with seafood.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6 servings
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup yellow cornmeal
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp granulated sugar
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)
- 1/2 cup finely chopped onion
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup buttermilk
- 2 tbsp milk
- Vegetable oil for deep frying

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and cayenne pepper (if using).
2. Stir in the chopped onion.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the egg, buttermilk, and milk.
4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
5. Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C).
6. Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through.
7. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
8. Serve hot.

name: Johnnycake
description:
A simple, griddle-cooked cornmeal flatbread, Johnnycakes are a New England classic, often served with butter and maple syrup, or as a savory accompaniment.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 johnnycakes
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup fine cornmeal
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tbsp granulated sugar (optional)
- 1 1/2 cups boiling water
- 2 tbsp melted butter or bacon grease (plus more for cooking)

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, combine cornmeal, salt, and sugar (if using).
2. Carefully pour in the boiling water and stir until a thick batter forms. Let stand for 5 minutes.
3. Stir in the melted butter or bacon grease.
4. Heat a lightly greased griddle or cast iron skillet over medium heat.
5. Drop spoonfuls of batter onto the hot griddle, flattening slightly with the back of the spoon to form thin cakes, about 3-4 inches in diameter.
6. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crisp.
7. Serve warm with butter, maple syrup, or savory toppings.

name: Spoonbread
description:
A light and fluffy Southern delicacy, spoonbread is a savory cornmeal pudding, so tender it must be eaten with a spoon, often served as a side dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 servings
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup yellow cornmeal
- 2 cups milk
- 1/4 cup (1/2 stick) unsalted butter
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 3 large eggs, separated

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 1 1/2-quart baking dish.
2. In a medium saucepan, combine cornmeal, milk, butter, and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a porridge-like consistency, about 5-7 minutes.
3. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
4. Stir in the baking powder and egg yolks until well combined.
5. In a separate clean bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.
6. Gently fold the beaten egg whites into the cornmeal mixture until just combined.
7. Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish.
8. Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until puffed, golden brown, and set in the center.
9. Serve immediately with a spoon.

name: Tortilla, NFS
description:
A versatile flatbread, typically thin and round, made from either corn or wheat flour, forming the foundation for countless dishes in Mexican and Central American cuisine.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 tortillas
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 20-30 min rest)

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour (or masa harina for corn)
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 cup vegetable shortening (or lard)
- 1/2 cup warm water

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, combine flour and salt.
2. Cut in shortening using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
3. Gradually add warm water, mixing until a dough forms. Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth. (For corn tortillas, knead until pliable).
4. Divide into 8-10 balls, cover with a damp cloth, and let rest for 20-30 minutes.
5. Heat a comal or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
6. Roll each ball into a thin circle (about 6-8 inches in diameter) using a rolling pin or tortilla press.
7. Cook each tortilla on the hot, ungreased griddle for 30-60 seconds per side, until lightly browned and puffed.
8. Stack cooked tortillas and keep warm in a tortilla warmer or wrapped in a clean towel.

name: Tortilla, corn
description:
A staple of Mexican cuisine, corn tortillas are thin, round flatbreads made from masa harina, offering an earthy flavor and pliable texture, perfect for tacos and enchiladas.

4. Heat a comal or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.

7. Stack cooked tortillas and keep warm in a tortilla warmer or wrapped in a clean towel.

description:
A healthier alternative to traditional flour tortillas, whole wheat tortillas offer a nutty flavor and a slightly denser, chewier texture, perfect for wraps and healthy meals.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 tortillas
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 20-30 min rest)

Ingredients:

name: Taco shell, corn
description:
Crispy and crunchy, corn taco shells are typically made from corn tortillas that are fried or baked into a U-shape, providing a sturdy and flavorful vessel for taco fillings.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 taco shells
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 12 pre-made corn tortillas
- Vegetable oil for frying (or cooking spray for baking)

Instructions:
1. For frying: Heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
2. Carefully place one tortilla into the hot oil. As it softens (about 10-15 seconds), use tongs to fold it in half, creating a U-shape. Hold it in place for a few seconds until it holds its shape.
3. Fry for 1-2 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crisp. Remove and drain on paper towels.
4. For baking: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly spray tortillas with cooking spray.
5. Drape tortillas over two bars of an oven rack, creating a U-shape. Bake for 7-10 minutes, or until crisp and golden.
6. Serve immediately with your favorite taco fillings.

name: Taco shell, flour
description:
Soft and pliable, flour taco shells are typically made from flour tortillas, offering a milder flavor and chewier texture than corn, often served warm and folded.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 taco shells
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 12 pre-made flour tortillas

Instructions:
1. Heat a dry skillet or comal over medium-high heat.
2. Place one flour tortilla on the hot surface and cook for 15-20 seconds per side, until lightly warmed and pliable, with a few browned spots.
3. Alternatively, microwave tortillas for 15-30 seconds until warm and soft.
4. Serve immediately, folded or filled with your favorite taco ingredients.

name: Arepa Dominicana
description:
A sweet and savory cornmeal cake, Arepa Dominicana is a unique baked dish, often enriched with coconut milk, raisins, and spices, creating a dense, comforting treat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 servings
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups fine cornmeal
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
- 4 cups coconut milk
- 1/2 cup raisins
- 1/4 cup (1/2 stick) unsalted butter, melted

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, sugar, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
3. Gradually whisk in the coconut milk until smooth. Stir in the raisins and melted butter.
4. Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
5. Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
6. Let cool slightly before serving. It will firm up as it cools.

name: Muffin, NFS
description:
A versatile baked good, muffins are individual, quick breads, often moist and tender, perfect for breakfast, snacks, or light desserts.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 muffins
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1 large egg
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or melted butter)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease well.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, milk, and vegetable oil.
4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix; a few lumps are fine.
5. Fill muffin cups about 2/3 full.
6. Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until golden brown and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Let cool in the tin for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

description:
Bursting with flavor, fruit muffins are tender, moist, and studded with fresh or frozen berries, diced apples, or other fruits, making them a delightful breakfast or snack.

Ingredients:

- 1/4 tsp salt

5. Fill muffin cups about 2/3 full.
6. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Let cool in the tin for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

name: Muffin, oatmeal
description:
Hearty and comforting, oatmeal muffins are made with rolled oats, offering a chewy texture and a wholesome, slightly nutty flavor, perfect for a nourishing breakfast.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 muffins
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup rolled oats
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 1 tbsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 large egg
- 1 cup milk
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or melted butter)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease well.

4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
5. Fill muffin cups about 2/3 full.
6. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until golden brown and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Let cool in the tin for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

name: Muffin, oat bran
description:
Nutritious and moist, oat bran muffins are packed with fiber, offering a wholesome and satisfying texture with a mild, earthy flavor, ideal for a healthy start to the day.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 muffins
Prep Time: 15 minutes

- 1 cup oat bran
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 1 tbsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 large egg
- 1 1/4 cups milk
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or melted butter)

name: Muffin, plain
description:
A simple yet satisfying classic, plain muffins are tender, moist, and subtly sweet, providing a perfect canvas for butter, jam, or simply enjoyed on their own.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12 muffins
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1 large egg
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or melted butter)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease well.
