name: Yokan
description: A traditional Japanese dessert, yokan is a thick, jellied confection made from red bean paste, agar-agar, and sugar. It has a firm, smooth texture and a subtly sweet, earthy flavor, often served in blocks with green tea.

name: Haupia
description:
A traditional Hawaiian coconut pudding, haupia is a creamy, firm, and subtly sweet dessert made from coconut milk, sugar, and cornstarch. It's often cut into squares and served chilled, offering a taste of the tropics.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 can (13.5 oz) full-fat coconut milk
- 1/2 cup water
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar
- 1/4 cup cornstarch

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, whisk together coconut milk, water, and sugar until sugar is dissolved.
2. In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of the coconut milk mixture until smooth.
3. Add the cornstarch slurry back into the saucepan with the remaining coconut milk mixture.
4. Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil.
5. Reduce heat to low and continue to stir for 1-2 minutes.
6. Pour the mixture into an 8x8 inch pan (or similar shallow dish) that has been lightly moistened with water.
7. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until completely firm.
8. Once firm, cut into squares and serve chilled.

name: Italian Ice
description: A refreshing, dairy-free frozen dessert with a smooth, granular texture, made from fruit juice or purees, sugar, and water. It's a vibrant, flavorful treat, perfect for cooling down on a hot day.

name: Italian Ice, no sugar added
description: A light and refreshing frozen dessert, offering the vibrant fruit flavors and granular texture of traditional Italian ice, but without any added sugar. It's a cool, guilt-free treat for those managing sugar intake.

name: Freezer pop
description: A simple, refreshing frozen treat consisting of flavored, sweetened liquid encased in a plastic sleeve. These icy pops are a nostalgic summer staple, easy to enjoy by simply snipping off the top.

name: Snow cone
description: A classic icy treat made from finely shaved ice packed into a cone-shaped cup and drenched with brightly colored, fruit-flavored syrups. It's a simple, refreshing way to beat the heat.

name: Snow cone, no sugar added
description: A refreshing icy treat featuring finely shaved ice doused in flavorful, brightly colored syrups, but without any added sugar. It offers a cool, sweet escape for those seeking a sugar-conscious option.

name: Candy, NFS
description: A broad category encompassing a wide array of sweet confections, typically made primarily from sugar, often with flavorings, colorings, and other ingredients. Candies offer a delightful burst of sweetness in various forms and textures.

name: Almonds, chocolate covered candy
description: Crunchy, roasted almonds enrobed in a smooth, rich layer of chocolate. This classic confection offers a delightful contrast of textures and a harmonious blend of nutty and sweet flavors.

name: Chocolate candy, other, NFS
description: A diverse range of sweet confections primarily featuring chocolate, beyond standard bars or common types. These can include unique shapes, fillings, or flavor combinations, offering a delightful surprise for chocolate lovers.

name: Chocolate candy
description: A beloved sweet confection made primarily from cocoa solids, cocoa butter, and sugar. It comes in countless forms, from solid bars to intricate filled pieces, offering a rich, indulgent, and universally adored flavor.

name: Chocolate candy with nuts, other, NFS
description: A delightful chocolate confection featuring various nuts, offering a satisfying crunch and nutty flavor alongside the rich sweetness of chocolate. This category encompasses a wide range of nut and chocolate combinations.

name: Chocolate candy with nuts
description: A classic confection combining the rich, smooth taste of chocolate with the satisfying crunch and earthy flavor of nuts. This popular pairing offers a delightful textural contrast and a balanced sweet and savory experience.

name: Chocolate candy with cereal
description: A playful confection that marries the rich sweetness of chocolate with the crispy, airy texture of cereal pieces. This combination creates a delightful crunch and a unique, satisfying bite.

name: Chocolate candy, cookie filled
description: An indulgent chocolate confection featuring a delightful cookie center, offering a satisfying crunch or chew within the smooth chocolate shell. It's a perfect blend of two beloved treats.

name: Chocolate chips
description: Small, teardrop-shaped pieces of chocolate, designed to hold their shape when baked. They are a staple in baking, adding bursts of rich chocolate flavor and melty goodness to cookies, muffins, and other desserts.

name: Candy, sprinkles
description: Tiny, colorful confectionery decorations, typically made from sugar, cornstarch, and food coloring. Sprinkles add a festive touch, vibrant color, and a subtle crunch to cakes, cookies, ice cream, and other sweet treats.

name: Dark chocolate candy, other, NFS
description: A sophisticated range of confections made with dark chocolate, characterized by a higher cocoa content and a less sweet, more intense flavor profile. These can include various forms and fillings, appealing to true chocolate connoisseurs.

name: Dark chocolate candy
description: An intense and sophisticated confection made with a high percentage of cocoa solids, resulting in a rich, slightly bitter, and deeply aromatic flavor. It offers a complex taste experience, often enjoyed for its robust chocolate notes.

name: Dark chocolate candy with nuts, other, NFS
description: A refined confection combining the intense, slightly bitter notes of dark chocolate with the satisfying crunch and earthy flavor of various nuts. This pairing offers a sophisticated balance of textures and tastes.

name: Dark chocolate candy with nuts
description: A sophisticated treat featuring rich, intense dark chocolate paired with crunchy, earthy nuts. The slight bitterness of the dark chocolate beautifully complements the nutty flavor, creating a complex and satisfying indulgence.

name: White chocolate candy
description: A creamy, sweet confection made from cocoa butter, sugar, and milk solids, without cocoa solids. Its smooth texture and delicate vanilla notes offer a distinct, mellow sweetness, often used in desserts and confections.

name: Chocolate candy, fudge
description: A dense, rich, and intensely sweet confection with a smooth, melt-in-your-mouth texture, made from chocolate, sugar, butter, and milk. It's a classic homemade treat, often enjoyed in squares.

name: Chocolate candy, caramel filled
description: An irresistible confection featuring a luscious, chewy caramel center enrobed in smooth, rich chocolate. The combination of sweet, buttery caramel and decadent chocolate creates a truly indulgent experience.

name: Chocolate candy, caramel filled with nuts
description: A decadent treat combining the rich sweetness of chocolate with a gooey, buttery caramel filling, further enhanced by the satisfying crunch of nuts. It's a symphony of textures and flavors in every bite.

name: Chocolate candy, coconut filled
description: A tropical delight featuring a sweet, moist, and often shredded coconut filling enrobed in smooth chocolate. This confection offers a delightful contrast between the rich chocolate and the chewy, exotic coconut.

name: Chocolate candy, cream filled
description: An elegant confection consisting of a soft, smooth, and often flavored cream center, delicately enrobed in rich chocolate. These candies offer a luxurious, melt-in-your-mouth experience.

name: Chocolate candy, nougat filled
description: A satisfying confection featuring a light, chewy, and often nutty nougat center, enveloped in smooth chocolate. The combination offers a delightful textural contrast and a balanced sweetness.

name: Chocolate candy, nougat filled with nuts
description: An indulgent treat combining the rich sweetness of chocolate with a chewy, airy nougat center, further enhanced by the satisfying crunch of nuts. It's a harmonious blend of textures and flavors.

name: Chocolate candy, peanut butter filled
description: A beloved confection featuring a creamy, salty-sweet peanut butter filling encased in smooth, rich chocolate. This classic pairing offers an irresistible balance of flavors and textures.

name: Chocolate candy with dried fruit
description: A delightful confection that pairs the rich sweetness of chocolate with the chewy texture and concentrated flavor of dried fruits like raisins, cranberries, or cherries. It's a harmonious blend of sweet and fruity notes.

name: Chocolate candy, sugar free
description: A sweet indulgence offering the rich, satisfying taste of chocolate without the added sugar. Sweetened with alternatives, it's a delightful option for those managing their sugar intake while still craving a chocolate treat.

name: Candy, non chocolate, other, NFS
description: A vast and colorful category of sweet confections that do not contain chocolate. These can range from fruity gummies and hard candies to chewy caramels and mints, offering a diverse array of flavors and textures.

name: Ladoo, round ball
description: A traditional Indian sweet, ladoo is a spherical confection made from flour, sugar, and fat, often flavored with cardamom, nuts, or dried fruits. These dense, sweet balls are popular during festivals and celebrations.

name: Candy, licorice
description: A distinctive confection known for its unique flavor derived from the licorice root. It comes in various forms, from chewy ropes to hard pastilles, offering a sweet, earthy, and sometimes anise-like taste.

name: Candy, marshmallow
description: A soft, spongy confection made from sugar, gelatin, and air, resulting in a light and airy texture. Marshmallows are beloved for their sweet, vanilla flavor and are often enjoyed toasted, in hot cocoa, or as a standalone treat.

name: Candy, caramel
description: A chewy, buttery, and intensely sweet confection made by cooking sugar until it caramelizes, then adding butter and cream. Its rich, golden-brown hue and melt-in-your-mouth texture make it a classic indulgence.

name: Candy, nougat with nuts
description: A delightful confection featuring a light, airy, and chewy nougat base studded with crunchy nuts. This sweet treat offers a satisfying textural contrast and a harmonious blend of nutty and sweet flavors.

name: Peanuts, chocolate covered candy
description: Crunchy, roasted peanuts generously coated in a smooth, sweet layer of chocolate. This classic combination offers a perfect balance of salty, nutty, and sweet flavors, with a satisfying textural contrast.

name: Candy, peanut brittle
description: A thin, crunchy confection made from caramelized sugar and peanuts, often with a hint of butter and baking soda for a delicate, airy texture. Its irresistible snap and sweet-nutty flavor make it a beloved treat.

name: Candy, mint
description: A refreshing confection characterized by its cool, invigorating mint flavor. Mints come in various forms, from hard candies to chewy pastilles, offering a crisp, clean taste that can freshen the breath.

name: Candy, gummy
description: A chewy, fruit-flavored confection with a soft, gelatinous texture. Gummy candies come in an endless array of fun shapes, colors, and flavors, making them a popular and playful treat for all ages.

name: Candy, hard
description: A solid, rigid confection made by boiling sugar syrup to a high temperature and then cooling it. Hard candies come in various shapes and flavors, offering a long-lasting sweetness as they slowly dissolve in the mouth.

name: Candy, lollipop
description: A classic hard candy mounted on a stick, designed for convenient, long-lasting enjoyment. Lollipops come in countless flavors, shapes, and colors, offering a simple, sweet pleasure.

name: Cough drops
description: Small, medicated lozenges designed to soothe sore throats and suppress coughs. They typically contain menthol or other active ingredients, often flavored to make them more palatable.

name: Candy, cotton
description: A whimsical, airy confection made from spun sugar, resembling fluffy clouds. Its delicate, melt-in-your-mouth texture and pure sweet flavor make it a nostalgic treat, often associated with fairs and carnivals.

name: Candy, fruit flavored pieces
description: Small, chewy or hard confections bursting with vibrant fruit flavors. These candies come in various shapes and textures, offering a sweet and tangy taste experience reminiscent of fresh fruits.

name: Chocolate candy, candy shell
description: A delightful confection featuring a rich chocolate center encased in a thin, crisp, and often colorful candy shell. The shell provides a satisfying crunch and protects the chocolate within.

name: Chocolate candy, candy shell with nuts
description: A crunchy and sweet confection featuring a nut (like a peanut or almond) at its core, surrounded by a layer of chocolate, and then finished with a crisp, colorful candy shell. It offers a delightful multi-textural experience.

name: Candy, fruit snacks
description: Chewy, often fruit-shaped confections made primarily from fruit juice concentrates, sugar, and gelatin. They offer a sweet, fruity taste and a soft, gummy texture, popular as a convenient snack.

name: Candy, fruit leather
description: A thin, chewy, and pliable confection made from pureed fruit that has been dried into a sheet. It offers a concentrated, natural fruit flavor and a satisfyingly chewy texture, often rolled up for easy snacking.

name: Candy, taffy
description: A chewy, elastic confection made by stretching and pulling boiled sugar syrup until it becomes aerated and opaque. Taffy comes in a myriad of flavors and colors, offering a delightful, long-lasting chew.

name: Candy, non chocolate, sugar free
description: A diverse range of sweet confections, free from chocolate and added sugar, offering a guilt-free indulgence. These candies come in various flavors and textures, sweetened with alternatives for those managing sugar intake.

name: Chewing gum, sugar free
description: A flexible, flavored confection designed for chewing, providing a burst of flavor and freshening breath without added sugar. It's a popular choice for maintaining oral hygiene and satisfying cravings.

name: Coffee, NS as to type
description: A stimulating beverage brewed from roasted and ground coffee beans. Its rich aroma and robust flavor make it a popular choice worldwide, enjoyed for its energizing effects and complex taste profile.

name: Coffee, NS as to brewed or instant
description: A versatile and invigorating beverage derived from coffee beans, offering a rich aroma and stimulating properties. It can be prepared either by brewing ground beans or by dissolving instant granules in hot water.

name: Coffee, brewed
description: A classic and widely enjoyed beverage made by steeping ground coffee beans in hot water. It offers a rich, aromatic, and often robust flavor, providing a comforting and energizing start to the day.

name: Coffee, brewed, blend of regular and decaffeinated
description: A balanced coffee option that combines the full flavor of regular coffee with a reduced caffeine content, thanks to a blend of both regular and decaffeinated beans. It offers a milder stimulant effect.

name: Coffee, Turkish
description: A unique and intensely flavorful coffee prepared by boiling finely ground coffee beans with water (and often sugar) in a special pot called a cezve. It's served unfiltered, allowing the grounds to settle, resulting in a thick, rich brew.

name: Coffee, espresso
description: A concentrated coffee beverage made by forcing hot, pressurized water through finely ground coffee beans. It's characterized by its intense flavor, thick crema, and small serving size, forming the base for many coffee drinks.

name: Coffee, espresso, decaffeinated

name: Coffee, brewed, flavored

name: Coffee, Cuban
description: A strong, sweet, and highly concentrated coffee, typically an espresso shot sweetened with demerara sugar that's whipped with the first few drops of espresso to create a creamy 'espumita' foam. It's known for its bold flavor and rich sweetness.

name: Coffee, macchiato
description: An espresso 'marked' with a small dollop of foamed milk. It's a strong, concentrated coffee drink that highlights the espresso's flavor, softened slightly by the creamy milk.

name: Coffee, macchiato, sweetened
description: A classic espresso macchiato, 'marked' with a dollop of foamed milk, but with added sweetness. This version offers a delightful balance of strong coffee flavor and a touch of sugary indulgence.

name: Coffee, cafe con leche
description: A popular Latin American coffee drink consisting of strong brewed coffee (often espresso) mixed with steamed milk. It's a comforting and creamy beverage, typically served hot and often sweetened.

name: Coffee, cafe con leche, decaffeinated
description: A comforting and creamy Latin American coffee drink, featuring strong decaffeinated coffee blended with steamed milk. It offers the beloved taste and warmth of cafe con leche without the stimulating effects of caffeine.

name: Coffee, Latte
description: A popular coffee beverage made with espresso and a generous amount of steamed milk, topped with a thin layer of foamed milk. Its creamy texture and balanced coffee flavor make it a comforting and widely enjoyed drink.

name: Coffee, Latte, nonfat
description: A lighter version of the classic latte, made with espresso and steamed nonfat milk, topped with a thin layer of foam. It offers the same comforting creaminess and coffee flavor with fewer calories and less fat.

name: Coffee, Latte, with non-dairy milk
description: A creamy and comforting latte made with espresso and a non-dairy milk alternative, such as almond, soy, or oat milk. It offers a delicious option for those avoiding dairy, with a unique flavor profile from the plant-based milk.

name: Coffee, Latte, flavored
description: A delightful variation of the classic latte, infused with sweet syrups like vanilla, caramel, or hazelnut. These flavored lattes offer a comforting blend of espresso, steamed milk, and a burst of additional sweetness and aroma.

name: Coffee, Latte, nonfat, flavored
description: A lighter, yet indulgent, latte featuring espresso, steamed nonfat milk, and a sweet flavor syrup. It provides the comforting creaminess and aromatic taste of a flavored latte with reduced fat content.

name: Coffee, Latte, with non-dairy milk, flavored
description: A delicious and dairy-free latte, combining espresso with a non-dairy milk alternative and a sweet flavor syrup. It offers a customized, aromatic, and creamy coffee experience for those with dietary preferences.

name: Coffee, Latte, decaffeinated
description: A comforting and creamy latte made with decaffeinated espresso and steamed milk, topped with a thin layer of foam. It offers the beloved taste and texture of a classic latte without the stimulating effects of caffeine.

name: Coffee, Latte, decaffeinated, nonfat
description: A lighter, caffeine-free version of the classic latte, made with decaffeinated espresso and steamed nonfat milk. It provides a comforting and creamy coffee experience with reduced fat and no caffeine.

name: Frozen coffee drink, nonfat
description: A refreshing and lighter version of a blended coffee beverage, made with coffee, ice, nonfat milk, and often sweeteners or flavorings. It offers a cool, creamy, and invigorating treat with reduced fat content.

name: Frozen coffee drink, with non-dairy milk
description:
A frosty, invigorating blend of coffee, ice, and creamy non-dairy milk, perfect for a refreshing pick-me-up.

Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup strong brewed coffee, chilled
- 1/2 cup non-dairy milk
- 2 tbsp sugar (or to taste)
- 1.5 cups ice cubes

Instructions:
1. Combine chilled coffee, non-dairy milk, sugar, and ice in a blender.
2. Blend until smooth and frosty.
3. Pour into a glass and serve immediately.

description:
A cool and creamy decaffeinated frozen coffee, made with your favorite non-dairy milk for a smooth, satisfying, and caffeine-free treat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup strong decaffeinated brewed coffee, chilled
- 1/2 cup non-dairy milk
- 2 tbsp sugar (or to taste)
- 1.5 cups ice cubes

Instructions:
1. Combine chilled decaffeinated coffee, non-dairy milk, sugar, and ice in a blender.
2. Blend until smooth and frosty.
3. Pour into a glass and serve immediately.

name: Coffee, Cafe Mocha
description:
A classic coffeehouse favorite, blending rich espresso with decadent chocolate syrup and steamed milk, topped with a delicate layer of foam.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 shot (1 oz) espresso
- 1-2 tbsp chocolate syrup
- 6-8 oz steamed milk

Instructions:
1. Pour chocolate syrup into a mug.
2. Add freshly brewed espresso and stir to combine.
3. Steam milk until hot and frothy.
4. Pour steamed milk over the coffee mixture.
5. Top with a thin layer of foam and serve.

name: Coffee, Cappuccino
description:
An iconic Italian coffee drink, featuring equal parts espresso, steamed milk, and a generous cap of frothed milk, often dusted with cocoa.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 shot (1 oz) espresso
- 4-5 oz milk

Instructions:
1. Brew a shot of espresso into a cappuccino cup.
2. Steam milk until hot and frothy, aiming for equal parts steamed milk and foam.
3. Pour steamed milk over the espresso, holding back the foam initially, then spooning a generous cap of foam on top.
4. Serve immediately.

- Ice for serving

Instructions:
1. Rinse the rice thoroughly. In a bowl, combine the rinsed rice, 2 cups of water, and the cinnamon stick. Let it soak at room temperature for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight.
2. Transfer the rice, cinnamon stick, and soaking water to a blender. Add the remaining 2 cups of water. Blend on high until the rice is completely pulverized and the mixture is milky, about 2-3 minutes.
3. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a pitcher, pressing down on the solids to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard the solids.
4. Stir in the sugar and vanilla extract (if using) until the sugar is fully dissolved.
5. Chill thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving. Serve over ice.

name: Horchata, made with milk
description:
A creamy, refreshing Latin American beverage made from rice, milk, cinnamon, and vanilla, often served chilled.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes active, 4+ hours soaking/chilling

Ingredients:
- 1 cup white rice
- 4 cups water
- 1/2 cup milk (or more to taste)
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar (or to taste)
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract

Instructions:
1. 1. Rinse rice and soak with water and cinnamon stick for at least 4 hours or overnight.
2. 2. Blend the rice, water, and cinnamon stick until smooth.
3. 3. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth.
4. 4. Stir in milk, sugar, and vanilla extract.
5. 5. Chill thoroughly before serving over ice.

name: Frescavena
description:
A popular, comforting Latin American drink, often made with oats, milk, cinnamon, and sugar, served either warm or cold.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rolled oats
- 3 cups water
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 cup sugar (or to taste)
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract

Instructions:
1. 1. Combine oats, water, and cinnamon stick in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes until oats are soft.
2. 2. Remove cinnamon stick. Let cool slightly.
3. 3. Blend the oat mixture until smooth.
4. 4. Stir in milk, sugar, and vanilla extract. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Atole de avena
description:
A warm, thick, and comforting Mexican beverage made from oats, milk, piloncillo (or brown sugar), and cinnamon, perfect for a chilly morning.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup rolled oats
- 4 cups water
- 1 cup milk
- 1/4 cup piloncillo (or brown sugar)
- 1 cinnamon stick
- pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. 1. Combine oats, water, piloncillo, cinnamon stick, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oats are very soft and mixture thickens.
2. 2. Remove cinnamon stick.
3. 3. Stir in milk and continue to cook for another 5 minutes, ensuring it doesn't boil over.
4. 4. Serve warm.

name: Sugar cane beverage
description:
A naturally sweet and refreshing drink extracted directly from sugar cane stalks, often served with a squeeze of lime or ginger.

3. 3. Using a juicer designed for sugar cane (or a very powerful juicer), extract the juice.
4. 4. Strain the juice to remove any fibrous bits.
5. 5. Serve immediately over ice, with a squeeze of fresh lime juice if desired.

name: Atole
description:
A traditional warm, thick, and nourishing Mexican drink, often made with masa (corn dough), water or milk, and sweetened with piloncillo or sugar, flavored with cinnamon or vanilla.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup masa harina
- 4 cups water
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 cup piloncillo (or brown sugar)
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract

Instructions:
1. 1. In a saucepan, whisk masa harina with 1 cup of water until smooth.
2. 2. Add remaining water, milk, piloncillo, and cinnamon stick to the saucepan.
3. 3. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly to prevent lumps, until thickened (about 10-15 minutes).
4. 4. Remove cinnamon stick. Stir in vanilla extract.
5. 5. Serve warm.

name: Atole de chocolate
description:
A rich and comforting Mexican hot chocolate, thickened with masa harina, spiced with cinnamon, and sweetened, offering a unique creamy texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/4 cup masa harina
- 4 cups milk
- 1/4 cup piloncillo (or brown sugar)
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 2 oz Mexican chocolate (or unsweetened cocoa powder + more sugar)

Instructions:
1. 1. In a small bowl, whisk masa harina with 1/2 cup of the milk until smooth. Set aside.
2. 2. In a saucepan, combine remaining milk, piloncillo, cinnamon stick, and Mexican chocolate. Heat over medium heat, stirring until chocolate and piloncillo dissolve.
3. 3. Slowly whisk in the masa harina mixture.
4. 4. Continue to cook, whisking constantly, until the atole thickens to your desired consistency (about 10-15 minutes).
5. 5. Remove cinnamon stick and serve warm.

Ingredients:
- 1 (750ml) bottle dry red wine
- 1/4 cup brandy

A warm and aromatic Scandinavian mulled wine, spiced with cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and ginger, often fortified with spirits and served with raisins and almonds.

Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (750ml) bottle red wine
- 1/2 cup brandy (or vodka)

name: Desserts, flan, caramel custard, prepared-from-recipe
description:
A silky-smooth baked custard topped with a glistening layer of golden caramel, flan is a classic dessert known for its elegant simplicity and rich, sweet flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 1/4 cup water
- 4 large eggs
- 1 (14 oz) can sweetened condensed milk
- 1 (12 oz) can evaporated milk
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. In a small saucepan, combine 1 cup sugar and 1/4 cup water. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar dissolves and mixture turns a golden amber caramel. Pour immediately into a 9-inch round baking dish or 6 ramekins, tilting to coat the bottom.
3. In a large bowl, whisk eggs. Gradually whisk in sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, and vanilla extract until smooth.
4. Pour the custard mixture over the caramel in the baking dish/ramekins.
5. Place the baking dish/ramekins in a larger baking pan. Fill the larger pan with hot water to reach halfway up the sides of the flan dish(es) (water bath).
6. Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center still jiggles slightly. A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.
7. Carefully remove from water bath and let cool completely on a wire rack. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight.
8. To serve, run a knife around the edge of the flan, then invert onto a serving plate.

Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 cup butter

- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions:

5. Let cool completely at room temperature, then cut into squares.

5. Let cool completely at room temperature (several hours or overnight), then use the foil to lift the fudge out of the pan and cut into squares.

name: Moose, liver, braised (Alaska Native)
description:
Tender and rich, braised moose liver, a traditional Alaska Native dish, is slow-cooked to perfection, offering a distinct, earthy flavor and a nutrient-dense meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb moose liver, sliced
- 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil (e.g., canola or bear fat)
- 1 large onion, sliced
- 2 cups beef or game broth

Instructions:
1. Pat moose liver slices dry. In a shallow dish, combine flour, salt, and pepper. Dredge liver slices in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
2. Heat cooking oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear liver slices in batches until browned on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove liver and set aside.
3. Add sliced onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Pour in broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
5. Return liver slices to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 30-45 minutes, or until liver is tender and cooked through. Serve hot.

description: White-winged scoter duck meat, a traditional food for Alaska Natives, is a dark, flavorful wild game bird, offering a unique taste of the Alaskan wilderness.

name: Sea cucumber, yane (Alaska Native)
description: Yane sea cucumber, a traditional marine food for Alaska Natives, is known for its unique texture and subtle oceanic flavor, often consumed for its nutritional value.

name: Squirrel, ground, meat (Alaska Native)
description: Ground squirrel meat, a traditional food source for Alaska Natives, is a lean and flavorful wild game, often used in stews or other preparations.

name: Tea, tundra, herb and laborador combination (Alaska Native)
description:
A traditional Alaska Native beverage, this tundra tea combines various wild herbs, including Labrador tea, to create an aromatic and earthy infusion with potential medicinal properties.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon dried tundra herbs and Labrador tea leaves (or a tea bag blend)
- 1 cup hot water

Instructions:
1. Place the dried herbs/tea leaves in a mug.
2. Pour hot (not boiling) water over the herbs.
3. Steep for 5-10 minutes, or to desired strength.
4. Strain out the herbs (if using loose leaf) and enjoy. Sweeten with honey if desired.

name: Walrus, meat, dried (Alaska Native)
description: Dried walrus meat, a traditional and essential food for Alaska Natives, is a highly concentrated source of protein, offering a chewy texture and robust, savory flavor.

name: Deer (venison), sitka, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Lean and tender, raw Sitka venison is a prized wild game meat for Alaska Natives, offering a distinct, earthy flavor, ready for various traditional culinary uses.

name: Whale, bowhead, subcutaneous fat (blubber) (Alaska Native)
description: Bowhead whale blubber, a vital traditional food for Alaska Natives, is a rich source of energy and nutrients, offering a unique texture and flavor, often consumed raw.

name: Whale, bowhead, skin and subcutaneous fat (muktuk) (Alaska Native)
description: Muktuk, consisting of bowhead whale skin and blubber, is a highly esteemed traditional food for Alaska Natives, known for its chewy texture and rich, distinct flavor, often eaten raw or frozen.

name: Oil, whale, bowhead (Alaska Native)
description: Bowhead whale oil, a traditional and essential energy source for Alaska Natives, is rich in vital nutrients and offers a distinct flavor, deeply rooted in cultural practices.

name: Fish, whitefish, broad, liver (Alaska Native)
description: Broad whitefish liver, a nutrient-rich delicacy for Alaska Natives, offers a distinct flavor and is valued for its traditional dietary importance and health benefits.

name: Mush, blue corn with ash (Navajo)
description:
A traditional Navajo staple, blue corn mush with ash is a hearty and nutritious porridge made from ground blue corn and wood ash, offering a unique earthy flavor and cultural significance.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup blue cornmeal
- 4 cups water
- 1 tablespoon juniper ash (or food-grade hardwood ash)
- Pinch of salt (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, combine blue cornmeal and water. Stir well to prevent lumps.
2. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring frequently, for 20-30 minutes, or until thickened to a porridge consistency.
3. In a small bowl, mix juniper ash with a few tablespoons of water to create a slurry.
4. Stir the ash slurry into the simmering corn mush. Continue to cook for another 5-10 minutes, stirring, until the mush turns a deeper blue/purple color and is fully cooked.
5. Add a pinch of salt if desired. Serve warm, often with milk or honey.

name: Cornmeal, blue (Navajo)
description: Finely ground from dried blue corn, Navajo blue cornmeal is a culturally significant ingredient, prized for its distinct color, earthy flavor, and nutritional value in traditional dishes.

name: Melon, banana (Navajo)
description: A unique variety of melon cultivated by the Navajo, the banana melon offers a sweet, aromatic flesh with a flavor reminiscent of bananas, making it a refreshing and traditional fruit.

name: Chilchen (Red Berry Beverage) (Navajo)
description:
Chilchen, a traditional Navajo red berry beverage, is a refreshing and tart drink made from wild red berries, often sweetened, offering a taste of the natural landscape.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups fresh or frozen wild red berries (e.g., chokecherries, currants)
- 4 cups water
- Sugar or honey to taste (optional)

Instructions:
1. Wash berries thoroughly. In a saucepan, combine berries and water.
2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until berries are soft and have released their color.
3. Mash the berries gently with a spoon or potato masher to extract more juice.
4. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth, pressing on the solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
5. Sweeten the liquid with sugar or honey to taste, if desired. Serve chilled or warm.

name: Corn, dried (Navajo)
description: A fundamental staple in Navajo cuisine, dried corn is preserved for long-term storage and use, offering a concentrated corn flavor and a chewy texture once rehydrated and cooked.

name: Squash, Indian, cooked, boiled (Navajo)
description:
Boiled Indian squash, a traditional Navajo vegetable, offers a tender texture and mild, earthy sweetness, serving as a comforting and nutritious side dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 medium Indian squash (or similar winter squash like butternut or acorn)
- 4 cups water
- Pinch of salt (optional)

Instructions:
1. Wash the squash thoroughly. Carefully cut the squash in half, scoop out seeds and fibrous bits.
2. Cut the squash into manageable pieces (e.g., 1-inch cubes or wedges).
3. Place squash pieces in a large pot and cover with water. Add a pinch of salt if desired.
4. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-25 minutes, or until the squash is fork-tender.
5. Drain the water and serve hot. Can be mashed or served as chunks.

name: Bread, kneel down (Navajo)
description:
Kneel down bread, or 'to'oshjeeh,' is a traditional Navajo steamed corn bread, made from fresh ground corn, often wrapped in corn husks, offering a sweet, moist, and dense texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 30 minutes (plus grinding/rehydration time)

Ingredients:
- 4 cups fresh corn kernels (or 2 cups dried corn, rehydrated and ground)
- 1/2 cup blue cornmeal (optional, for color/texture)
- 1/4 cup vegetable shortening or lard (optional)
- Salt to taste
- Corn husks for wrapping

Instructions:
1. If using fresh corn, grind it into a coarse meal. If using dried corn, rehydrate overnight and then grind.
2. In a large bowl, combine the ground corn, blue cornmeal (if using), shortening/lard (if using), and salt. Mix well to form a thick dough. Add a little water if too dry, or more cornmeal if too wet.
3. Take a handful of dough and shape it into a small log or patty. Wrap each piece tightly in a corn husk, tying the ends with strips of husk or string.
4. Arrange the wrapped breads in a steamer basket. Steam over boiling water for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until firm and cooked through.
5. Serve warm, unwrapped.

name: Mutton, cooked, roasted (Navajo)
description:
Roasted mutton, a cornerstone of Navajo cuisine, is slow-cooked to tender perfection, offering a rich, savory, and deeply satisfying flavor, often seasoned simply to highlight the meat's natural taste.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 3-4 lb mutton roast (e.g., leg or shoulder)
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil or lard
- 2 teaspoons salt
- 1 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 onion, quartered (optional)
- 2 cloves garlic, smashed (optional)
- 1 cup water or broth

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
2. Pat the mutton roast dry. Rub with cooking oil/lard, then season generously with salt and pepper.
3. Place the roast in a large roasting pan. Add onion and garlic around the roast if desired. Pour water or broth into the bottom of the pan.
4. Roast for 2-3 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C) for medium-rare, or 160°F (71°C) for medium, or 170°F (77°C) for well-done. Baste occasionally with pan juices.
5. Remove from oven, tent with foil, and let rest for 15-20 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Frybread, made with lard (Navajo)
description:
A beloved staple of Navajo cuisine, frybread made with lard is a golden, puffy, and irresistibly chewy flatbread, deep-fried to perfection, offering a slightly savory taste and a comforting texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 pieces
Prep Time: 45 minutes (including rest time)

Ingredients:
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tablespoon baking powder
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 cup warm water (or more as needed)
- 1/4 cup lard, melted (for dough)
- 2-3 cups lard or vegetable oil (for frying)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
2. Add melted lard to the dry ingredients, then gradually add warm water, mixing until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
3. Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
4. Heat 2-3 cups of lard or oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to 350-375°F (175-190°C).
5. Divide the dough into 10-12 equal pieces. Flatten each piece into a round or oval shape, about 1/4 inch thick. You can make a small hole in the center to ensure even cooking.
6. Carefully place 1-2 pieces of frybread into the hot oil (do not overcrowd). Fry for 1-2 minutes per side, or until golden brown and puffed up.
7. Remove with tongs and drain on paper towels. Serve warm with honey, jam, or as a base for savory toppings.

name: Tamales (Navajo)
description:
Navajo tamales are a savory and comforting dish, typically made with a corn masa dough filled with seasoned meat (often mutton or beef) and sometimes green chile, steamed in corn husks for a tender, flavorful meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 tamales
Prep Time: 60 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Masa: 2 cups masa harina
- 1 1/2 cups warm water or broth
- 1/2 cup lard or vegetable shortening, softened
- 1 teaspoon salt
- For Filling: 1 lb cooked, shredded mutton or beef
- 1/2 cup green chile, chopped (optional)
- 1/2 teaspoon cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 20-25 dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Instructions:
1. Prepare the filling: Combine shredded meat, green chile (if using), cumin, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
2. Prepare the masa: In a large bowl, beat softened lard/shortening until fluffy. In a separate bowl, combine masa harina and salt. Gradually add warm water/broth to the masa harina, mixing until a soft dough forms. Add the masa dough to the fluffy lard and beat until well combined and light.
3. Spread masa: Take a soaked corn husk, pat dry. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider end of the husk, leaving a border.
4. Add filling: Place 1-2 tablespoons of filling in the center of the masa.
5. Fold tamale: Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold the narrow end up. Repeat with remaining masa and filling.
6. Steam tamales: Arrange tamales upright in a steamer basket over boiling water. Ensure water does not touch the tamales. Cover and steam for 1-1.5 hours, or until the masa is firm and pulls away easily from the husk.
7. Serve warm.

name: Stew, steamed corn (Navajo)
description:
Navajo steamed corn stew is a hearty and traditional dish, featuring tender steamed corn kernels often combined with beans, squash, and sometimes meat, creating a comforting and flavorful meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
- 1 cup cooked pinto beans
- 1 cup diced squash (e.g., zucchini or yellow squash)
- 1/2 cup diced onion
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 4 cups vegetable or chicken broth
- 1/2 lb cooked, diced mutton or beef (optional)
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 tablespoon cooking oil or lard

Instructions:
1. Heat oil/lard in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
2. Stir in corn kernels, cooked pinto beans, diced squash, and cooked meat (if using).
3. Pour in broth, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-30 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and flavors have melded. Adjust seasoning as needed.
5. Serve hot.

name: Fish, halibut, raw, with skin (Alaska Native)
description: Raw halibut with skin, a prized catch for Alaska Natives, offers firm, white flesh and a mild, sweet flavor, rich in omega-3s, ready for various traditional preparations.

name: Fish, salmon, coho (silver), raw (Alaska Native)
description: Raw Coho (Silver) salmon, a vibrant and flavorful fish for Alaska Natives, boasts firm, orange-red flesh and a delicate taste, perfect for traditional cooking methods.

name: Blueberries, wild, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Small, sweet, and bursting with flavor, raw wild blueberries from Alaska are a cherished traditional food, packed with antioxidants and offering a taste of the pristine wilderness.

name: Oil, spotted seal (Alaska Native)
description: Spotted seal oil, a traditional and essential energy source for Alaska Natives, is rich in vital nutrients and offers a distinct flavor, deeply rooted in cultural practices.

name: Fish, salmon, red, canned, bones removed (Alaska Native)

name: Fish, whitefish, eggs (Alaska Native)
description: Whitefish eggs, a delicacy for Alaska Natives, are small, delicate roe with a subtle flavor and unique texture, often consumed fresh or lightly prepared.

name: Caribou, rump meat, half dried (Alaska Native)
description: Half-dried caribou rump meat, a traditional Alaska Native food, offers a concentrated, savory flavor and a chewy texture, providing a portable and nutrient-dense protein source.

name: Fish, salmon, red, (sockeye), canned, smoked (Alaska Native)
description: Smoked and canned Sockeye (Red) salmon, a traditional Alaska Native food, delivers a rich, smoky flavor and firm, vibrant red flesh, offering a convenient and flavorful protein source.

name: Fish, salmon, red, (sockeye), kippered (Alaska Native)
description: Kippered Sockeye (Red) salmon, a traditional Alaska Native preparation, is hot-smoked to create a moist, flaky, and intensely flavorful fish with a distinctive smoky and savory taste.

name: Fish, salmon, king, with skin, kippered, (Alaska Native)
description: Kippered King salmon with skin, a prized Alaska Native delicacy, is hot-smoked to perfection, yielding a rich, buttery, and intensely flavorful fish with a tender, flaky texture.

name: Fish, sheefish, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Raw sheefish, a large freshwater fish prized by Alaska Natives, offers firm, white flesh with a mild, delicate flavor, suitable for various traditional cooking methods.

name: Buffalo, free range, top round steak, raw (Shoshone Bannock)
description: Lean and robust, raw free-range buffalo top round steak, a traditional food for the Shoshone Bannock, offers a rich, slightly sweet game flavor, ready for cooking.

name: Seal, bearded (Oogruk), meat, partially dried (Alaska Native)
description: Partially dried bearded seal (Oogruk) meat, a traditional Alaska Native food, offers a concentrated, savory flavor and a chewy texture, providing a portable and nutrient-dense protein source.

name: Buffalo, free range, top round steak, cooked (Shoshone Bannock)
description:
Cooked free-range buffalo top round steak, a traditional Shoshone Bannock food, is lean, tender, and boasts a rich, slightly sweet game flavor, offering a hearty and nutritious meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb free-range buffalo top round steak
- 1 tablespoon olive oil or lard
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions:
1. Pat the buffalo steak dry with paper towels.
2. Rub both sides of the steak with olive oil/lard, then season generously with salt and pepper.
3. Heat a cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until very hot.
4. Sear the steak for 3-5 minutes per side for medium-rare (internal temperature 130-135°F / 54-57°C), or longer for desired doneness. Buffalo cooks faster than beef due to its leanness.
5. Remove steak from pan, tent loosely with foil, and let rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing against the grain and serving.

name: Elk, free range, roast, eye of round, raw (Shoshone Bannock)
description: Raw free-range elk eye of round roast, a prized wild game for the Shoshone Bannock, is exceptionally lean and offers a mild, earthy game flavor, ideal for roasting.

name: Corn, dried, yellow (Northern Plains Indians)
description: A staple food for Northern Plains Indians, dried yellow corn is preserved for long-term use, offering a concentrated sweet corn flavor and a chewy texture once rehydrated and cooked.

name: Smelt, dried (Alaska Native)
description: Dried smelt, a traditional Alaska Native food, are small, flavorful fish preserved through drying, offering a concentrated savory taste and a chewy texture, often eaten as a snack.

name: Frybread, made with lard (Apache)
description:
A cherished staple of Apache cuisine, frybread made with lard is a golden, fluffy, and satisfyingly chewy flatbread, deep-fried to perfection, offering a slightly savory taste and comforting texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 pieces
Prep Time: 45 minutes (including rest time)

Ingredients:
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tablespoon baking powder
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 cup warm water (or more as needed)
- 1/4 cup lard, melted (for dough)
- 2-3 cups lard or vegetable oil (for frying)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
2. Add melted lard to the dry ingredients, then gradually add warm water, mixing until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
3. Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
4. Heat 2-3 cups of lard or oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to 350-375°F (175-190°C).
5. Divide the dough into 10-12 equal pieces. Flatten each piece into a round or oval shape, about 1/4 inch thick. You can make a small hole in the center to ensure even cooking.
6. Carefully place 1-2 pieces of frybread into the hot oil (do not overcrowd). Fry for 1-2 minutes per side, or until golden brown and puffed up.
7. Remove with tongs and drain on paper towels. Serve warm with honey, jam, or as a base for savory toppings.

name: Corned beef and potatoes in tortilla (Apache)
description:
A hearty and flavorful Apache dish, this combines savory corned beef and tender potatoes, often seasoned and wrapped in a warm tortilla, creating a satisfying and portable meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-5
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb corned beef, cooked and shredded or diced
- 2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1/2 onion, diced
- 2 tablespoons cooking oil or lard
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 8-10 flour tortillas

Instructions:
1. Heat oil/lard in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced potatoes and onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and lightly browned, about 10-15 minutes.
2. Stir in cooked corned beef. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
3. Warm tortillas according to package directions (microwave, skillet, or oven).
4. Spoon the corned beef and potato mixture into the center of each warm tortilla. Fold or roll up and serve immediately.

name: Restaurant, Mexican, soft taco with ground beef, cheese and lettuce
description:
A classic Mexican-American favorite, this soft taco features seasoned ground beef, shredded cheese, and crisp lettuce, all nestled in a warm, pliable flour tortilla for a satisfying bite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-5
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground beef
- 1 packet taco seasoning
- 1/2 cup water
- 8-10 soft flour tortillas
- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- 1 cup shredded lettuce
- Optional: diced tomatoes, sour cream, salsa

Instructions:
1. Brown ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it apart as it cooks. Drain any excess fat.
2. Stir in taco seasoning and water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until liquid has mostly evaporated and beef is well seasoned.
3. Warm tortillas according to package directions (microwave, skillet, or oven).
4. Assemble tacos: Place a spoonful of seasoned ground beef in the center of each warm tortilla. Top with shredded cheese and lettuce. Add optional toppings as desired.
5. Serve immediately.

name: Restaurant, Latino, chicken and rice, entree, prepared
description:
A comforting and flavorful staple in Latino cuisine, this prepared chicken and rice entree features tender chicken pieces simmered with rice, often with vegetables and aromatic spices, creating a hearty and complete meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 onion, diced
- 1 bell pepper (any color), diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup long-grain white rice
- 2 cups chicken broth
- 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
2. Add onion and bell pepper to the pot and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in rice, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until rice is lightly toasted.
4. Pour in chicken broth and tomato sauce. Bring to a boil, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Return chicken to the pot.
5. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
6. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Restaurant, Latino, empanadas, beef, prepared
description:
Savory and satisfying, these prepared Latino beef empanadas feature a flavorful ground beef filling, often seasoned with spices and vegetables, encased in a tender, flaky pastry crust, then baked or fried to golden perfection.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12-15 empanadas
Prep Time: 60 minutes (plus chilling time)

Ingredients:
- For Filling: 1 lb ground beef
- 1/2 onion, finely diced
- 1/2 bell pepper, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup tomato sauce
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon paprika
- Salt and pepper to taste
- For Dough: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cubed
- 1/2 cup ice water (approx.)
- 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash, if baking)
- Vegetable oil (if frying)

Instructions:
1. Prepare filling: Brown ground beef in a skillet, drain fat. Add onion, bell pepper, and garlic; cook until softened. Stir in tomato sauce, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 10-15 minutes until flavors meld and liquid reduces. Let cool completely.
2. Prepare dough: In a large bowl, whisk flour and salt. Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add ice water, mixing until a dough forms. Knead briefly, then flatten into a disk, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
3. Assemble empanadas: Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to 1/8-inch thickness. Cut out 4-5 inch circles. Place a spoonful of cooled filling on one half of each circle. Moisten edges with water, fold the other half over, and crimp edges with a fork to seal.
4. Cook empanadas: To bake: Place on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown. To fry: Heat 2-3 inches of oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry empanadas in batches for 3-5 minutes per side, until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
5. Serve warm.

name: Restaurant, Latino, pupusas con frijoles (pupusas, bean)
description:
A beloved Salvadoran specialty, pupusas con frijoles are thick, handmade corn tortillas generously stuffed with savory refried beans, then griddled until golden and slightly crispy, offering a comforting and flavorful bite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 pupusas
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Masa: 2 cups masa harina
- 1 1/2 cups warm water (approx.)
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (for hands)
- For Filling: 1 cup refried beans (thick consistency)

Instructions:
1. Prepare masa: In a large bowl, combine masa harina and salt. Gradually add warm water, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. It should be moist but not sticky. Knead for a few minutes. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
2. Prepare filling: Ensure refried beans are thick and cooled.
3. Assemble pupusas: Lightly oil your hands. Take a golf-ball sized piece of masa dough and roll it into a ball. Flatten it slightly in your palm to form a thick disc. Make an indentation in the center and place about 1 tablespoon of refried beans.
4. Carefully bring the edges of the masa up and over the filling, sealing it completely. Gently flatten the ball back into a disc, about 1/2 inch thick, ensuring the filling is evenly distributed.
5. Cook pupusas: Heat a comal or non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook pupusas for 4-6 minutes per side, or until golden brown and slightly puffed. Serve immediately with curtido (pickled cabbage slaw) and salsa roja.

name: Restaurant, Latino, pupusas con queso (pupusas, cheese)
description:
A delightful Salvadoran classic, pupusas con queso are thick, handmade corn tortillas generously filled with gooey, melted cheese, then griddled until golden and slightly crispy, offering a warm, cheesy indulgence.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 pupusas
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Masa: 2 cups masa harina
- 1 1/2 cups warm water (approx.)
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (for hands)
- For Filling: 1 1/2 cups shredded cheese (e.g., mozzarella, Oaxaca, or a blend)

Instructions:
1. Prepare masa: In a large bowl, combine masa harina and salt. Gradually add warm water, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. It should be moist but not sticky. Knead for a few minutes. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
2. Assemble pupusas: Lightly oil your hands. Take a golf-ball sized piece of masa dough and roll it into a ball. Flatten it slightly in your palm to form a thick disc. Make an indentation in the center and place about 1 tablespoon of shredded cheese.
3. Carefully bring the edges of the masa up and over the filling, sealing it completely. Gently flatten the ball back into a disc, about 1/2 inch thick, ensuring the filling is evenly distributed.
4. Cook pupusas: Heat a comal or non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook pupusas for 4-6 minutes per side, or until golden brown and slightly puffed, and the cheese is melted and gooey. Serve immediately with curtido (pickled cabbage slaw) and salsa roja.

name: Restaurant, Latino, pupusas del cerdo (pupusas, pork)
description:
A hearty Salvadoran favorite, pupusas del cerdo are thick, handmade corn tortillas generously stuffed with seasoned, tender cooked pork, then griddled until golden and slightly crispy, offering a rich and savory experience.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8 pupusas
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Masa: 2 cups masa harina
- 1 1/2 cups warm water (approx.)
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (for hands)
- For Filling: 1 cup cooked, shredded pork (e.g., carnitas or slow-cooked pork shoulder), seasoned with salt, pepper, and a pinch of cumin

Instructions:
1. Prepare masa: In a large bowl, combine masa harina and salt. Gradually add warm water, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. It should be moist but not sticky. Knead for a few minutes. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
2. Assemble pupusas: Lightly oil your hands. Take a golf-ball sized piece of masa dough and roll it into a ball. Flatten it slightly in your palm to form a thick disc. Make an indentation in the center and place about 1 tablespoon of seasoned shredded pork.
3. Carefully bring the edges of the masa up and over the filling, sealing it completely. Gently flatten the ball back into a disc, about 1/2 inch thick, ensuring the filling is evenly distributed.
4. Cook pupusas: Heat a comal or non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook pupusas for 4-6 minutes per side, or until golden brown and slightly puffed. Serve immediately with curtido (pickled cabbage slaw) and salsa roja.

name: Restaurant, Latino, tamale, corn
description:
A classic Latino comfort food, corn tamales feature a sweet or savory corn masa dough, often filled with cheese, vegetables, or a hint of spice, all steamed in corn husks for a moist and tender texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 tamales
Prep Time: 60 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Masa: 2 cups masa harina
- 1 1/2 cups warm vegetable broth or water
- 1/2 cup vegetable shortening or lard, softened
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
- For Filling: 1 cup fresh or frozen corn kernels
- 1/2 cup shredded cheese (e.g., Monterey Jack)
- 1/4 cup chopped green chiles (optional)
- 20-25 dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Instructions:
1. Prepare filling: Combine corn kernels, shredded cheese, and green chiles (if using). Set aside.
2. Prepare masa: In a large bowl, beat softened shortening/lard until fluffy. In a separate bowl, combine masa harina, salt, and baking powder. Gradually add warm broth/water to the masa harina, mixing until a soft dough forms. Add the masa dough to the fluffy shortening and beat until well combined and light.
3. Spread masa: Take a soaked corn husk, pat dry. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider end of the husk, leaving a border.
4. Add filling: Place 1-2 tablespoons of filling in the center of the masa.
5. Fold tamale: Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold the narrow end up. Repeat with remaining masa and filling.
6. Steam tamales: Arrange tamales upright in a steamer basket over boiling water. Ensure water does not touch the tamales. Cover and steam for 1-1.5 hours, or until the masa is firm and pulls away easily from the husk.
7. Serve warm.

name: Restaurant, Mexican, spanish rice
description:
A vibrant and flavorful side dish, Mexican Spanish rice is made with long-grain rice cooked in a tomato-based broth with onions, garlic, and spices, resulting in fluffy, reddish-orange grains perfect for complementing any Mexican meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
- 1 cup long-grain white rice
- 1/2 onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce
- 2 cups chicken or vegetable broth
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon chili powder (optional)
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat vegetable oil in a medium saucepan or pot over medium heat. Add rice and cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden brown.
2. Add onion and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes. Add garlic and frozen mixed vegetables; stir-fry for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in tomato sauce, broth, cumin, chili powder (if using), and salt. Bring to a boil.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
5. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Restaurant, Mexican, refried beans
description:
A creamy and savory staple of Mexican cuisine, refried beans are made from cooked pinto beans that are mashed and then fried with lard or oil, often seasoned with onion, garlic, and spices, creating a rich and comforting side dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons lard or vegetable oil
- 1/4 cup finely diced onion
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 (15 oz) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
- 1/2 cup water or chicken broth
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- Salt to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat lard/oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
2. Add drained pinto beans, water/broth, and cumin to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
3. Using a potato masher or fork, mash the beans to your desired consistency (chunky or smooth).
4. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the beans are heated through and have thickened, about 5-10 minutes. Season with salt to taste.
5. Serve hot as a side dish or filling.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, egg rolls, assorted
description:
Crispy on the outside and savory within, assorted Chinese egg rolls are deep-fried appetizers filled with a variety of ingredients like shredded cabbage, carrots, and seasoned meat or vegetables, offering a delightful crunch and flavorful bite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 16-20 egg rolls
Prep Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground pork or chicken (optional)
- 2 cups shredded cabbage
- 1 cup shredded carrots
- 1/2 cup chopped green onions
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon sesame oil
- 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 package (16-20 count) egg roll wrappers
- 4 cups vegetable oil (for frying)

Instructions:
1. If using meat, brown ground pork/chicken in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Drain fat. Add cabbage, carrots, green onions, garlic, and ginger. Cook until vegetables are tender-crisp, about 5-7 minutes.
2. Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil, and black pepper. Cook for 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
3. Lay an egg roll wrapper on a clean surface with a corner pointing towards you. Place about 2 tablespoons of filling just below the center. Fold the bottom corner over the filling, then fold in the side corners. Roll tightly upwards to form a cylinder. Moisten the top corner with water to seal.
4. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C).
5. Carefully place 3-4 egg rolls into the hot oil (do not overcrowd). Fry for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Remove with tongs and drain on paper towels.
6. Serve hot with dipping sauce.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, fried rice, without meat
description:
A classic Chinese comfort food, this meatless fried rice features fluffy rice stir-fried with scrambled egg, mixed vegetables (like peas, carrots, and corn), soy sauce, and sesame oil, creating a savory and satisfying dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided
- 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
- 4 cups cold cooked white rice (day-old rice works best)
- 1 cup mixed frozen vegetables (peas, carrots, corn)
- 1/2 onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 3 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon sesame oil
- 1/4 cup chopped green onions (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in beaten eggs and scramble until just set. Remove eggs from wok and set aside.
2. Add remaining 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil to the wok. Add diced onion and cook for 2-3 minutes until softened. Add garlic and frozen mixed vegetables; stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
3. Add cold cooked rice to the wok. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes, ensuring rice is heated through and slightly toasted.
4. Return scrambled eggs to the wok. Pour in soy sauce and sesame oil. Stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes until everything is well combined and heated through.
5. Garnish with chopped green onions and serve hot.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, lemon chicken
description:
A popular Chinese-American dish, lemon chicken features crispy, battered chicken pieces tossed in a sweet and tangy lemon sauce, offering a delightful balance of flavors and textures.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Chicken: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 1/4 cup water
- 3 cups vegetable oil (for frying)
- For Sauce: 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice
- 2 tablespoons sugar
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch
- 1 teaspoon lemon zest

Instructions:
1. Prepare chicken: In a bowl, whisk together cornstarch, flour, salt, and pepper. In another bowl, whisk egg and water. Dip chicken pieces first in the egg mixture, then dredge in the flour mixture, ensuring they are fully coated. Set aside.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C). Fry chicken in batches for 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
3. Prepare sauce: In a small saucepan, whisk together chicken broth, lemon juice, sugar, soy sauce, and cornstarch until smooth. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and becomes clear, about 3-5 minutes. Stir in lemon zest.
4. Combine: Add the fried chicken to the sauce and toss gently to coat. Serve immediately, often with steamed rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, general tso's chicken
description:
A beloved Chinese-American classic, General Tso's chicken features crispy, deep-fried chicken pieces coated in a sticky, sweet, savory, and slightly spicy sauce, often with a hint of ginger and garlic.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 35 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Chicken: 1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 3 cups vegetable oil (for frying)
- For Sauce: 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 tablespoons rice vinegar
- 2 tablespoons sugar
- 1 tablespoon hoisin sauce
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (or to taste)
- Optional: green onions and sesame seeds for garnish

Instructions:
1. Prepare chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with beaten egg. In another bowl, whisk cornstarch, flour, and salt. Dredge chicken pieces in the flour mixture, ensuring they are fully coated. Set aside.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C). Fry chicken in batches for 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
3. Prepare sauce: In a small saucepan, whisk together chicken broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, hoisin sauce, cornstarch, ginger, garlic, and red pepper flakes until smooth. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and becomes clear, about 3-5 minutes.
4. Combine: Add the fried chicken to the sauce and toss gently to coat. Serve immediately, garnished with green onions and sesame seeds if desired, often with steamed rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, kung pao chicken
description:
A spicy and savory Szechuan-inspired dish, Kung Pao chicken features diced chicken stir-fried with peanuts, vegetables (like bell peppers and zucchini), and chili peppers in a bold, flavorful sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs, diced
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch
- 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
- 1/2 cup roasted peanuts
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- 6-8 dried red chilies, whole or cut (remove seeds for less heat)
- 1/2 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 zucchini, diced
- 2 green onions, chopped
- For Sauce: 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
- 1 tablespoon hoisin sauce
- 1 tablespoon sugar
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch
- 2 tablespoons chicken broth

Instructions:
1. Marinate chicken: In a bowl, combine diced chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch. Mix well and set aside for 15 minutes.
2. Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
3. Stir-fry: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 4-6 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
4. Add peanuts, garlic, ginger, and dried red chilies to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant (be careful not to burn garlic/chilies).
5. Add red bell pepper and zucchini. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
6. Return chicken to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken and vegetables. Stir in chopped green onions.
7. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, vegetable lo mein, without meat
description:
A popular Chinese noodle dish, meatless vegetable lo mein features soft, chewy egg noodles stir-fried with a colorful assortment of fresh vegetables and a savory soy-based sauce, creating a satisfying and flavorful meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 8 oz lo mein noodles (or spaghetti)
- 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
- 1 cup sliced cabbage
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 cup sliced bell peppers (any color)
- 1 cup sliced mushrooms
- 1/2 onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- For Sauce: 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon oyster sauce (or vegetarian oyster sauce)
- 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
- 1 tablespoon sugar
- 1 teaspoon sesame oil
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch
- 2 tablespoons water
- Optional: chopped green onions for garnish

Instructions:
1. Cook lo mein noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain, rinse with cold water, and toss with a little oil to prevent sticking. Set aside.
2. Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
3. Stir-fry vegetables: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion, cabbage, carrots, bell peppers, and mushrooms. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
4. Add garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
5. Add cooked noodles to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes, ensuring noodles and vegetables are well coated and heated through.
6. Garnish with chopped green onions if desired and serve immediately.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, chicken and vegetables
description:
A wholesome and flavorful Chinese stir-fry, chicken and vegetables features tender pieces of chicken breast or thigh stir-fried with a colorful array of fresh vegetables in a light, savory sauce, offering a balanced and nutritious meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch
- 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1 cup sliced bell peppers (any color)
- 1/2 onion, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
- For Sauce: 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon oyster sauce
- 1 teaspoon sugar
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch
- 1/2 teaspoon sesame oil

Instructions:
1. Marinate chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon cornstarch. Mix well and set aside for 15 minutes.
2. Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together all sauce ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
3. Stir-fry chicken: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 4-6 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
4. Stir-fry vegetables: Add remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok. Add broccoli, carrots, bell peppers, and onion. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
5. Add garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
6. Return chicken to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken and vegetables.
7. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, orange chicken
description:
A popular Chinese-American dish, orange chicken features crispy, battered chicken pieces coated in a sweet, tangy, and slightly spicy orange-flavored sauce, often garnished with orange zest.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 35 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Chicken: 1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 3 cups vegetable oil (for frying)
- For Sauce: 1/2 cup orange juice
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tablespoons rice vinegar
- 2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon orange zest
- 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water (slurry)

Instructions:
1. Prepare chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with beaten egg. In another bowl, whisk cornstarch, flour, and salt. Dredge chicken pieces in the flour mixture, ensuring they are fully coated. Set aside.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C). Fry chicken in batches for 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
3. Prepare sauce: In a small saucepan, combine orange juice, sugar, rice vinegar, soy sauce, orange zest, ginger, garlic, and red pepper flakes (if using). Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Whisk in the cornstarch slurry and cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy, about 2-3 minutes.
4. Combine: Add the fried chicken to the sauce and toss gently to coat. Serve immediately, often with steamed rice.

name: Restaurant, Italian, spaghetti with meat sauce
description:
A timeless Italian-American classic, spaghetti with meat sauce features al dente spaghetti generously topped with a rich, slow-simmered sauce made with ground meat (beef, pork, or a mix), tomatoes, herbs, and spices, offering a hearty and comforting meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 45 minutes (plus simmering time)

Ingredients:
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 lb ground beef (or a mix of beef and pork)
- 1 onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 1 (15 oz) can tomato sauce
- 1/2 cup beef broth or red wine
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1/2 teaspoon dried basil
- 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- 1 lb spaghetti
- Grated Parmesan cheese (for serving)
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
2. Add diced onion to the pot and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth/red wine, oregano, basil, red pepper flakes (if using), salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for at least 30 minutes (preferably 1-2 hours for richer flavor), stirring occasionally.
5. While sauce simmers, cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
6. Serve spaghetti topped generously with meat sauce. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh parsley.
