name: Candies, fondant, prepared-from-recipe
description:
A smooth, pliable, and sweet confection, fondant, often used for decorating cakes or as a candy center, prepared from a classic recipe.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: Varies, yields about 1.5 lbs
Prep Time: 20 minutes active, 1 hour cooling, 24 hours ripening

Ingredients:
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- 1/2 cup water
- 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract (or other flavorings)

Instructions:
1. 1. Combine sugar, water, and cream of tartar in a saucepan. Stir over low heat until sugar dissolves.
2. 2. Increase heat and boil without stirring until the mixture reaches 238°F (114°C) on a candy thermometer (soft-ball stage).
3. 3. Remove from heat and let cool undisturbed to 110°F (43°C).
4. 4. Add vanilla extract.
5. 5. Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon or stand mixer until the mixture becomes thick, opaque, and creamy. It will go from glossy to dull.
6. 6. Knead briefly until smooth. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and let it ripen for at least 24 hours before using.

name: Candies, fudge, chocolate, prepared-from-recipe
description:
Rich, dense, and irresistibly creamy chocolate fudge, a classic homemade confection that melts in your mouth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 36 squares
Prep Time: 15 minutes active, 2 hours cooling

Ingredients:
- 3 cups granulated sugar
- 1 cup milk
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter
- 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- Pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. 1. Grease an 8x8 inch pan.
2. 2. In a large saucepan, combine sugar, milk, butter, cocoa powder, and salt.
3. 3. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
4. 4. Reduce heat to medium-low and continue to boil, stirring occasionally, until a candy thermometer reaches 234°F (112°C) (soft-ball stage).
5. 5. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract.
6. 6. Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon or electric mixer until the fudge thickens and loses its gloss (about 5-7 minutes).
7. 7. Quickly pour into the prepared pan and spread evenly. Let cool completely before cutting into squares.

name: Soup, fish, homemade (Alaska Native)
description:
A comforting and hearty homemade fish soup, a staple in Alaska Native cuisine, often featuring local fish and vegetables for a nourishing meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb white fish fillets (e.g., cod, halibut)
- 4 cups fish broth or water
- 1 onion (chopped)
- 2 carrots (chopped)
- 2 celery stalks (chopped)
- 2 potatoes (diced)
- 1/2 cup wild rice (optional)
- 1/4 cup fresh dill (chopped)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tbsp oil

Instructions:
1. 1. Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
2. 2. Add fish broth (or water) and potatoes (and wild rice if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until vegetables are tender, about 15-20 minutes.
3. 3. Cut fish fillets into 1-inch pieces. Add fish to the simmering soup and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
4. 4. Stir in fresh dill, salt, and pepper. Serve hot.

name: Stew, dumpling with mutton (Navajo)
description:
A comforting and hearty Navajo stew featuring tender mutton simmered with fluffy, savory dumplings, creating a rich and satisfying meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb mutton, cubed
- 4 cups water or broth
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup cornmeal
- 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/4 cup milk or water
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Brown mutton in a large pot. Add onion and garlic, cook until softened.
2. Pour in water or broth, bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook for 1.5-2 hours until mutton is tender.
3. For dumplings, combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Gradually add milk or water, mixing until a soft dough forms.
4. Drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering stew. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until dumplings are cooked through.
5. Serve hot.

description: A traditional Alaska Native delicacy, dried bearded seal (Oogruk) meat preserved in oil offers a rich, unique flavor and substantial energy, a vital food source.

name: Fish, whitefish, dried (Alaska Native)
description: Dried whitefish, a traditional method of preservation, provides a concentrated source of protein and nutrients, a staple food for Alaska Native communities.

name: Seal, bearded (Oogruk), meat, low quadrant, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Raw bearded seal (Oogruk) meat from the low quadrant, a traditional and highly valued food source for Alaska Natives, offering unique flavor and essential nutrients.

name: Fish, salmon, chum, dried (Alaska Native)
description: Dried chum salmon, a traditional and effective preservation method, provides a lean, flavorful, and nutrient-dense food, crucial for Alaska Native sustenance.

name: Elk, free range, ground, cooked patties (Shoshone Bannock)
description:
Lean and flavorful, these cooked patties made from free-range ground elk are a healthy and delicious staple in Shoshone Bannock cuisine, offering a taste of the wild.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground elk
- 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (optional)
- 1 small onion, finely minced (optional)
- 1 egg (optional, for binding)
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp olive oil or cooking fat

Instructions:
1. In a bowl, gently combine ground elk with breadcrumbs, minced onion, egg (if using), salt, and pepper. Do not overmix.
2. Form the mixture into 4-6 patties, about 1/2 inch thick.
3. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
4. Cook patties for 4-6 minutes per side, or until cooked through to your desired doneness (internal temperature of 160°F/71°C for well-done).
5. Serve hot.

name: Elk, free range, ground, raw (Shoshone Bannock)
description: Lean and robust, raw free-range ground elk is a versatile and healthy protein, a traditional component of Shoshone Bannock diets, ready for various culinary preparations.

name: Elk, free range, roast, eye of round, cooked (Shoshone Bannock)
description: A tender and flavorful cooked eye of round roast from free-range elk, a lean and prized cut, traditionally prepared by the Shoshone Bannock for a hearty meal.

name: Chokecherries, raw, pitted (Shoshone Bannock)
description: Tart and slightly sweet, raw pitted chokecherries are a traditional wild fruit gathered by the Shoshone Bannock, enjoyed for their unique flavor and nutritional benefits.

name: Steelhead trout, dried, flesh (Shoshone Bannock)
description: Dried steelhead trout flesh, a traditional Shoshone Bannock method of preservation, provides a concentrated source of lean protein and rich flavor, ideal for sustenance.

name: Steelhead trout, boiled, canned (Alaska Native)
description: Convenient and ready-to-eat, boiled and canned steelhead trout is a practical way for Alaska Natives to preserve and enjoy this nutritious fish, offering a mild, flaky texture.

name: Acorn stew (Apache)
description:
A deeply traditional and nourishing Apache stew, featuring the earthy richness of acorns, often combined with meat and vegetables for a hearty, culturally significant meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup acorn meal (leached)
- 4 cups water or broth
- 1/2 lb stew meat (e.g., venison, beef), cubed (optional)
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 carrot, diced
- 1 celery stalk, diced
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. If using meat, brown it in a pot. Add onion, carrot, and celery, cook until softened.
2. Stir in water or broth and bring to a simmer. Cook for 30-45 minutes if meat is used, or until vegetables are tender.
3. Gradually whisk in acorn meal, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Continue to simmer, stirring frequently, until the stew thickens to your desired consistency (about 15-20 minutes).
4. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

name: Restaurant, Italian, chicken parmesan without pasta
description:
A classic Italian-American dish featuring a breaded and fried chicken cutlet, smothered in rich marinara sauce and melted mozzarella cheese, served without pasta.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 cup breadcrumbs (Panko preferred)
- 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1/2 tsp garlic powder
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup olive oil (for frying)
- 1.5 cups marinara sauce
- 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
- Fresh basil for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Pound chicken breasts to 1/2-inch thickness.
2. Set up a breading station: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten egg, one plate with breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper.
3. Dredge each chicken breast in flour, then egg, then breadcrumb mixture, pressing to coat well.
4. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken for 3-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove and drain on paper towels.
5. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
6. Spread a thin layer of marinara sauce in an oven-safe dish. Place chicken cutlets on top, then spoon more marinara over each, and top generously with mozzarella.
7. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly. Garnish with fresh basil if desired.

name: Restaurant, Latino, arroz con leche (rice pudding)
description:
A beloved Latin American dessert, arroz con leche is a creamy, sweet rice pudding infused with cinnamon and often a hint of citrus, a comforting classic.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup short-grain rice
- 4 cups whole milk
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar (adjust to taste)
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 1 strip lemon or orange peel (optional)
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
- Ground cinnamon for garnish

Instructions:
1. Rinse rice thoroughly. In a medium saucepan, combine rice, milk, sugar, cinnamon stick, and citrus peel (if using).
2. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
3. Reduce heat to low and continue to simmer, stirring frequently, for 30-45 minutes, or until rice is tender and the pudding has thickened to a creamy consistency.
4. Remove cinnamon stick and citrus peel. Stir in vanilla extract.
5. Serve warm or chilled, garnished with ground cinnamon.

name: Restaurant, Latino, Arroz con frijoles negros (rice and black beans)
description:
A quintessential Latin American staple, Arroz con Frijoles Negros combines fluffy white rice with savory black beans, often seasoned with aromatic sofrito, a comforting and complete meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup long-grain white rice
- 2 cups water
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
- 1/2 small onion, finely chopped
- 1/2 green bell pepper, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1/4 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Cook rice: Rinse rice. In a saucepan, combine rice and water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
2. While rice cooks, prepare beans: Heat olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper, cook until softened (about 5 minutes). Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in the rinsed black beans. Add a splash of water (about 1/4 cup) if needed to create a saucy consistency. Simmer for 5-7 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
4. Season beans with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Serve the black beans over the cooked white rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro if desired.

name: Restaurant, Latino, Arroz con habichuelas colorados (Rice And Red Beans)
description:
A vibrant and hearty Latin American dish, Arroz con Habichuelas Colorados features fluffy rice paired with tender red beans, often simmered in a rich, flavorful sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup long-grain white rice
- 2 cups water
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 (15 oz) can small red beans, rinsed and drained
- 1/2 small onion, finely chopped
- 1/2 green bell pepper, finely chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1/4 tsp dried oregano
- 1/4 cup tomato sauce (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Cook rice: Rinse rice. In a saucepan, combine rice and water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
2. While rice cooks, prepare beans: Heat olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper, cook until softened (about 5 minutes). Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
3. Stir in the rinsed red beans and tomato sauce (if using). Add a splash of water (about 1/4 cup) if needed to create a saucy consistency. Simmer for 5-7 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
4. Season beans with salt and pepper to taste.
5. Serve the red beans over the cooked white rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro if desired.

name: Restaurant, Latino, Arroz con grandules (rice and pigeonpeas)
description:
A festive and flavorful Caribbean and Latin American dish, Arroz con Gandules combines seasoned rice with tender pigeon peas, often enhanced with sofrito and pork.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup long-grain white rice
- 2 cups water or chicken broth
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 (15 oz) can pigeon peas (gandules), rinsed and drained
- 1/4 cup sofrito (store-bought or homemade)
- 1/4 cup tomato sauce
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1/4 tsp dried oregano
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2-3 oz diced ham or pork belly (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a medium pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. If using ham/pork belly, cook until lightly browned.
2. Add sofrito and cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Stir in tomato sauce, cumin, and oregano, cook for another minute.
3. Add rinsed pigeon peas, rice, and water/broth. Stir well. Bring to a boil.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
5. Fluff with a fork and season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Restaurant, Latino, tamale, pork
description:
A traditional Latin American delicacy, a pork tamale features seasoned shredded pork encased in a savory masa dough, all steamed within a corn husk for a tender, flavorful bite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 tamales
Prep Time: 45 minutes (plus cooking time for pork)

Ingredients:
- For the Pork Filling:
- 1 lb pork shoulder, cubed
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (10 oz) can red enchilada sauce
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste
- For the Masa Dough:
- 2 cups masa harina
- 1.5 cups warm chicken broth
- 1/2 cup lard or vegetable shortening, softened
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- Dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Instructions:
1. Prepare pork filling: Brown pork in a pot. Add onion and garlic, cook until softened. Stir in enchilada sauce, cumin, salt, and pepper. Simmer, covered, for 1.5-2 hours until pork is very tender. Shred pork and mix back into sauce.
2. Prepare masa dough: In a large bowl, beat lard/shortening until fluffy. In another bowl, combine masa harina, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add warm broth to masa harina, mixing until combined.
3. Add masa mixture to the fluffy lard, beating until well combined and light. The dough should be spreadable.
4. Assemble tamales: Lay a softened corn husk flat. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa dough evenly over the wider end of the husk, leaving a border. Place 1-2 tablespoons of pork filling in the center of the masa.
5. Fold one side of the husk over the filling, then the other, overlapping. Fold up the bottom of the husk. Repeat with remaining ingredients.
6. Steam tamales: Arrange tamales upright in a steamer basket over boiling water. Steam for 1-1.5 hours, or until the masa pulls away easily from the husk. Serve hot.

name: Restaurant, Latino, black bean soup
description:
A rich and hearty Latin American classic, black bean soup is a flavorful blend of tender black beans, aromatic vegetables, and spices, often pureed for a creamy texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 green bell pepper, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
- 2 cups vegetable or chicken broth
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1/4 tsp dried oregano
- 1 bay leaf
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Fresh cilantro or sour cream for garnish (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper, cook until softened (about 5 minutes). Add garlic, cumin, and oregano, cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
2. Stir in black beans, broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat and cook for 15-20 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
3. Remove bay leaf. Using an immersion blender, or carefully transferring to a regular blender, blend a portion of the soup until creamy, leaving some beans whole for texture (or blend completely smooth).
4. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro or a dollop of sour cream if desired.

name: Restaurant, Latino, tripe soup
description:
A robust and traditional Latin American soup, tripe soup (often called Menudo or Mondongo) features tender tripe simmered with vegetables and spices in a rich, savory broth, a true comfort food.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus long cooking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef tripe, cleaned and cut into 1-inch pieces
- 6 cups water or beef broth
- 1 onion, quartered
- 3 cloves garlic, smashed
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1 (15 oz) can hominy, drained and rinsed (optional)
- 1/2 cup diced carrots
- 1/2 cup diced potatoes
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Lime wedges and chopped cilantro for serving

Instructions:
1. In a large pot, combine tripe, water/broth, onion, garlic, bay leaf, oregano, and cumin. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until tripe is very tender.
2. Remove onion, garlic, and bay leaf. Add hominy (if using), carrots, and potatoes to the pot. Continue to simmer for 20-30 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
3. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
4. Serve hot with lime wedges and fresh cilantro.

name: Restaurant, Latino, arepa (unleavened cornmeal bread)
description:
A versatile and beloved Latin American staple, the arepa is a thick, unleavened cornmeal patty, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, perfect for stuffing or as a side.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8 arepas
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups pre-cooked white cornmeal (masarepa)
- 2.5 cups warm water
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tbsp oil (for cooking)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine masarepa and salt. Gradually add warm water, mixing with your hands until a soft, pliable dough forms. Knead for a few minutes until smooth. Let rest for 5 minutes.
2. Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a ball, then flatten into a disc about 1/2 inch thick and 3-4 inches in diameter.
3. Heat a lightly oiled griddle or heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat. Cook arepas for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and a crust forms.
4. To ensure they are cooked through, you can finish them in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 10-15 minutes, or until they sound hollow when tapped.
5. Serve warm, plain or split and filled with cheese, meat, or avocado.

name: Restaurant, Latino, bunuelos (fried yeast bread)
description:
A delightful Latin American treat, buñuelos are light, airy fried yeast breads, often dusted with sugar or drizzled with syrup, a popular festive indulgence.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10 buñuelos
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 1.5 hours rising time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp granulated sugar
- 1/2 tsp active dry yeast
- 1/4 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup warm milk (105-115°F/40-46°C)
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
- Vegetable oil for frying
- Powdered sugar or cinnamon sugar for dusting

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Gradually add warm milk and melted butter, mixing until a soft dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
2. Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
3. Punch down the dough and divide into 8-10 small balls. Roll each ball into a thin disc (about 4-5 inches in diameter).
4. Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
5. Carefully fry buñuelos one or two at a time for 1-2 minutes per side, until golden brown and puffed. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
6. Dust generously with powdered sugar or cinnamon sugar while still warm. Serve immediately.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, beef and vegetables
description:
A classic Chinese stir-fry, tender slices of beef are quickly cooked with a colorful assortment of crisp-tender vegetables in a savory, aromatic sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 onion, sliced
- 1 bell pepper (any color), sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup beef broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp cornstarch

Instructions:
1. Marinate beef: Toss sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch. Set aside for 15 minutes.
2. Prepare sauce: Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
3. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add beef and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until browned. Remove beef from wok and set aside.
4. Add a little more oil if needed. Add onion, bell pepper, and broccoli to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
5. Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
6. Return beef to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the beef and vegetables.
7. Serve immediately with rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, shrimp and vegetables
description:
A light and flavorful Chinese stir-fry, succulent shrimp are quickly cooked with a medley of fresh, crisp vegetables in a delicate, savory sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 cup snap peas
- 1 cup sliced carrots
- 1/2 red bell pepper, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp cornstarch

Instructions:
1. Marinate shrimp: Toss shrimp with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch. Set aside for 10 minutes.
2. Prepare sauce: Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
3. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add shrimp and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until pink and cooked through. Remove shrimp from wok and set aside.
4. Add a little more oil if needed. Add snap peas, carrots, and red bell pepper to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
5. Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
6. Return shrimp to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the shrimp and vegetables.
7. Serve immediately with rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, sweet and sour chicken
description:
A popular Chinese-American dish, crispy fried chicken pieces are coated in a vibrant, tangy-sweet sauce, often with bell peppers and pineapple.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 1 egg, beaten
- Vegetable oil for frying
- 1/2 green bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 cup pineapple chunks (canned or fresh)
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp ketchup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1/4 cup water

Instructions:
1. Prepare sauce: Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Set aside.
2. Coat chicken: Toss chicken pieces with cornstarch, then dip in beaten egg, then toss again in cornstarch to ensure a good coating.
3. Fry chicken: Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C). Fry chicken in batches for 4-6 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
4. Assemble: In a large skillet or wok, add a tablespoon of oil. Add bell peppers and pineapple, stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
5. Pour in the prepared sweet and sour sauce. Bring to a simmer, stirring until thickened.
6. Add the fried chicken to the sauce, tossing to coat evenly. Serve immediately with rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, sweet and sour pork
description:
A classic Chinese-American dish, crispy fried pork pieces are coated in a vibrant, tangy-sweet sauce, often with bell peppers and pineapple.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb pork shoulder or loin, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 1 egg, beaten
- Vegetable oil for frying
- 1/2 green bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 red bell pepper, diced
- 1/2 cup pineapple chunks (canned or fresh)
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 2 tbsp ketchup
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp cornstarch
- 1/4 cup water

Instructions:
1. Prepare sauce: Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Set aside.
2. Coat pork: Toss pork pieces with cornstarch, then dip in beaten egg, then toss again in cornstarch to ensure a good coating.
3. Fry pork: Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C). Fry pork in batches for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
4. Assemble: In a large skillet or wok, add a tablespoon of oil. Add bell peppers and pineapple, stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
5. Pour in the prepared sweet and sour sauce. Bring to a simmer, stirring until thickened.
6. Add the fried pork to the sauce, tossing to coat evenly. Serve immediately with rice.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, chicken chow mein
description:
A popular Chinese noodle dish, chicken chow mein features stir-fried noodles with tender chicken, crisp vegetables, and a savory sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 8 oz chow mein noodles (fresh or dried, cooked per package)
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, thinly sliced
- 1 cup shredded cabbage
- 1 carrot, julienned
- 1/2 onion, thinly sliced
- 1 stalk celery, thinly sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup chicken broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp oyster sauce (optional)
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp cornstarch

Instructions:
1. Cook noodles according to package directions; drain and set aside.
2. Prepare sauce: Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
3. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until cooked through. Remove chicken and set aside.
4. Add a little more oil if needed. Add cabbage, carrot, onion, and celery to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
5. Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
6. Return chicken to the wok. Add cooked noodles. Pour in the prepared sauce. Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes until heated through and coated with sauce.
7. Serve immediately.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, vegetable chow mein, without meat or noodles
description:
A vibrant and healthy Chinese stir-fry, this vegetable chow mein features a medley of crisp-tender vegetables in a savory sauce, served without meat or noodles.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 cup shredded cabbage
- 1 carrot, julienned
- 1/2 onion, thinly sliced
- 1 stalk celery, thinly sliced
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 1/2 red bell pepper, sliced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 inch ginger, grated
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup vegetable broth
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1 tsp cornstarch

Instructions:
1. Prepare sauce: Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
2. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add cabbage, carrot, onion, celery, broccoli, and red bell pepper. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
3. Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4. Pour in the prepared sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the vegetables.
5. Serve immediately as a side or light meal.

name: Restaurant, Chinese, sesame chicken
description:
A beloved Chinese-American dish, crispy fried chicken pieces are coated in a rich, sweet, and savory sesame sauce, often garnished with sesame seeds.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 cup cornstarch
- 1 egg, beaten
- Vegetable oil for frying
- For the sauce:
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- 2 tbsp honey or sugar
- 1 tbsp sesame oil
- 1 tbsp ketchup
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water (slurry)
- Sesame seeds for garnish

Instructions:
1. Coat chicken: Toss chicken pieces with cornstarch, then dip in beaten egg, then toss again in cornstarch to ensure a good coating.
2. Fry chicken: Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C). Fry chicken in batches for 4-6 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
3. Prepare sauce: In a saucepan, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey/sugar, sesame oil, ketchup, ginger, and garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
4. Whisk in the cornstarch slurry and cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens.
5. Add the fried chicken to the sauce, tossing to coat evenly. Garnish with sesame seeds.
6. Serve immediately with rice.

name: Syrups, grenadine
description: A vibrant red, non-alcoholic syrup made from pomegranates, grenadine adds a sweet-tart flavor and beautiful color to cocktails and mocktails.

name: Imitation cheese, american or cheddar, low cholesterol
description: A dairy-free or modified cheese product designed to mimic the flavor and texture of American or cheddar cheese, formulated to be low in cholesterol.

name: Babyfood, banana juice with low fat yogurt
description: A smooth and creamy baby food blend combining the natural sweetness of banana juice with the mild tang of low-fat yogurt, perfect for developing palates.

name: Babyfood, mixed fruit juice with low fat yogurt
description: A delightful baby food blend featuring a medley of fruit juices combined with creamy low-fat yogurt, offering a variety of flavors and nutrients for infants.

name: Ham, turkey, sliced, extra lean, prepackaged or deli
description: Thinly sliced, extra lean turkey ham, a healthier alternative to traditional pork ham, offering a savory flavor perfect for sandwiches and salads.

name: Salad dressing, peppercorn dressing, commercial, regular

name: Plantains, green, fried
description:

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 green plantains
- 1/2 cup vegetable oil, for frying
- Salt to taste

Instructions:
1. Peel the green plantains and slice them into 1-inch thick rounds.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
3. Fry the plantain slices for 2-3 minutes per side, until lightly golden.
4. Remove from oil, place on a cutting board, and flatten each slice using a tostone press or the bottom of a glass.
5. Return flattened plantains to the hot oil and fry for another 1-2 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
6. Remove, drain on paper towels, and season immediately with salt.

4. Remove from oil and drain on paper towels. Serve warm.

name: Pork, fresh, leg (ham), whole, separable lean and fat, cooked, roasted
description:
A succulent, tender roasted pork leg, offering a hearty and flavorful centerpiece for any meal, with a perfect balance of lean meat and savory fat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-15
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 whole pork leg (ham), bone-in, skin on (approx. 10-15 lbs)
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 tbsp fresh rosemary, chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tbsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
2. Score the skin of the pork leg in a diamond pattern.
3. In a small bowl, mix olive oil, rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt, and pepper.
4. Rub the mixture all over the pork leg, ensuring it gets into the scores.
5. Place the pork leg on a rack in a roasting pan.
6. Roast for 20-25 minutes per pound, or until an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C) is reached in the thickest part (avoiding the bone).
7. Let rest for 15-20 minutes before carving.

name: Desserts, mousse, chocolate, prepared-from-recipe
description:
An airy and decadent chocolate mousse, handcrafted from scratch, offering a rich, melt-in-your-mouth experience with intense cocoa flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 4 oz bittersweet chocolate, chopped
- 2 large eggs, separated
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar
- 1 cup heavy cream
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- Pinch of salt

Instructions:
1. Melt chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (double boiler) or in the microwave, stirring until smooth. Let cool slightly.
2. In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks with half of the sugar until pale and creamy.
3. Gradually whisk the melted chocolate into the egg yolk mixture.
4. In a clean bowl, beat egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining sugar and beat until stiff, glossy peaks form.
5. In another bowl, whip heavy cream with vanilla extract until medium-stiff peaks form.
6. Gently fold one-third of the whipped cream into the chocolate mixture to lighten it.
7. Then, gently fold in the remaining whipped cream.
8. Finally, carefully fold in the beaten egg whites until just combined, being careful not to deflate the mixture.
9. Spoon the mousse into individual serving glasses or a large bowl.
10. Chill for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, before serving.

name: Candies, praline, prepared-from-recipe
description:
A traditional Southern confection, these pralines are rich, buttery, and sweet, packed with pecans and boasting a slightly grainy, melt-in-your-mouth texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: About 2 dozen pralines
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- 1 cup packed light brown sugar
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 1/2 cup milk
- 4 tablespoons unsalted butter
- 1 1/2 cups pecan halves
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions:
1. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or wax paper.
2. In a large heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine granulated sugar, brown sugar, heavy cream, milk, and butter. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sugars dissolve and butter melts.
3. Bring the mixture to a boil without stirring. Continue to boil until a candy thermometer reads 235-240°F (soft-ball stage).
4. Remove from heat and immediately stir in the pecan halves and vanilla extract.
5. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture begins to thicken and lose its gloss (this can take 3-5 minutes). It will start to look grainy.
6. Quickly drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet. Work quickly as the pralines will set fast.
7. Let cool completely until firm before serving.

name: Candies, fudge, chocolate marshmallow, with nuts, prepared-by-recipe
description:
A decadent, homemade chocolate fudge, enriched with fluffy marshmallow and crunchy nuts, offering a rich, chewy, and irresistible treat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: About 36 squares
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 3 cups granulated sugar
- 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter
- 1 (5 oz) can evaporated milk
- 1 (12 oz) package semi-sweet chocolate chips
- 1 (7 oz) jar marshmallow creme
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 cup chopped nuts (e.g., walnuts or pecans)

Instructions:
1. Line a 9x13 inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal. Lightly grease the paper.
2. In a large heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar, butter, and evaporated milk. Bring to a full rolling boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
3. Boil for 5 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
4. Remove from heat. Immediately stir in chocolate chips until melted and smooth.
5. Add marshmallow creme and vanilla extract, stirring until fully incorporated.
6. Stir in chopped nuts.
7. Pour the fudge mixture into the prepared pan and spread evenly.
8. Let cool completely at room temperature for several hours, or chill in the refrigerator until firm.
9. Once firm, use the parchment paper overhang to lift the fudge from the pan and cut into squares.

Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:

Instructions:

name: Candies, divinity, prepared-from-recipe
description:
A classic Southern confection, divinity is a light, airy, and sweet nougat-like candy, typically made with egg whites, sugar, corn syrup, and often nuts.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: About 2 dozen pieces
Prep Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 1/2 cups granulated sugar
- 1/2 cup light corn syrup
- 1/2 cup water
- 2 large egg whites, at room temperature
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 cup chopped pecans (optional)

Instructions:
1. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or wax paper.
2. In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, and water. Cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Bring to a boil without stirring, then insert a candy thermometer.
3. Continue to boil without stirring until the syrup reaches 260°F (hard-ball stage).
4. While the syrup is cooking, in a large, clean bowl, beat egg whites with salt using an electric mixer on high speed until stiff peaks form.
5. Once the syrup reaches 260°F, slowly and carefully pour a thin stream of the hot syrup into the beaten egg whites, continuing to beat on high speed. Do not pour directly onto the beaters.
6. Continue beating on high speed for 5-7 minutes, or until the mixture is very thick, glossy, and holds its shape.
7. Stir in vanilla extract and chopped pecans (if using).
8. Working quickly, drop spoonfuls of the divinity onto the prepared baking sheet.
9. Let cool completely until firm before serving.

name: Pasta, homemade, made with egg, cooked
description:
Freshly made pasta crafted with eggs, resulting in a rich, tender, and flavorful noodle that elevates any sauce or dish with its superior texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 45 minutes (plus 30 minutes rest)

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 large eggs
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon olive oil (optional)

Instructions:
1. On a clean surface, make a well with the flour. Crack eggs into the center, add salt and olive oil.
2. Gently whisk eggs with a fork, gradually incorporating flour from the sides until a shaggy dough forms.
3. Knead the dough for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in plastic and let rest for 30 minutes.
4. Divide dough into portions. Roll each portion very thinly with a pasta machine or rolling pin.
5. Cut into desired pasta shapes (e.g., fettuccine, spaghetti).
6. Cook in a large pot of salted boiling water for 2-4 minutes, or until al dente. Drain and serve immediately.

description: A traditional Alaska Native food, raw beluga whale flipper is a rich source of nutrients, consumed for its distinct flavor and cultural significance.

name: Whale, beluga, liver, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Raw beluga whale liver, a highly prized and nutrient-dense traditional food among Alaska Natives, valued for its unique taste and cultural importance.

description: Naturally growing wild blackberries, harvested by Alaska Natives, offering a burst of sweet-tart flavor and essential vitamins when eaten fresh.

name: Caribou, liver, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Raw caribou liver, a nutrient-rich and traditional food source for Alaska Natives, valued for its distinct flavor and high vitamin content.

name: Stew/soup, caribou (Alaska Native)
description:
A hearty and nourishing traditional Alaska Native stew or soup, featuring tender caribou meat simmered with vegetables and broth, providing warmth and sustenance.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb caribou meat, cubed
- 4 cups water or broth
- 1 onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 potatoes, cubed
- 1/2 cup wild rice (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Brown caribou meat in a large pot or Dutch oven.
2. Add onion and cook until softened. Add water or broth and bring to a simmer.
3. Stir in carrots, potatoes, and wild rice (if using). Season with salt and pepper.
4. Cover and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until caribou is tender and vegetables are cooked through.
5. Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

name: Caribou, tongue, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Raw caribou tongue, a traditional and flavorful cut of meat for Alaska Natives, often prepared by boiling or roasting for a tender texture.

name: Chiton, leathery, gumboots (Alaska Native)
description: A large marine mollusk, the gumboot chiton is a traditional Alaska Native food, often harvested from rocky shores and consumed for its unique texture and briny taste.

name: Fish, devilfish, meat (Alaska Native)
description: The meat of the devilfish (likely octopus or a type of sculpin), a traditional food source for Alaska Natives, known for its firm texture and mild flavor.

name: Fireweed, young leaves, raw (Alaska Native)
description: Tender young leaves of the fireweed plant, a wild edible traditionally gathered by Alaska Natives, offering a slightly bitter, fresh flavor, often eaten raw in salads.

name: Fish, herring eggs on giant kelp, Pacific (Alaska Native)
description: A delicacy for Alaska Natives, Pacific herring eggs naturally deposited on giant kelp, offering a unique briny flavor and crunchy texture, often eaten raw.

name: Fish, herring eggs, Pacific, dry (Alaska Native)
description: Dried Pacific herring eggs, a traditional and nutrient-rich food for Alaska Natives, providing a concentrated source of flavor and sustenance.

name: Stew, moose (Alaska Native)
description:
A hearty and warming traditional Alaska Native stew, featuring tender moose meat slow-cooked with root vegetables and broth, a staple for sustenance in the Arctic.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs moose meat, cubed
- 1 tablespoon oil or lard
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 3 carrots, chopped
- 3 potatoes, cubed
- 4 cups water or broth
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper

Instructions:
1. Heat oil or lard in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown moose meat on all sides.
2. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
3. Stir in carrots, potatoes, water or broth, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
4. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until moose meat is very tender.
5. Adjust seasoning if needed and serve hot.

name: Agave, cooked (Southwest)

description: A rich and robust organ meat, highly valued in Alaska Native diets for its nutritional content and distinct flavor.

name: Sea lion, Steller, meat (Alaska Native)
description: Lean and flavorful meat, a traditional food source for Alaska Native peoples, providing essential sustenance from marine resources.

name: Piki bread, made from blue cornmeal (Hopi)
description:
A delicate, paper-thin bread made from blue cornmeal, traditionally prepared by the Hopi people, known for its unique texture and cultural significance.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: Varies
Prep Time: 30 minutes (plus cooking time)

Ingredients:
- Blue cornmeal
- Juniper ash (or baking soda)
- Water

Instructions:
1. Mix blue cornmeal with water and a small amount of juniper ash (or baking soda) to form a thin batter.
2. Heat a piki stone (or flat griddle) to a very high temperature.
3. Using hands, quickly spread a thin layer of batter onto the hot stone, allowing it to cook almost instantly into a delicate, crispy sheet.
4. Peel off and stack.

name: Wocas, tuber, cooked, Oregon, yellow pond lily (Klamath)
description: The starchy, edible tuber of the yellow pond lily, traditionally harvested and cooked by the Klamath people of Oregon, offering a unique indigenous food source.

name: Stew, pinto bean and hominy, badufsuki (Hopi)
description:
A hearty and comforting stew, traditionally prepared by the Hopi, featuring tender pinto beans and chewy hominy in a savory broth.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus soaking time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried pinto beans
- 1 cup dried hominy
- 1 onion (chopped)
- 2 cloves garlic (minced)
- 1-2 green chiles (roasted, peeled, chopped)
- 4 cups vegetable broth
- 1 tsp cumin
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Soak pinto beans and hominy overnight. Drain.
2. In a large pot, combine soaked beans, hominy, onion, garlic, green chiles, and broth.
3. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until beans and hominy are tender.
4. Add cumin, salt, and pepper. Serve hot.

name: Tamales, masa and pork filling (Hopi)
description:
Savory steamed parcels of masa dough filled with seasoned pork, a traditional and beloved dish among the Hopi people, offering rich flavors and a satisfying texture.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12 tamales
Prep Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups masa harina
- 1.5 cups warm chicken broth
- 1/2 cup lard or vegetable shortening
- 1 tsp baking powder
- Salt to taste
- 1 lb cooked shredded pork (seasoned with chili powder, cumin, garlic)
- 20-25 dried corn husks (soaked)

Instructions:
1. Beat lard/shortening until fluffy.
2. In a separate bowl, combine masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
3. Gradually add warm broth to masa mixture, then beat in the fluffy lard until a soft, spreadable dough forms.
4. Spread a thin layer of masa onto a soaked corn husk.
5. Place a spoonful of seasoned pork in the center.
6. Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold up the bottom.
7. Steam tamales upright in a steamer basket for 1-1.5 hours, or until masa is firm and pulls away easily from the husk.

name: Restaurant, family style, fried mozzarella sticks
description:
Crispy, golden-fried sticks of melted mozzarella cheese, often served with a tangy marinara sauce, a popular appetizer for sharing.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 30 minutes freezing)

Ingredients:
- 12 mozzarella string cheese sticks
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 large eggs (beaten)
- 1 cup breadcrumbs (panko recommended)
- 1 tsp Italian seasoning
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Vegetable oil for frying
- Marinara sauce for dipping

Instructions:
1. Place flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs (mixed with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper) in three separate shallow dishes.
2. Dredge each mozzarella stick first in flour, then in egg, then in breadcrumbs, ensuring full coating. For extra crispiness, repeat the egg and breadcrumb coating.
3. Freeze coated sticks for at least 30 minutes.
4. Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
5. Fry mozzarella sticks in batches for 2-3 minutes, or until golden brown and melted. Drain on paper towels. Serve immediately with marinara sauce.

name: Restaurant, family style, sirloin steak
description:
A flavorful and tender cut of beef, typically grilled or pan-seared to perfection, offering a classic steakhouse experience.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (1.5 lb) sirloin steak (about 1-inch thick)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp butter (optional)

Instructions:
1. Pat steak dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
2. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron works best) over high heat until smoking.
3. Carefully place steak in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness.
4. For extra flavor, add butter during the last minute of cooking and baste the steak.
5. Remove steak from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes before slicing against the grain.

name: Restaurant, family style, coleslaw
description:
A refreshing side dish made from shredded cabbage and carrots, tossed in a creamy, tangy dressing, perfect for complementing rich meals.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 head green cabbage (shredded)
- 1-2 carrots (shredded)
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp celery seed
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage and carrots.
2. In a separate small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, celery seed, salt, and pepper until smooth.
3. Pour dressing over the cabbage mixture and toss well to coat.
4. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.

name: Restaurant, family style, onion rings
description:
Crispy, golden-fried rings of sweet onion, coated in a seasoned batter, a beloved classic appetizer or side dish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 large yellow onions (sliced into 1/2-inch rings)
- 1.5 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1 cup milk
- 1 large egg
- Vegetable oil for frying

Instructions:
1. Separate onion slices into individual rings.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk milk and egg. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing until just combined (a few lumps are okay).
4. Heat 2-3 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
5. Dip onion rings one by one into the batter, letting excess drip off.
6. Carefully place battered rings into the hot oil, frying in batches for 2-4 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
7. Drain on paper towels and season with extra salt if desired.

name: Restaurant, family style, chili with meat and beans
description:
A hearty and robust stew, slow-cooked with ground meat, beans, tomatoes, and a blend of savory spices, offering a comforting and flavorful meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 lb ground beef
- 1 large onion (chopped)
- 2 cloves garlic (minced)
- 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 1 (15 oz) can kidney beans (drained and rinsed)
- 1 (15 oz) can pinto beans (drained and rinsed)
- 1 cup beef broth
- 2 tbsp chili powder
- 1 tsp cumin
- 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Optional toppings: shredded cheese, sour cream, chopped green onions

Instructions:
1. In a large pot or Dutch oven, brown ground beef over medium-high heat, breaking it apart. Drain excess fat.
2. Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
3. Add crushed tomatoes, kidney beans, pinto beans, beef broth, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika.
4. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for at least 30 minutes (or longer for richer flavor), stirring occasionally.
5. Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with desired toppings.

name: Restaurant, family style, spaghetti and meatballs
description:
A classic Italian-American comfort dish featuring tender spaghetti pasta tossed in a rich marinara sauce, topped with savory, homemade meatballs.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- For Meatballs: 1 lb ground beef
- 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese
- 1 large egg
- 2 tbsp milk
- 1 clove garlic (minced)
- 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning
- Salt and pepper to taste
- For Sauce & Pasta: 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp dried basil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1 lb spaghetti

Instructions:
1. For meatballs: In a bowl, gently mix ground beef, breadcrumbs, Parmesan, egg, milk, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Form into 1.5-inch meatballs.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Brown meatballs on all sides, then remove and set aside.
3. Add crushed tomatoes, water, sugar, and basil to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then return meatballs to the sauce. Cover and simmer for at least 20-30 minutes, or until meatballs are cooked through and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
4. Cook spaghetti according to package directions. Serve meatballs and sauce over hot spaghetti.

name: Restaurant, Mexican, cheese quesadilla
description:
A simple yet satisfying Mexican dish, featuring a flour tortilla filled with melted cheese, folded and grilled until golden and crispy.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1-2
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 large flour tortillas
- 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese
- 1 tbsp butter or oil
- Salsa, sour cream, or guacamole for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat. Melt butter or add oil.
2. Place one tortilla in the skillet. Sprinkle half of the cheese evenly over the tortilla. Place the second tortilla on top.
3. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until tortillas are golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly.
4. Alternatively, place one tortilla in the skillet, sprinkle with all the cheese on one half, then fold the other half over. Cook until golden and cheese is melted.
5. Remove from skillet, slice into wedges, and serve immediately with desired toppings.

name: Restaurant, Italian, cheese ravioli with marinara sauce
description:
Tender pasta pockets filled with a rich blend of cheeses, served with a classic, vibrant marinara sauce, a comforting Italian favorite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3-4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 (20 oz) package fresh or frozen cheese ravioli
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 clove garlic (minced)
- 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes
- 1/2 tsp dried basil
- 1/4 tsp dried oregano
- Pinch of sugar
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Grated Parmesan cheese for serving

Instructions:
1. Cook ravioli according to package directions until al dente.
2. While ravioli cooks, prepare the marinara sauce: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3. Stir in crushed tomatoes, basil, oregano, and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat and let it gently bubble for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
4. Season with salt and pepper. Drain cooked ravioli and toss gently with the marinara sauce. Serve hot, garnished with grated Parmesan cheese.

name: Salad dressing, caesar dressing, regular
description:
A classic, creamy salad dressing characterized by its savory blend of Parmesan cheese, garlic, anchovies, and lemon juice.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 large egg yolk
- 1 clove garlic (minced)
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil
- 2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a medium bowl, whisk together egg yolk, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and Worcestershire sauce.
2. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil and vegetable oil while continuously whisking until the dressing emulsifies and thickens.
3. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

name: Salad dressing, coleslaw
description:
A creamy, tangy, and slightly sweet dressing specifically designed to coat shredded cabbage and carrots for classic coleslaw.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1 cup (enough for 1 head of cabbage)
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp celery seed
- 1/4 tsp onion powder
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, sugar, celery seed, onion powder, salt, and pepper until smooth and well combined.
2. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.

name: Salad dressing, green goddess, regular
description:
A rich and herbaceous creamy dressing, typically featuring a blend of mayonnaise, sour cream, fresh herbs, and anchovy, offering a distinctive savory flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup sour cream
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped)
- 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped)
- 1 tbsp fresh tarragon (chopped)
- 1 clove garlic (minced)
- 1 anchovy fillet (minced, optional)
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a food processor or blender, combine mayonnaise, sour cream, parsley, chives, tarragon, minced garlic, minced anchovy (if using), and lemon juice.
2. Process until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
3. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.

description: A convenient and energy-boosting bar packed with wholesome oats, sweet raisins, and tropical coconut, often enjoyed as a quick breakfast or snack.

name: Pretzels, soft
description:
Warm, chewy, and often salted, these iconic baked goods are characterized by their distinctive twisted shape and soft interior.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 8-10
Prep Time: 30 minutes (plus 1 hour rise time)

Ingredients:
- 1.5 cups warm water (105-115°F)
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 2 tsp active dry yeast
- 4.5 cups all-purpose flour
- 1.5 tsp salt
- 4 cups water (for boiling)
- 1/2 cup baking soda
- 1 large egg (beaten, for egg wash)
- Coarse salt for sprinkling

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine warm water, sugar, and yeast. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
2. Add flour and salt, mix until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
3. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled.
4. Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C). Bring 4 cups of water and baking soda to a rolling boil in a large pot.
5. Divide dough into 8-10 pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope (about 24 inches), then form into a pretzel shape.
6. Carefully drop one or two pretzels into the boiling water for 30 seconds. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
7. Brush with egg wash and sprinkle with coarse salt. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.

name: Beans, chili, barbecue, ranch style, cooked
description: Savory and smoky beans, slow-cooked in a rich barbecue-style chili sauce, offering a robust and flavorful side dish or meal component.

name: Luncheon slices, meatless
description: Plant-based slices designed to mimic traditional deli meats, offering a savory and convenient option for sandwiches and snacks.

name: Meatballs, meatless
description:
Savory, plant-based spheres crafted to resemble traditional meatballs, perfect for vegetarian and vegan dishes.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup cooked brown lentils (mashed)
- 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup finely chopped onion
- 2 cloves garlic (minced)
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tsp Italian seasoning
- 1/4 cup nutritional yeast (optional, for cheesy flavor)
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine mashed lentils, breadcrumbs, chopped onion, minced garlic, soy sauce, Italian seasoning, nutritional yeast (if using), salt, and pepper. Mix well until a cohesive mixture forms. If too dry, add a tiny bit of water; if too wet, add more breadcrumbs.
2. Form the mixture into 1-inch balls.
3. Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Cook meatballs in batches, turning occasionally, until golden brown and heated through, about 8-10 minutes. Serve with your favorite sauce.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried sulfured peaches
- 2 cups water
- 1/4 cup sugar (or to taste)

Instructions:
1. Rinse dried peaches.
2. In a saucepan, combine peaches, water, and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
3. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-30 minutes, or until peaches are tender and plump and the liquid has thickened slightly. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Potato salad, home-prepared
description:
A beloved classic, home-prepared potato salad is a creamy, tangy, and satisfying side dish, perfect for picnics, barbecues, or any gathering.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 lbs russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 1/4 cup yellow mustard
- 2 celery stalks, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup red onion, finely chopped
- 2 hard-boiled eggs, chopped (optional)
- 2 tbsp fresh dill or parsley, chopped (optional)
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Pinch of paprika for garnish

Instructions:
1. Place diced potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt.
2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes. Do not overcook.
3. Drain the potatoes thoroughly and let them cool slightly in a colander for about 5-10 minutes to allow excess steam to escape.
4. In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, mustard, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
5. Add the slightly cooled potatoes, chopped celery, red onion, and chopped hard-boiled eggs (if using) to the bowl.
6. Gently fold all ingredients together until the potatoes are evenly coated. Be careful not to mash the potatoes too much.
7. Stir in fresh dill or parsley (if using).
8. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. For best flavor, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
9. Garnish with a sprinkle of paprika before serving.

name: Beef, ground, 70% lean meat / 30% fat, loaf, cooked, baked
description:
A comforting classic, this baked beef meatloaf is made with a savory blend of ground beef, offering a moist and flavorful centerpiece for any family meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1.5 lbs ground beef (70% lean / 30% fat)
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup milk
- 1/4 cup finely chopped onion
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 cup ketchup (for topping)
- 1 tbsp brown sugar (for topping)
- 1 tsp mustard (for topping)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. In a large bowl, combine ground beef, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, chopped onion, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined; do not overmix.
3. Shape the mixture into a loaf and place it in a lightly greased 9x5 inch loaf pan, or on a baking sheet.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together ketchup, brown sugar, and mustard for the topping.
5. Spread the topping evenly over the meatloaf.
6. Bake for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, or until an internal temperature of 160°F (71°C) is reached.
7. Let the meatloaf rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Alcoholic beverage, daiquiri, prepared-from-recipe
description:

--- RECIPE ---

Prep Time: 5 minutes

Ingredients:

5. Garnish with a lime wheel or wedge, if desired.

name: Candies, truffles, prepared-from-recipe
description:
Decadent homemade chocolate truffles, rich and creamy ganache centers coated in cocoa powder or chocolate, offering a luxurious melt-in-your-mouth experience.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12-15 truffles
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 2 hours chilling)

Ingredients:
- 8 oz good quality dark chocolate (60-70% cocoa), finely chopped
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder (for coating)

Instructions:
1. Place chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
2. Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan over medium heat until it just begins to simmer (do not boil).
3. Pour hot cream over the chocolate and let sit for 5 minutes. Add butter.
4. Stir gently with a whisk until the chocolate and butter are completely melted and smooth.
5. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until firm enough to roll.
6. Scoop small portions (about 1 teaspoon) of the chilled ganache and quickly roll into balls between your palms.
7. Roll each truffle in cocoa powder to coat evenly.
8. Store truffles in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

name: Candies, peanut brittle, prepared-from-recipe
description:
Crisp, buttery homemade peanut brittle, studded with crunchy roasted peanuts, offering a delightful snap and sweet, nutty flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 10-12
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus cooling time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 1/2 cup light corn syrup
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 cup roasted peanuts
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 1 tsp baking soda

Instructions:
1. Lightly grease a large baking sheet and set aside.
2. In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, and water. Cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
3. Bring to a boil without stirring, then add peanuts. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the mixture reaches 300°F (149°C) on a candy thermometer (hard crack stage).
4. Remove from heat and quickly stir in butter and baking soda. The mixture will foam up.
5. Immediately pour the brittle onto the prepared baking sheet and spread thinly with a heatproof spatula or the back of a greased spoon.
6. Let cool completely (about 30-60 minutes) until hard and brittle.
7. Once cooled, break the brittle into pieces.

name: Desserts, egg custard, baked, prepared-from-recipe
description:
A classic baked egg custard, featuring a silky-smooth texture and delicate vanilla flavor, often topped with a hint of nutmeg for a comforting finish.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 3 large eggs
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- 2 cups whole milk
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- Pinch of salt
- Ground nutmeg, for sprinkling

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). Place four 6-ounce ramekins in a baking dish.
2. In a large bowl, whisk eggs, sugar, vanilla, and salt until well combined.
3. Gently whisk in the milk until just combined (do not overmix to avoid excess foam).
4. Pour the custard mixture evenly into the ramekins.
5. Sprinkle a little nutmeg on top of each custard.
6. Carefully pour hot water into the baking dish around the ramekins, reaching about halfway up their sides (this creates a water bath).
7. Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the custards are just set but still slightly jiggly in the center.
8. Carefully remove ramekins from the water bath and let cool on a wire rack.
9. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Desserts, apple crisp, prepared-from-recipe
description:

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 6-8
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 6 medium apples (such as Granny Smith or Honeycrisp), peeled, cored, and sliced
- 1/2 cup granulated sugar (for apples)
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon (for apples)
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour (for topping)
- 1/2 cup packed light brown sugar (for topping)
- 1/2 cup rolled oats (for topping)
- 1/2 cup (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces (for topping)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. In a large bowl, combine sliced apples, granulated sugar, and cinnamon. Toss to coat. Pour into an 8x8 inch baking dish.
3. In a separate bowl, combine flour, brown sugar, and rolled oats. Cut in the cold butter with a pastry blender or your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
4. Sprinkle the oat topping evenly over the apples.
5. Bake for 45-50 minutes, or until the apples are tender and the topping is golden brown and bubbly.
6. Serve warm, optionally with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

name: Candies, fudge, chocolate marshmallow, prepared-from-recipe
description:
Rich, creamy, and irresistibly sweet, this homemade chocolate marshmallow fudge is a classic treat, melting in your mouth with every bite.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 24 pieces
Prep Time: 10 minutes (plus 2 hours chilling)

Ingredients:
- 3 cups (18 oz) semi-sweet chocolate chips
- 1 (14 oz) can sweetened condensed milk
- 1/4 cup butter
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 2 cups miniature marshmallows

Instructions:
1. Line an 8x8 inch pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides.
2. In a large microwave-safe bowl, combine chocolate chips, sweetened condensed milk, and butter.
3. Microwave on high for 1 minute, then stir. Continue microwaving in 30-second intervals, stirring after each, until mixture is smooth and melted (about 2-3 minutes total).
4. Stir in vanilla extract and miniature marshmallows until just combined.
5. Pour the fudge into the prepared pan and spread evenly.
6. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until firm.
7. Use the parchment paper overhang to lift the fudge from the pan, then cut into squares.

name: Candies, taffy, prepared-from-recipe
description:
Chewy, sweet, and fun to pull, homemade taffy is a delightful confection that can be flavored and colored to your heart's content.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 12-16 pieces
Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus cooling and pulling time)

Ingredients:
- 2 cups granulated sugar
- 1 cup light corn syrup
- 1/2 cup water
- 1 tablespoon butter
- 1 teaspoon flavoring (e.g., vanilla, peppermint, lemon)
- Food coloring (optional)

Instructions:
1. Grease a large baking sheet or marble slab with butter.
2. In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar, corn syrup, and water. Cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
3. Insert a candy thermometer and continue to cook without stirring until the mixture reaches 260°F (127°C).
4. Remove from heat and stir in butter, flavoring, and food coloring (if using).
5. Pour the hot mixture onto the greased surface. Let it cool for a few minutes until it's cool enough to handle but still pliable.
6. Grease your hands lightly with butter. Gather the taffy and begin to pull it, stretching and folding it repeatedly until it becomes opaque and firm (about 10-15 minutes).
7. Once pulled, stretch it into a long rope and cut into bite-sized pieces. Wrap each piece in wax paper.

name: Candies, toffee, prepared-from-recipe
description:
Crisp, buttery, and utterly addictive, homemade toffee is a classic candy, often coated in chocolate and nuts for an extra layer of indulgence.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 16-20 pieces
Prep Time: 15 minutes (plus cooling time)

Ingredients:
- 1 cup unsalted butter
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 cup chocolate chips (optional)
- 1/2 cup chopped nuts (optional)

Instructions:
1. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
2. In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine butter, sugar, and water. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves.
3. Insert a candy thermometer and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the mixture reaches 300-310°F (149-154°C), or hard crack stage. The mixture will turn a rich amber color.
4. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract.
5. Immediately pour the hot toffee onto the prepared baking sheet and spread thinly with an offset spatula.
6. If using, sprinkle chocolate chips over the hot toffee. Let them sit for a few minutes to melt, then spread evenly. Sprinkle with chopped nuts.
7. Let cool completely at room temperature or in the refrigerator until hard.
8. Once firm, break the toffee into pieces.

name: Macaroni and cheese, box mix with cheese sauce, prepared
description:
A beloved comfort food, this classic macaroni and cheese features tender pasta coated in a creamy, savory cheese sauce, prepared from a convenient box mix.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 3
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 box (7.25 oz) macaroni and cheese mix
- 6 cups water
- 1/4 cup milk
- 2 tbsp butter or margarine

Instructions:
1. Boil 6 cups of water in a medium saucepan. Add macaroni and cook for 7-8 minutes, or until tender, stirring occasionally.
2. Drain water from saucepan. Return macaroni to saucepan.
3. Add 1/4 cup milk, 2 tbsp butter or margarine, and cheese sauce mix. Stir until butter is melted and sauce is well blended. Serve hot.

name: Taquitos, frozen, chicken and cheese, oven-heated
description:
Crispy, rolled tortillas filled with savory chicken and melted cheese, conveniently frozen and ready to be oven-heated for a quick and satisfying snack or meal.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 6 frozen chicken and cheese taquitos
- Cooking spray (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Arrange frozen taquitos in a single layer on a baking sheet. You may lightly spray them with cooking spray for extra crispiness.
3. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until crispy and heated through. Let stand for 1 minute before serving. Serve with your favorite dipping sauce.

name: Taquitos, frozen, beef and cheese, oven-heated
description:
Deliciously seasoned beef and melted cheese rolled in a crispy tortilla, these frozen taquitos are perfect for a quick oven-heated snack or appetizer.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 2-3
Prep Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients:
- 6 frozen beef and cheese taquitos
- Cooking spray (optional)

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Arrange frozen taquitos in a single layer on a baking sheet. You may lightly spray them with cooking spray for extra crispiness.
3. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until crispy and heated through. Let stand for 1 minute before serving. Serve with your favorite dipping sauce.

name: Spanish rice mix, dry mix, prepared (with canola/vegetable oil blend or diced tomatoes and margarine)
description:
A flavorful and aromatic rice dish, prepared from a dry mix, featuring a vibrant blend of spices and often enhanced with a canola/vegetable oil blend or diced tomatoes and margarine, delivering a taste of Spanish cuisine.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 box (6 oz) Spanish rice mix
- 2 cups water
- 1 tbsp vegetable oil or margarine
- 1/2 cup diced tomatoes (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a medium saucepan, combine rice mix, water, and oil/margarine. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
2. If desired, stir in diced tomatoes during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Fluff with a fork before serving.

name: Rice mix, cheese flavor, dry mix, unprepared
description: A convenient dry mix for a cheesy rice dish, offering a quick and easy way to prepare a flavorful side or base for your meal.

name: Dumpling, potato- or cheese-filled, frozen
description: Tender dough filled with savory potato or rich cheese, these frozen dumplings are a versatile and comforting addition to any meal, ready for cooking.

name: Turnover, chicken- or turkey-, and vegetable-filled, reduced fat, frozen
description: A wholesome and reduced-fat turnover, featuring a savory filling of chicken or turkey and mixed vegetables, encased in a flaky pastry, frozen for convenience.

name: Sausage, egg and cheese breakfast biscuit
description:
A hearty breakfast classic featuring a fluffy biscuit, savory sausage, a fried egg, and melted cheese, perfect for a quick and satisfying start to your day.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 1
Prep Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 large biscuit, split
- 1 breakfast sausage patty, cooked
- 1 large egg, fried or scrambled
- 1 slice American cheese

Instructions:
1. Cook the sausage patty according to package directions. Fry or scramble the egg to your preference.
2. Split the biscuit in half. Place the cooked sausage patty on the bottom half of the biscuit, top with the cheese slice, then the cooked egg. Place the top half of the biscuit on top. Serve warm.

name: Tennis Bread, plain (Apache)
description:
A traditional Apache bread, plain Tennis Bread is a simple yet satisfying staple, often enjoyed for its soft texture and subtle flavor.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4-6
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tbsp shortening or lard
- 3/4 cup warm water (approx.)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt. Cut in shortening or lard until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
2. Gradually add warm water, mixing until a soft dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
3. Divide dough into small balls and flatten into discs. Cook on a lightly greased griddle or in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.

name: Caribou, hind quarter, meat, cooked (Alaska Native)
description: Lean and flavorful, cooked caribou hind quarter meat is a traditional and vital protein source for Alaska Natives, offering a robust taste.

name: Agutuk, fish with shortening (Alaskan ice cream) (Alaska Native)
description:
A traditional Alaska Native delicacy, Agutuk, or "Alaskan ice cream," is a unique blend of whipped fat (often shortening), berries, and sometimes fish, creating a rich and creamy treat.

--- RECIPE ---
Servings: 4
Prep Time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:
- 1 cup solid shortening (or seal oil/tallow)
- 1/2 cup cooked, flaked white fish (e.g., cod, halibut)
- 1/2 cup wild berries (e.g., blueberries, cranberries)
- Sugar to taste (optional)

Instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whip the solid shortening until light and fluffy. Gradually add the cooked, flaked fish, continuing to whip until well combined.
2. Gently fold in the wild berries. If desired, add sugar to taste. Serve immediately or chill briefly. Traditionally, this is made with rendered animal fat.

description: Steller sea lion meat with fat is a traditional and important food source for Alaska Natives, providing essential nutrients and energy.
